source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2119).

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: For clarity, OPTIONAL attributes (specification-defined and extensions) are OPTIONAL for clients to use, but the servers' responsibility will vary. Server-unknown extension attributes MUST be silently stored in the backing datastore. Specification-defined attributes and server-known extension attributes MUST generate an error if the corresponding feature is not supported or enabled. However, as with all attributes, if accepting the attribute results in a bad state (such as exceeding a size limit or resulting in a security issue), then the server MAY choose to reject the request.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: In the pseudo JSON format snippets `?` means the preceding item is OPTIONAL, `*` means the preceding item MAY appear zero or more times, and `+` means the preceding item MUST appear at least once. The presence of the `#` character means the remaining portion of the line is a comment. Whitespace characters in the JSON snippets are used for readability and are not normative.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: - `<TYPE>` - one of the allowable data type names (MUST be in lower case) listed in [Attributes and Extensions](#attributes-and-extensions)

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Terminology / Group

requirements.text: Groups, as the name implies, allow related Resources to be arranged together under a single collection - the Group. The reason for the grouping is not defined by this specification, so the owners of the Registry MAY choose to define (or enforce) any pattern they wish. In this sense, a Group is similar to a "directory" on a filesystem.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Terminology / Resource

requirements.text: Resources, typically, represent the main data of interest for the Registry. In the filesystem analogy, these would be the "files". Each Resource MUST exist under a single Group and, similar to Groups, have a set of Registry metadata. However, unlike a Group, which only has Registry metadata, each Resource MAY also have a secondary domain-specific "document" associated with it. For example, a "schema" Resource might have a "schema document" as its "document". This specification places no restriction on the type of content stored in the Resource's document. Additionally, Resources (unlike Groups) MAY be versioned.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Terminology / Version

requirements.text: A Version is an instance of a Resource that represents a particular state of the Resource. Each Version of a Resource has its own set of xRegistry metadata and possibly a domain-specific document associated with it. Each Resource MUST have at least one Version associated with it.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Terminology / Version

requirements.text: Clients MAY interact with specific Versions or with the Resource itself, which is equivalent to interacting with the Resource's "default" Version. While in many cases the "default" Version will be the "newest" Version, this specification allows for the "default" Version to be explicitly chosen and unaffected as other Versions are added or removed.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Design / Design: Registry Entity

requirements.text: - The domain-specific ["model"](./model.md#registry-model) that defines the types of entities being managed by the Registry. For example, the model might define a Group called `schemagroups` that has `schemas` as the Resources within those Groups. All xRegistry protocol specifications (e.g. `http`(./http.md) MUST define at least one REQUIRED mechanism by which the model can be retrieved.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Design / Design: Resource and Version Entities / Document Resources vs Metadata-Only Resources

requirements.text: Each Resource MAY be defined to have a "domain-specific" document associated with it. These documents MAY be stored within the Registry as an attribute on its Versions, or MAY be stored external to the Registry and a URL to its location will be stored within the Version instead. This model design choice is specified via the [`hasdocument` aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument) of the Resource type's model definition.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Design / Design: Registry Views / Single Document View

requirements.text: In this view, clients retrieving all (or part) of the Registry hierarchy as a single document. In this case, nested (or child) entities MAY be "inlined" into the retrieved document such that the need for secondary interactions with the server is reduced.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Design / Design: No-Code Servers

requirements.text: To support these simple (no-code) scenarios, this specification (and the protocol binding specifications) are written such that the support for the various operations and features (e.g. [request flags](#request-flags)) will typically be marked as OPTIONAL (often with a "SHOULD" RFC2119 key word). However, it is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED that full servers support as many of the operations and features/flags when possible to enable a better user experience, and increase interoperability.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Design / Design: Protocol Bindings

requirements.text: In general, almost all interactions with a server are OPTIONAL and dictated by the specific needs of the environment in which it is being used. However, it is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED that servers support the "read" operations, and in particular the ability to retrieve the "capabilities" and "model" such that tooling can then dynamically discover the remaining data within the Registry.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Design / Design: Protocol Bindings

requirements.text: Implementations MAY choose to incorporate authentication and/or authorization mechanisms as needed, but those are out of scope for this specification.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Design / Design: JSON Serialization

requirements.text: This specification defines the JSON serialization of the xRegistry entities. Alternative serialization formats MAY be defined.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Design / Design: JSON Serialization

requirements.text: If there is an issue with reading or parsing the data provided to the server, then an error ([parsing_data](#parsing_data)) MUST be generated.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Design / Design: Data Retrieval Issues

requirements.text: In general, if a server is unable to retrieve all of the data intended to be sent in a response, then an error ([data_retrieval_error](./spec.md#data_retrieval_error)) MUST be generated and the request rejected without any changes being made. However, it is permissible for a server to attempt some creative processing. For example, if while processing a query the server can only retrieve half of the entities to be returned at the current point in time, then it could return those with an indication of there being more (via use of a [pagination](../pagination/spec.md) type of specification). Then during the next query request it could return the remainder of the data - or an error if it is still not available to retrieve the data. Note that if an entity is to be sent, then it MUST be serialized in its entirety (all attributes, and requested child entities) or an error MUST be generated.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Design / Design: Importing Data

requirements.text: There might be situations where someone will do a query to retrieve data from a Registry, and then do an update operation to a Registry with that data. Depending on the use case, they might not want some of the retrieved data to be applied during the update. For example, they might not want the `epoch` validation checking to occur. Rather than forcing the user to edit the data to remove the potentially problematic attributes, a client MAY use the [Ignore Flag](#ignore-flag) to ignore some of the data in the incoming request.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Design / Design: JSON `$schema` keyword

requirements.text: Any JSON xRegistry metadata message that represents a single entity (i.e. not a map) MAY include a top-level "$schema" attribute that points to a JSON Schema document that describes the message contents. These notations can be used or ignored by receivers of these messages. There is no requirement for implementations of this specification to persist these values, to include them in responses or to use this information.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Design / Design: Implicit Creation of Parent Entities

requirements.text: To reduce the number of interactions needed when creating an entity, if any of its parent entities do not exist, then they MUST be implicitly created. Each of those entities MUST be created with the appropriate `<SINGULAR>id` as specified by the protocol-specific mechanism by which the nested entity is identified. For example, in HTTP the `<PATH>` would include the `<SINGULAR>id` values of the parent entities. If any of those entities have REQUIRED attributes whose values cannot be populated by the server or by defaults, then they cannot be implicitly created, and would need to be created directly. This also means that the creation of the original entity would fail and generate an error ([required_attribute_missing](./spec.md#required_attribute_missing)) for the appropriate parent entity.

review.note: Nested creation stages missing parents with path-derived identifiers. Tests cover a complete nested creation, rejection and rollback when the implicit Group has an unsatisfied required attribute (including the Group error subject), and successful creation when its default supplies that attribute.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Design / Design: Events

requirements.text: xRegistry defines a set of events that SHOULD be generated when changes are made to the entities within a Registry. See the [xRegistry Events](./events.md) specification for more information.

review.note: The server emits change events for created, updated and deleted entities and persists each interaction in the atomic outbox. The listed tests cover attribute changes and default-Version projections, descendant deletion and parent membership changes, exact committed CloudEvent identity/time, and outbox publication. This does not re-review or promote the separate Events requirements.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model

requirements.text: Unless otherwise stated in a protocol binding specification, if the processing of a request fails (even during the generation of the response) then an error MUST be generated and the entire request MUST be undone. See the [Error Processing](#error-processing) section for more information.

review.note: The engine renders the result and runs response preparation before publishing state, events and allocation mutations as one persistence commit. Tests verify rollback on cancellation and response-preparation failure, including no event publication and reuse of a failed WoT allocation.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Implementation Customizations

requirements.text: Any feature, whether it is specification-defined or not, that has not been explicitly defined as REQUIRED is OPTIONAL (but RECOMMENDED) to be supported by implementations. Implementations SHOULD document which features they do not support. For example, the specification defines a `createdat` attribute for the entities within a Registry. The specification is written such that it is assumed that if the entity is mutable, then the `createdat` attribute is mutable as well. However, it is permissible for implementations to ban updating of this attribute once the entity is created, if their requirements mandate this behaviour.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Implementation Customizations

requirements.text: Additionally, implementations MAY choose to customize the data and behavior on a per-user basis as needed. For example, the following non-exhaustive list of customizations might be implemented:

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Implementation Customizations

requirements.text: Implementations MAY (but are NOT REQUIRED) to validate cross-entity constraints that might be violated due to changes in a referenced entity. For example, [Endpoint's `envelope`](../endpoint/spec.md#envelope) attribute mandates that all Messages in that Endpoint use that same `envelope` value. One of those Messages might have a `basemessage` value that points to a Message that breaks that rule. For a variety of reasons (e.g. authorization constraints), server implementations might not be able to verify this constraint. Likewise, the same situation might occur via the use of `xref`. Clients need to be aware of these possibilities.

review.note: Cross-entity constraint validation is optional. This implementation elects to enforce reverse Group constraints on referenced targets; the tests exercise invalidating writes, authorization limits, atomic final-state evaluation, and cancellation rollback. The optional spec language does not require every implementation to provide this behavior.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Data Types

requirements.text: Unless otherwise noted, all attributes and extensions MUST be mutable and MUST be one of the following data types:

review.note: All 19 Core data types compile. The focused test checks each type and confirms that omitted `readonly` and `immutable` values default to `false` for custom attributes; the shared compiler applies these defaults at every declaration site.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Data Types

requirements.text: - `any` - an attribute of this type is one whose type is not known in advance and at runtime MUST be one of the concrete types listed here.

review.note: The validator preserves non-null JSON values declared as `any`. `AnyAttributesPreserveConcreteRuntimeJsonKinds` covers string, boolean, integer, decimal, array, and object values; `OpaqueAnyScopesRemainExemptEvenWhenTheirRuntimeValueIsScalar` verifies opaque object members are not reinterpreted as modeled attributes.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Data Types

requirements.text: - Some serializations, such as JSON, allow for a `null` value to appear in an array (e.g. `[ null, 2, 3 ]` in an array of integers). In these cases, while it is valid for the serialization being used, it is not valid for xRegistry since `null` is not a valid `integer`. Meaning, the serialization of an array that is syntactically valid for the format being used, but not semantically valid per the [xRegistry model](./model.md#registry-model) definition, MUST NOT be accepted and MUST generate an error ([invalid_attribute](#invalid_attribute)).

review.note: Typed array traversal rejects a null item as `invalid_attribute` at its index; `CollectionAndNestedErrorsRetainPrecisePointers` asserts the error code and pointer for `[1,null]`. The validator also rejects mismatched non-null items with the same code.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Data Types

requirements.text: - `map` - set of key/value pairs, where the key MUST be of type string. The value MUST be of one of the types defined here.

review.note: Map declarations require a typed item definition. The compiler parses item types through the Core type registry, and runtime validation applies that item definition to every value; tests preserve typed string values and reject null or integer values for a string map.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Data Types

requirements.text: - Each key MUST: - Be a non-empty string consisting of only lowercase alphanumeric characters (`[a-z0-9]`), `:`, `-`, `_` or a `.`. - Be no longer than 63 characters. - Start with an alphanumeric character. - Be unique within the scope of this map.

review.note: The validator enforces the map-key grammar and 63-character limit. `MapKeysFollowCoreCharacterAndLengthRules` checks allowed punctuation, the maximum length, and invalid forms; `DuplicateMapKeysAreRejectedDuringJsonParsing` rejects duplicate members at the map path.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Data Types

requirements.text: - `timestamp` - an [RFC3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339) timestamp. Use of a `time-zone` notation is RECOMMENDED. All timestamps returned by a server MUST be normalized to UTC to allow for easy (and consistent) comparisons.

review.note: The validator accepts RFC3339 timestamps with a zone and normalizes values to UTC. `ScalarValuesPreserveTypePrecisionAndNormalizeTimestamps` verifies offset conversion; `TimestampScalarBoundaryPreservesAllFractionalDigits` verifies precision preservation.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Data Types

requirements.text: - `xid` - MUST be a case-sensitive URL (xid) reference to another entity defined within the Registry. The actual entity attribute value MAY reference a non-existing entity (i.e. be a dangling pointer), but the syntax MUST reference a defined/valid type in the Registry. This type of attribute is used in place of `url` so that the Registry can do "type checking" to ensure the value references the correct type of Registry entity. See the definition of the [`target` model attribute](./model.md#attributesstringtarget) for more information. Its value MUST start with a `/`.

review.note: `RegistryPath.Parse` requires root-relative XIDs and preserves their path spelling. `CheckXidTarget` checks the referenced model type and target kind without checking entity existence, so dangling IDs remain valid. Tests cover case-preserving IDs, wrong types, absolute URL rejection, and dangling targets.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Data Types

requirements.text: - `xidtype` - MUST be a URL reference to an [xRegistry model](./model.md#registry-model) type. The reference MUST point to one of: the Registry itself (`/`), a Group type (`/<GROUPS>`), a Resource type (`/<GROUPS>/<RESOURCES>`) or Version type for a Resource (`/<GROUPS>/<RESOURCES>/versions`). Its value MUST reference a defined/valid type in the Registry. It MUST use the plural names of the referenced types, if it is a Group, Resource or Version.

review.note: `ModelPaths.ParseType` accepts `/`, defined plural Group types, Resource types, or their `/versions` collection; `CheckModelType` rejects undefined types. Tests cover each valid form and reject singular, unknown, entity, template, uppercase, and absolute-URL paths.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Data Types

requirements.text: The 6 variants of URI/URL are provided to allow for strict type adherence when needed. However, for attributes that are simply "pointers" that might in practice be any of those 6 types, it is RECOMMENDED that `uri` be used.

review.note: This recommendation is directed at model authors. The shipped model defines no generic pointer attribute whose type can vary among the six URI/URL variants; the implementation supports the `uri` type.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Data Types

requirements.text: Attributes that are defined to be relative URIs or URLs MUST state what they are relative to and any constraints on their values, if any. How, or where, this is specified is out of scope of this specification.

review.note: The requirement is directed at model declarations, but the spec defines no machine-readable field or validation rule for the base and value constraints. No such relative URI/URL attribute is declared by the shipped model; automatic enforcement for extension models remains unqualified.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Attributes

requirements.text: All attributes (specification-defined and extensions) MUST adhere to the following rules:

review.note: This clause introduces the following attribute-specific rules; it adds no behavior independent of those child requirements.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Attributes

requirements.text: - Their names MUST be between 1 and 63 characters in length.

review.note: Model declarations enforce the inclusive 1-63 character bound.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Attributes

requirements.text: - Their names MUST only contain lowercase alphanumeric characters or an underscore (`[a-z0-9_]`) and MUST NOT start with a digit (`[0-9]`).

review.note: Model declarations enforce the lowercase alphanumeric/underscore grammar and reject leading digits.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Attributes

requirements.text: - For string attributes, an empty string is a valid value and MUST NOT be treated the same as an attribute with no value (or absence of the attribute).

review.note: The validator preserves an explicitly supplied empty string as a present string value; an omitted attribute remains absent.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Attributes

requirements.text: - For scalar attributes, the string serialization of the attribute name and its value MUST NOT exceed 4096 bytes. This is to ensure that it can appear in an HTTP header without exceeding implementation limits (see [RFC6265/Limits](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6265#section-6.1)). In cases where larger amounts of data are needed, it is RECOMMENDED that an attribute (of type URL) be defined that references a separate document. For example, `documentation` can be considered such an attribute for `description`.

review.note: Scalar name/value serialization is capped at 4096 UTF-8 bytes; the system model exposes the documentation URL field for longer descriptions.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Attributes

requirements.text: - If an attribute's type is not fully defined (i.e. it is defined as an `any` type) but a concrete type is needed to successfully process it, then the server SHOULD default it to type `string`. For example, if an extension is defined as a map whose values are of type `any`, but it appears in an HTTP header with a value of `5` (and it is not clear if this would be an integer or a string), if the server needs to convert this to a concrete data type, then `string` is the default choice.

review.note: The HTTP header codec uses the raw field text as a string for Any-valued attributes and map members when conversion to JSON metadata is required.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Attributes

requirements.text: - There might be cases when it is not possible to know whether a field name is part of an object (in which case it is an "attribute name"), or is part of a map (in which case it is a "key name"). This decision would impact verification of the field since key names allow for a superset of the characters allowed for attribute names. This will only happen when the `any` type has been used higher-up in the model. As a result, any portion of the entity that appears under the scope of an `any` typed attribute or map-value is NOT REQUIRED to be validated except to ensure that the syntax is valid per the rules of the serialization format used.

review.note: Any-typed attributes and map values are preserved without recursive model validation; outer map keys remain validated and JSON syntax is still parsed.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Attributes

requirements.text: - Attribute instances that have no value (and have no default value defined) are semantically equivalent to having a value of `null` or not being present at all, and for the sake of brevity, SHOULD NOT be serialized as part of its owning entity in server responses. Likewise, specifying them with a value of `null` in client requests SHOULD be reserved for cases where the client needs to indicate a request to delete that attribute value rather than to leave the attribute untouched (absent in the request), such as when `PATCH` is used in the [HTTP Binding Protocol](./http.md).

review.note: Complete metadata validation omits explicit null values without defaults; client-input validation preserves null as a deletion request and distinguishes it from omission.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Attributes

requirements.text: - Unless otherwise stated, requests to update read-only attributes MUST be silently ignored by servers, even if the contents of those attributes are invalid.

review.note: Client-input validation skips read-only values before inspecting their JSON shape, so invalid submitted content is ignored.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Attributes

requirements.text: - Unless otherwise stated, server managed changes to read-only attributes MUST NOT be treated the same as user initiated changes to non-read-only attributes with respect to updating attributes such as `modifiedat` and `epoch`. In other words, as these read-only attributes are changed, the entity MUST NOT be considered "updated".

review.note: Resource validation updates read-only validation metadata without advancing the Version epoch or modifiedat; a direct user update to a mutable attribute advances both.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Extensions

requirements.text: Implementations of this specification MAY define additional (extension) attributes. However, they MUST adhere to the following rules:

review.note: The following entries specify extension-attribute model and validation obligations; this introductory clause has no independent behavior.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Extensions

requirements.text: - All extension attributes that appear in the serialization of an entity MUST conform to the model definition of the Registry, otherwise an error ([unknown_attribute](#unknown_attribute)) MUST be generated. This means that they MUST satisfy at least one of the following:

review.note: Declared extension values are validated against the effective model; undeclared top-level and nested fields produce unknown_attribute.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Extensions

requirements.text: - They MUST NOT conflict with the name of an attribute defined by this specification, including the `<RESOURCE>*` and `<COLLECTION>*` attributes that are implicitly defined. Note that if a Resource type has the [`hasdocument` aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument) set the `false` then this rule does not apply for the `<RESOURCE>*` attributes as those attributes are not implicitly defined for that Resource type.

review.note: The compiler rejects incompatible definitions of document and collection system attributes. Resource document names are available as extensions when hasdocument is false.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Extensions

requirements.text: - It is RECOMMENDED that extension attributes on different entities do not use the same name unless they have the exact same semantic meaning.

review.note: This recommendation guides extension-model authors; the server cannot determine whether same-named attributes on different entities have identical semantics.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Extensions

requirements.text: - It is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED that they be named in such a way as to avoid potential conflicts with future xRegistry specification-defined attributes. For example, use of a model (or domain) specific prefix could be used to help avoid possible future conflicts.

review.note: Prefix choice is guidance for extension-model authors and cannot be enforced without imposing a naming convention absent from the specification.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Extensions

requirements.text: Use of an attribute (specification-defined, or extension) that does not conform to this specification MUST generate an error ([invalid_attribute](#invalid_attribute)).

review.note: Invalid scalar, typed collection, and name/value constraints produce invalid_attribute diagnostics.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes

requirements.text: For easy reference, the JSON serialization of these attributes MUST adhere to this form:

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `<SINGULAR>id` (`id`) Attribute

requirements.text: - Description: An immutable unique identifier of the owning entity. The actual name of this attribute will vary based on the model entity it identifies. For example, a `schema` Resource would use an attribute name of `schemaid`. This attribute MUST be named `registryid` for the Registry itself, and MUST be named `versionid` for all Version entities.

review.note: The effective model uses registryid at the Registry, each Group/Resource uses its declared singular plus id, and each Version also has versionid; verified for required immutable model attributes.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `<SINGULAR>id` (`id`) Attribute

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

review.note: The Core entity ID attributes are required in the compiled Registry, Group, Resource, and Version models.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `<SINGULAR>id` (`id`) Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be immutable.

review.note: The compiled Core entity ID attributes are immutable, and server updates reject a changed nested ID.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `<SINGULAR>id` (`id`) Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a non-empty string consisting of [RFC3986 `unreserved` characters](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-2.3) (ALPHA / DIGIT / `-` / `.` / `_` / `~`), `:` or `@`, MUST start with ALPHA, DIGIT or `_` and MUST be between 1 and 128 characters in length. Otherwise, an error ([malformed_id](#malformed_id)) MUST be generated.

review.note: The RegistryId parser enforces the specified starting characters, allowed set, and 1-128 character range with malformed_id on rejection.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `<SINGULAR>id` (`id`) Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be unique (case-insensitively) within the scope of the entity's parent.

review.note: Sibling IDs with case-only differences conflict, while encoded path IDs resolve to the same entity identity.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `<SINGULAR>id` (`id`) Attribute

requirements.text: - This attribute MUST be treated as case-sensitive for look-up purposes. For example, an HTTP request URL to an entity with the wrong case for its `<SINGULAR>id` MUST be treated as "not found".

review.note: A lookup using the exact stored ID succeeds, while a case-only variant returns not_found.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `<SINGULAR>id` (`id`) Attribute

requirements.text: - In cases where an entity's `<SINGULAR>id` is specified outside of the serialization of the entity (e.g. part of a request  URL, or a map key), its presence within the serialization of the entity is OPTIONAL. However, if present, it MUST be the same as any other specification of the `<SINGULAR>id` outside of the entity, and it MUST be the same as the entity's existing `<SINGULAR>id` if one exists, otherwise an error ([mismatched_id](#mismatched_id)) MUST be generated.

review.note: Path/map identity suffices when the body omits the ID; a conflicting supplied nested ID is rejected with mismatched_id.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `<SINGULAR>id` (`id`) Attribute

requirements.text: While `<SINGULAR>id` can be something like a UUID, when possible, it is RECOMMENDED that it be human friendly as these values will often appear in user-facing situations such as URLs or as command-line parameters. Additionally, In cases where [`name`](#name-attribute) is absent, the `<SINGULAR>id` might be used as the display name.

review.note: This is producer guidance rather than a server-enforceable constraint; the implementation accepts identifiers allowed by the normative grammar.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `self` Attribute

requirements.text: - Each entity in the Registry MUST have a unique `self` URL value that locates the entity in the Registry hierarchy and from where the entity can be retrieved.

review.note: The server emits distinct self URLs matching the Registry, Group, Resource, metadata, and Version retrieval paths.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `self` Attribute

requirements.text: - When specified as an absolute URL, it MUST be based on the URL of the Registry root appended with the hierarchy path of the Registry entities/collections leading to the entity (its `xid` value).

review.note: Absolute self values use the configured public Registry root followed by the entity hierarchy path.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `self` Attribute

requirements.text: - When specified as a relative URL, it MUST end with the entity's `xid` value.

review.note: Document-view self pointers are checked to end with the corresponding entity xid for Resources and Versions.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `self` Attribute

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

review.note: The compiled Registry, Group, Resource, Version, and Resource metadata models all require self.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `self` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be immutable.

review.note: The compiled self attribute is immutable across Registry, Group, Resource, Version, and Resource metadata planes.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `self` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a non-empty absolute URL based on the URL of the Registry.

review.note: API-view self values are non-empty absolute URLs rooted at the configured public Registry URL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `self` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a read-only attribute.

review.note: The compiled self attribute is marked read-only across Registry, Group, Resource, Version, and Resource metadata planes.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `self` Attribute

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

review.note: Document-view serializations include self pointers for the represented Resource and Version entities.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `self` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be immutable.

review.note: The compiled self attribute is immutable across all entity planes, including the document-view representation.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `self` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a relative URL of the form `#JSON-POINTER` where the `JSON-POINTER` locates this entity within the current document. See [Doc Flag](#doc-flag) for more information.

review.note: Document-view self values use fragment JSON Pointers locating the entity in the current export/document.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `self` Attribute

requirements.text: - This URL MUST NOT include any indicator signifying the entity's xRegistry metadata rather than its domain-specific document (e.g. `$details` in the [HTTP binding](./http.md) case).

review.note: Document-view self pointers are fragment references and do not carry the HTTP $details marker.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `shortself` Attribute

requirements.text: - Description: A server-generated unique absolute URL for an entity. This attribute MUST be an alternative URL for the entity's `self` (non-`$details` suffixed) URL. When a client constructs a request based on the `shortself` URL, it MAY append `$details`, or any flags (e.g. query parameters), that are valid for use on the `self` URL.

review.note: The server emits absolute /~/ URLs that resolve to the same entity, and callers can append a Version path and $details suffix.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `shortself` Attribute

requirements.text: The intention is that `shortself` SHOULD be shorter in length than `self` such that it MAY be used when the length of the URL referencing the entity is important. For example, in cases where the size of a message referencing this entity needs to be as small as possible.

review.note: Generated 72-bit tokens make shortself shorter than self for the tested Resource and Version document URLs; the Registry root and shallow paths may remain longer, so this SHOULD is qualified rather than universal.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `shortself` Attribute

requirements.text: If an entity is deleted and then a new entity is created that results in the same `self` URL, this specification does not mandate that the same `shortself` be generated, but it MAY do so.

review.note: The specification permits either reusing or changing the shortself after an entity is deleted and recreated with the same self URL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `shortself` Attribute

requirements.text: This attribute MUST only appear in the serialization if the `shortself` capability is enabled. However, if this capability is enabled, then disabled, and then re-enabled, the `shortself` values MUST retain their original values. In this sense, implementations might create a `shortself` that is known for the lifetime of the entity and the capability controls whether the attribute is serialized or not.

review.note: Disabling the capability hides shortself; re-enabling it after restart restores the entity's original URL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `shortself` Attribute

requirements.text: When the `shortself` capability is disabled, the attribute name `shortself` is still a reserved attribute name and MUST NOT be used as an extension.

review.note: The Core model reserves shortself even when the runtime capability is disabled.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `shortself` Attribute

requirements.text: - REQUIRED if the `shortself` capability is enabled.

review.note: When enabled, shortself is present on the Registry, Group, Resource, metadata, and Version representations.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `shortself` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST NOT appear in responses if the `shortself` capability is disabled.

review.note: With shortself disabled, API projections omit it from the Registry, Group, Resource, metadata, and Version outputs.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `shortself` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be immutable for the lifetime of the entity.

review.note: The short URL survives capability disable/enable and frozen persistence restart for the same entity.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `shortself` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be unique across all entities in the Registry.

review.note: Generated shortself values are distinct across the Registry, Group, Resource, metadata, and Version planes.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `shortself` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a non-empty absolute URL referencing the same entity as the `self` URL, either directly or indirectly via a protocol-specific redirect.

review.note: Generated shortself values are absolute and resolve to the entity's xid; aliases retain their own identity when resolving appended Version paths.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `shortself` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a read-only attribute.

review.note: The compiled shortself attribute is read-only across Registry, Group, Resource, Version, and Resource metadata planes.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `shortself` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST NOT contain the `$` character as that is reserved for specification defined suffixes (such as `$details`).

review.note: Generated shortself values omit the reserved $ character, including when a caller appends a Version path.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `xid` Attribute

requirements.text: - Description: An immutable server-generated unique identifier of the entity. Unlike `<SINGULAR>id`, which is unique within the scope of its parent, `xid` MUST be unique across the entire Registry, and as such is defined to be a relative URL from the root of the Registry. This value MUST be the same as the `<PATH>` portion of its `self` URL, after the Registry's base URL, without any protocol-specific xRegistry suffix (e.g. `$details` in the HTTP case). Unlike some other relative URIs, `xid` values MUST NOT be shortened based on the incoming request's URL; `xid`s are always relative to the root path of the Registry.

review.note: Server responses derive each entity XID from its full Registry path. Tests compare it with self, preserve it in nested projections, exclude $details from Version XIDs, and verify uniqueness.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `xid` Attribute

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

review.note: The compiled Core model declares xid required on Registry, Group, Resource, Version, and Resource Metadata.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `xid` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be immutable.

review.note: The compiled Core model declares xid immutable and read-only on each entity plane; creation ignores invalid client-supplied values at the root and nested Group.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `xid` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a case-sensitive non-empty relative URL to the current entity.

review.note: RegistryPath.ToXid preserves escaped identifier case and emits a non-empty Registry-root-relative path; generated XIDs are checked across entity planes and nested projections.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `xid` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be of the form: `/[<GROUPS>/<GID>[/<RESOURCES>/<RID>[/meta | /versions/<VID>]]]` and reference valid Group and Resource types. Otherwise, an error ([malformed_xid](#malformed_xid)) MUST be generated.

review.note: RegistryPath recognizes only defined entity shapes, generated XIDs use declared Group and Resource paths, and malformed typed XIDs return the malformed_xid error.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `xid` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST start with the `/` character.

review.note: RegistryPath.ToXid and server responses emit slash-rooted paths, with the Registry root represented by /.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `xid` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a read-only attribute.

review.note: The compiled Core model marks xid read-only on each entity plane; invalid client-supplied values are silently ignored and server-generated path values are returned.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `epoch` Attribute

requirements.text: - Description: A numeric value used to determine whether an entity has been modified. Each time the associated entity is updated, this value MUST be set to a new value that is greater than the current one. This attribute MUST be updated for every update operation, even if no attributes were explicitly updated, such as a "patch" type of operation when no attributes are specified. This then acts like a `touch` type of operation.

review.note: Epochs use arbitrary-precision unsigned values and advance on entity updates, including no-op PATCH/REPLACE operations; tests verify monotonic changes and large values.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `epoch` Attribute

requirements.text: During a create operation, if this attribute is present in the request, then it MUST be silently ignored by the server.

review.note: Creation ignores submitted epoch values, including invalid shapes; newly created Groups, Resources, and Versions receive a generated epoch of zero.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `epoch` Attribute

requirements.text: During an update, or delete, operation, if this attribute is present in the request, then an error ([mismatched_epoch](#mismatched_epoch)) MUST be generated if the request includes a non-null value that differs from the existing value. This allows for the detection of concurrent, but conflicting, updates to the same entity to be detected. A value of `null` MUST be treated the same as a request with no `epoch` attribute at all, in which case a check MUST NOT be performed.

review.note: Non-null update and delete guards must match the stored epoch; null or absent values skip the guard, invalid values fail, and guarded deletion is atomic.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `epoch` Attribute

requirements.text: If an entity has a nested xRegistry collection, its `epoch` value MUST be updated each time an entity in that collection is added or removed. However, its `epoch` value MUST NOT be updated solely due to modifications of an existing entity in the collection.

review.note: Adding or removing Groups, Resources, and Versions advances the owning Registry, Group, or Resource Metadata epoch; updating an existing child does not advance its parent.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `epoch` Attribute

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

review.note: The Core model requires epoch on Registry, Group, Resource Metadata, and Version entities, and server responses provide the generated value.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `epoch` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a [read-only](#read-only-changed) attribute.

review.note: The Core model declares epoch read-only; incoming values serve as update/delete guards and are ignored during entity creation.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `epoch` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be an unsigned integer equal to or greater than zero.

review.note: The Core model defines epoch as UInteger; tests cover zero, huge non-negative values, negative, fractional, and non-integer guards.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `epoch` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST increase in value each time the entity is updated.

review.note: Each update advances its entity epoch, including no-op writes; arbitrary-precision values increment without narrowing.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `name` Attribute

requirements.text: - Description: A human-readable name of the entity. This is often used as the "display name" for an entity rather than the `<SINGULAR>id` especially when the `<SINGULAR>id` might be something that isn't human friendly, like a UUID. In cases where `name` is absent, the `<SINGULAR>id` value SHOULD be displayed in its place.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `name` Attribute

requirements.text: This specification places no uniqueness constraints on this attribute. This means that two sibling entities MAY have the same value. Therefore, this value MUST NOT be used for unique identification purposes, the `<SINGULAR>id` MUST be used instead.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `name` Attribute

requirements.text: Note that implementations MAY choose to enforce additional constraints on this value. For example, they could mandate that `<SINGULAR>id` and `name` be the same value. Or, it could mandate that `name` be unique within the scope of a parent entity. How any such requirement is shared with all parties is out of scope of this specification.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `name` Attribute

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `name` Attribute

requirements.text: - If present, MUST be non-empty.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `description` Attribute

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `documentation` Attribute

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `documentation` Attribute

requirements.text: - If present, MUST be a non-empty URL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `documentation` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST support retrieving the information via a query to this URL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `icon` Attribute

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `icon` Attribute

requirements.text: - If present, MUST be a non-empty URL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `icon` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be retrievable via a query to this URL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `icon` Attribute

requirements.text: - STRONGLY RECOMMENDED that the icon be in SVG or PNG format and square.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `labels` Attribute

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `labels` Attribute

requirements.text: - If present, MUST be a map of zero or more name/value string pairs. See [Attributes and Extensions](#attributes-and-extensions) for more information.

review.note: The labels map accepts zero entries and string values, including the empty string. Tests reject null or non-string values and exercise map-key boundaries and allowed characters.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `labels` Attribute

requirements.text: - Keys MUST be non-empty strings.

review.note: The labels map rejects empty keys and accepts nonempty keys. Map-key tests also cover the general Core grammar and length boundaries.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `labels` Attribute

requirements.text: - Values MAY be empty strings.

review.note: Entity label serialization preserves an empty string value without converting it to null or absence.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `createdat` Attribute

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

review.note: The model test verifies required Timestamp attributes on Registry, Group, Resource, Resource Meta, and Version definitions. Server cases assert nested creation values and explicit/null createdat updates.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `createdat` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a [RFC3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339) timestamp.

review.note: Timestamp parsing accepts RFC3339 values and normalizes offsets to UTC; scalar tests cover invalid values and fractional precision.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `createdat` Attribute

requirements.text: - This specification places no restrictions on the value of this attribute, nor on its value relative to its `modifiedat` value or the current date/time. Implementations MAY choose to restrict its values if necessary.

review.note: The server test replaces an existing createdat with a distinct value and confirms that null resets it to the injected clock.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `createdat` Attribute

requirements.text: - If present in a write operation request, the value MUST override any existing value, however a value of `null` MUST use the current date/time as the new value.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `createdat` Attribute

requirements.text: - When absent in an update request, any existing value MUST remain unchanged.

review.note: Server and scalar tests confirm that updates omitting createdat preserve the existing value.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `createdat` Attribute

requirements.text: - During the processing of a single request, all entities that have their `createdat` or `modifiedat` attributes set to the current date/time MUST use the same value in all cases.

review.note: A single request creates a Group, Resource, and Version; the test asserts that each createdat and modifiedat value is equal across those entities.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `modifiedat` Attribute

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

review.note: The model test verifies required Timestamp attributes on Registry, Group, Resource, Resource Meta, and Version definitions. Server cases assert timestamps on created entities and collection membership changes.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `modifiedat` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a [RFC3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339) timestamp representing the time when the entity was last updated.

review.note: Server and scalar tests verify RFC3339 timestamp values, UTC normalization, and invalid timestamp rejection.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `modifiedat` Attribute

requirements.text: - This specification places no restrictions on the value of this attribute, nor on its value relative to its `createdat` value or the current date/time. Implementations MAY choose to restrict its values if necessary.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `modifiedat` Attribute

requirements.text: - Any update operation (even one that does not change any attribute, MUST update this attribute. This then acts like a `touch` type of operation.

review.note: The server test submits an empty update and asserts that modifiedat advances to the injected current time.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `modifiedat` Attribute

requirements.text: - Updates to an existing entity in an xRegistry collection MUST NOT cause an update to its parent entity's `modifiedat` value. However, adding or removing an entity from a nested xRegistry collection MUST update the `modifiedat` value of the parent entity.

review.note: The test asserts that Group, Resource, and Resource Meta modifiedat values advance on child creation or removal, while updates to existing children leave the parent's modifiedat unchanged.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `modifiedat` Attribute

requirements.text: - If present in a write operation request, the following applies: - If the request value is `null` or the same as the existing value, then the current date/time MUST be used as its new value. - If the request value is different than the existing value, then the request value MUST be used as its new value.

review.note: The server test asserts that distinct supplied values replace modifiedat, while equal and null values reset it to the injected current time.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `modifiedat` Attribute

requirements.text: - When absent in a write operation request, it MUST be set to the current date/time.

review.note: The server test omits modifiedat from an update and asserts that the injected current time is used; the empty update also verifies the touch behavior.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `modifiedat` Attribute

requirements.text: - During the processing of a single request, all entities that have their `createdat` or `modifiedat` attributes set to the current date/time MUST use the same value in all cases.

review.note: A single request creates a Group, Resource, and Version; the test asserts that each createdat and modifiedat value is equal across those entities.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `deprecated` Attribute

requirements.text:
- `effective`
An OPTIONAL property indicating the time when the entity entered, or will enter, a deprecated state. The date MAY be in the past or future. If this property is not present the entity is already in a deprecated state. If present, this MUST be an [RFC3339][rfc3339] timestamp.

review.note: The model test verifies optional Timestamp fields on Group and Resource Meta. Server cases cover absent, past, and future effective values and confirm that a future effective date without removal does not block deletion; scalar cases verify RFC3339 handling.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `deprecated` Attribute

requirements.text:
- `removal`
An OPTIONAL property indicating the time when the entity MAY be removed. The entity MUST NOT be removed before this time. If this property is not present, the client cannot make any assumptions as to when the entity might be removed. Note: as with most properties, this property is mutable. If present, this MUST be an [RFC3339][rfc3339] timestamp and MUST NOT be sooner than the `effective` time if present.

review.note: Completed Group and Resource Meta deprecation values reject removal before effective with invalid_attribute at deprecated.removal. Comparison uses normalized UTC instants and full fractional precision; equal instants in different offsets are allowed. A future removal promise blocks direct deletion, parent cascade, and deletion of the last Version without changing stored data or outbox state. Deletion resumes at the promised instant, the promise remains mutable, and nanosecond values are not rounded down. Without a removal value, a future effective value does not block deletion. These are implementation/evidence mappings, not release or all-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `deprecated` Attribute

requirements.text:
- `alternative`
An OPTIONAL property specifying the URL to an alternative entity the client can consider as a replacement for this entity. There is no guarantee that the referenced entity is an exact replacement, rather the client is expected to investigate the entity to determine if it is appropriate.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `deprecated` Attribute

requirements.text:
- `documentation`
An OPTIONAL property specifying the URL to additional information about the deprecation of the entity. This specification does not mandate any particular format or information, however some possibilities include: reasons for the deprecation or additional information about likely alternative entities. The URL MUST support retrieval of the information via a query.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `deprecated` Attribute

requirements.text: Note that an implementation is not mandated to use this attribute in advance of removing an entity, but it is RECOMMENDED to do so.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `deprecated` Attribute

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL

review.note: The model test asserts that deprecated and each of its defined fields are optional on Group and Resource Meta, and absent from the Registry, Resource, and Version planes.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `constraints` Attribute

requirements.text: These restrictions are designed to only allow subsetting of the definitions specified by the Resource type model and any Group type model [`constraints`](model.md#groupsstringconstraints) defined. They MUST NOT be used to extend the allowable values of the attributes being constrained.

review.note: Tests verify Group-instance enum and default restrictions against both Group-type and Resource-type constraints, plus matching or newly introduced equals expressions. Widening enum/default values and replacing an inherited equals expression are rejected.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `constraints` Attribute

requirements.text: The two layers of definitions of the constraints are merged such that any individual constraint aspect defined at the Group instance level MUST only further restrict any constraint aspect mentioned at the Group type level. Absence of (or `null` value for) an aspect at the Group instance level MUST NOT impact any constraints defined at the Group type level.

review.note: Tests verify instance enum/default narrowing, inheritance for absent or null aspects, exact equals matching, and the permitted introduction of equals when absent at the Group-type level. Invalid widening and changed equals expressions are rejected.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Attributes and Extensions / Common Attributes / `constraints` Attribute

requirements.text: - If `enum` is specified at both levels, then the Group instance `enum` set MUST be a subset of the `enum` defined at the Group type level.

review.note: Tests cover a proper subset, the unchanged set, an overlapping non-subset, and a superset against the Group-type enum while the Resource-type enum is wider. Accepted sets govern Resource values; invalid sets are rejected.

For clarity, a Group instance MAY introduce an `equals` aspect for a constraint key defined at the model Group type level that has no `equals` aspect.

review.note: Tests accept an identical instance expression, reject a changed expression, and accept an instance-added equals aspect when the Group-type constraint has none. Absent, null, and empty values preserve the inherited comparison.

review.note: API and document-view tests exercise Group, Resource and Version collections, including filtered and empty responses. This umbrella clause remains pending because it covers the full collection contract, whose individual requirements are tracked below.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections

requirements.text: The serialization of a collection is done as 3 attributes and they MUST adhere to their respective forms as follows:

review.note: API and document-view tests exercise collection maps, URLs and counts for Group, Resource and Version collections. This umbrella clause remains pending until every individual form and view requirement below is closed.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections

requirements.text: - The term `<COLLECTION>` MUST be the plural name of the collection (e.g. `endpoints`, `versions`).

review.note: API and document-view assertions verify plural collection names at Registry, Group and Resource levels, including the versions collection.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections

requirements.text: - The `<COLLECTION>url` attribute MUST be a URL that can be used to retrieve the `<COLLECTION>` map via a protocol-specific query mechanism. This URL MAY include any necessary [filtering](#filter-flag) and MUST be a read-only attribute. This attribute MUST be an absolute URL except in document view when the collection is inlined, in which case it MUST be a relative URL.

review.note: API tests assert absolute URLs at Registry, Group and Resource levels and follow a returned Version-collection URL. Document-view tests assert response-local relative pointers for inlined collections. Filtered URL generation and ignored read-only URL input are also covered.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections

requirements.text: - The `<COLLECTION>count` attribute MUST contain the number of entities in the `<COLLECTION>` map (after any necessary [filtering](#filter-flag)) and MUST be a read-only attribute.

review.note: Counts match filtered maps for empty and nonempty selections, and API/document-view tests assert counts at Group, Resource and Version collections. An attempted request overwrite is ignored and the computed count is returned.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections

requirements.text: - The `<COLLECTION>` attribute is a map and MUST contain the entities of the collection (after any necessary [filtering](#filter-flag)), and MUST use the `<SINGULAR>id` of each entity as its map key.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections

requirements.text: - The key of each entity in the collection map MUST be unique within the scope of the collection.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections

requirements.text: When the `<COLLECTION>` attribute is expected to be present in the serialization, but the number of entities in the collection is zero, it MUST still be included as an empty map (e.g. `{}`) in the serialization.

review.note: API and document-view tests assert empty maps when inline selection includes an empty collection, and query tests cover an empty filtered collection.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections / Collections in Document View

review.note: Optional marker only. The operative API and document-view presence rules are tracked in their own requirements.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections / Collections in Document View

requirements.text: - `<COLLECTION>` is conditional in responses based on the values in the [Inline Flag](#inline-flag). If the collection is not part of the flag value then `<COLLECTION>` MUST NOT be included in the response.

review.note: Document-view tests verify selected collections appear, including empty maps, while unselected collections are omitted. API-view tests cover the same inline selection rule and preserve URLs/counts when a map is omitted.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections / Collections in API View

requirements.text: - `<COLLECTION>url` is REQUIRED for responses even if there are no entities in the collection.

review.note: API-view assertions verify absolute collection URLs at Registry, Group and Resource levels, including empty collections and responses where the map is not inlined.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections / Collections in API View

requirements.text: - `<COLLECTION>count` is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED for responses even if there are no entities in the collection. This requirement is not mandated to allow for cases where calculating the exact count is too costly.

review.note: The implementation emits counts for empty and nonempty collections; tests assert exact counts for filtered, Registry, Group, Resource and Version views.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections / Collections in API View

requirements.text: - `<COLLECTION>url` and `<COLLECTION>count` are OPTIONAL in requests and MUST be silently ignored by the server if present.

review.note: A Group PATCH supplies invalid collection URL/count values; the request succeeds and returns the server-computed collection link and count.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections / Collections in API View

review.note: API-view tests verify that inline-selected maps are present, including empty maps, and that nonselected maps are omitted while their required URL/count metadata remains.

review.note: Optional marker only. The operative collection update behavior is tracked in the nested-collection requirements.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections / Updating Nested Registry Collections

requirements.text: When updating an entity that can contain xRegistry collections, the request MAY contain the 3 collection attributes. The `<COLLECTION>url` and `<COLLECTION>count` attributes MUST be silently ignored by the server.

review.note: A Group PATCH supplies invalid collection URL/count values; the request succeeds and returns the server-computed collection link and count.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections / Updating Nested Registry Collections

requirements.text: If the `<COLLECTION>` attribute is present, the server MUST process each entity in the collection map as a request to create or update that entity according to the semantics of the operation method used. An entry in the map that isn't a valid entity (e.g. is `null`) MUST generate an error ([bad_request](#bad_request)).

review.note: Tests exercise POST nested Group creation, PATCH nested Resource updates, and rejection of a null nested entity with bad_request.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections / Updating Nested Registry Collections

requirements.text: Any error while processing a nested collection entity MUST result in the entire request being rejected.

review.note: A nested null-entity failure rejects the parent PATCH; assertions verify the parent name, epoch and existing child collection remain unchanged.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections / Updating Nested Registry Collections

requirements.text: An absent `<COLLECTION>` attribute, or empty map, MUST be interpreted as a request to not modify the collection at all.

review.note: Tests update a nested child, then verify both an omitted collection and an explicit empty map preserve it.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections / Updating Nested Registry Collections

requirements.text: If a client wishes to delete an entity from the collection, or replace the entire collection, the client MUST use a "delete" type of operations on the collection. This means that delete operations on these entities would need to be handled in dedicated operations, separate from update operations.

review.note: The collection tests show PATCH with absent/empty nested maps preserves existing members, while collection DELETE requests remove selected or all entities.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Registry Collections / Updating Nested Registry Collections

requirements.text: In cases where a Resource update operation includes attributes meant to be applied to the "default" Version of a Resource, and the incoming inlined `versions` collections includes that "default" Version, the Resource's default Version attributes MUST be silently ignored. This is to avoid any possible conflicting data between the two sets of data for that Version. In other words, the Version attributes in the incoming `versions` collection wins. See [Resource Processing Algorithm](#resource-processing-algorithm) for more details.

review.note: A Resource update supplies an invalid top-level default-Version value and a valid value for that same Version in the nested versions map; the nested Version value is returned.

requirements.text: Some of the items listed are available via more than one mechanism. For example, "model", in the HTTP protocol case, is available the `/model` API as well as via the `?inline=model` query parameter. For example, it would violate this specification if the `/model` API was supported but `?inline=model` was not, assuming the `?inline` flag was supported. If the `?inline` flag, in general, was not supported then only allowing the retrieval of the model via the `/model` API is permitted. requirements.text: Groups represent entities that typically act as a collection mechanism for related Resources. However, it is worth noting that Groups do not have to have Resources associated with them. It is possible to have Groups be the main (or only) entity of a Registry. Each Group type MAY have any number of Resource types within it. This specification does not define how the Resources within a Group type are related to each other.
