requirements.text: - However, when the Resource is created as part of the current operation there is no "prior" default Version, so knowing how to apply those attributes requires some additional clarity: - If a Resource-level `versionid` attribute is present, and that Version is not in the request's `versions` collection, then a new Version with that `versionid` MUST be created with the Resource-level attributes. If it is in the `versions` collection then the Resource-level attributes MUST be ignored. - If `versionid` is not present, but `meta.defaultversionid` is present, and that Version is not in the request's `versions` collection, then a new Version with that `versionid` MUST be created, with the Resource-level attributes. If it is in the `versions` collection then the Resource-level attributes MUST be ignored. Also see [SetDefaultVersionID Flag](#setdefaultversionid-flag) for an additional mechanism by which it might be set. - If neither of those attributes are present, then the `versions` collection will dictate the result: - If `versions` is missing, or empty, then the server MUST generate a new unique [`versionid` value](#version-ids) and create a new Version using that value, with the Resource-level attributes. - If `versions` is present with at least one Version, then the Resource-level attributes MUST be ignored. This is because without any indication from the client as to which Version the Resource-level attributes need to be applied to, rather than creating a new Version, the assumption is that `versions` contains all of the Versions that are meant to be created.

Note that going from a "normal" Resource to a cross-reference Resource does not have this guarantee. If the target Resource no longer exists then `target_Resource_Epoch` MUST be treated as zero.

requirements.text: An `xref` value that points to a non-existing Resource, either because it was deleted, never existed or the current client does not have permission to see it, is not an error and is not a condition that a server is REQUIRED to detect. In these "dangling xref" situations, the serialization of the source Resource will not include any target Resource attributes or nested collections. Rather, it will only show the `xref` and ID-like attributes. Therefore, a client that receives a response containing only those attributes can treat this as an indicator that the target Resource is inaccessible, and can make the determination as to whether this is something to investigate or not.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Resource Entity / Cross Referencing Resources

requirements.text: However, a non-existing Resource is not the same as a poorly formed XID value. An `xref` that isn't syntactically correct, or references a non-existing Group type or Resource type , MUST generate an error ([malformed_xref](#malformed_xref)).

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `readonly` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a [read-only](#read-only-changed) attribute for non-admin users.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `readonly` Attribute

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `readonly` Attribute

requirements.text: - It MUST be a case-sensitive `true` or `false`.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `readonly` Attribute

requirements.text: - A request to update a read-only Resource SHOULD generate an error ([readonly](#readonly)) unless the [Ignore Flag](#ignore-flag) was used with the `readonly` value, in which case the error MUST be silently ignored, and the Resource MUST remain unchanged.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `compatibility` Attribute

requirements.text: For `compatibility` strategies that require understanding the lineage relationship between the Versions, the [`ancestorid`](#ancestorid-attribute) attribute on each Version MUST be used to determine that information.

review.note: Independent root Versions are accepted without comparing against unrelated collection neighbors. Reparenting the existing int-to-long lineage to a string root fails compatibility_violation; rejected ancestry changes preserve exact metadata, bytes and events across restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `compatibility` Attribute

requirements.text: This specification defines the following enumeration values. Implementations MAY choose to extend this list, or use a subset of it.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `compatibility` Attribute

requirements.text: When not specified, there is no statement being made as to the compatibility relationship between the Resource's Versions and the server MUST NOT perform any `compatibility` checking.

review.note: With format validation enabled, independently absent compatibility mode performs only syntax checks. Adding/removing mode changes real reference acquisition counts and creates/clears results for both Versions under both strictness settings.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `compatibility` Attribute

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `compatibility` Attribute

requirements.text: - If present, MUST be a case-insensitive non-empty value from the Registry's [`capabilities.compatibilities`](#compatibilities-capability) values for the set of `format` values used by the Versions of the Resource.

review.note: System Meta compatibility modes use case-insensitive model enum admission; selected validator capabilities are checked separately. The unconditional capabilities-membership requirement conflicts with Model strictvalidation permitting unsupported modes to remain unchecked when false. Live Core still contains both rules; xregistry/spec#721 W27 proposes distinguishing model admission from validator support. Keep this clause pending until the conflict is resolved.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `compatibility` Attribute

requirements.text: - When changing the value of this attribute, it MUST be applied to all Versions of the Resource, and an error ([compatibility_violation](#compatibility_violation)) MUST be generated if any Version can not conform to the requirements of the specified compatibility value.

review.note: Changing backward to forward rejects an incompatible older non-default int-to-long lineage even when the default Version is an independent string root. Mode and all Version metadata, bytes and events survive rejection and restart under both strictness settings. Enabling/removing mode separately creates/clears results for both existing Versions.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionid` Attribute

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

review.note: Meta exposes defaultversionid at initial creation and after select, clear, nonsticky, full replacement and freeze transitions; the required pointer survives restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionid` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be the `versionid` of the default Version of the Resource.

review.note: For all six pointer transitions, Meta defaultversionid matches the Resource's projected Version identity/name and exactly one Version's computed isdefault state before and after restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionid` Attribute

requirements.text: - A non-`null` value MUST set `defaultversionsticky` to `true`.

review.note: PATCH with only a non-null older defaultversionid implicitly sets sticky true; the selection remains unchanged when a newer Version is added or an unrelated Version removed.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionid` Attribute

requirements.text: - A `null` value MUST set `defaultversionsticky` to `false`.

review.note: PATCH with defaultversionid null and sticky omitted clears an established sticky selection, chooses newest semver and remains automatic after newer publication.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionid` Attribute

requirements.text: At the end of an update operation, this attribute MUST be set according to the [`versionmode`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringversionmode) value of the Resource in any of the following situations:

review.note: Semver default selection is checked for nonsticky output, full Meta replacement with sticky true and omitted ID, and PATCH false-to-true sticky with null ID. Sticky-only PATCH retains the prior default. All branches persist across restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionid` Attribute

requirements.text: Regardless of the reason for `defaultversionid` or `defaultversionsticky` being modified, those changes alone MUST NOT change any attributes in any Version of the Resource. For example, attributes such as `modifiedat` and `epoch` of the previous or current default Version remain unchanged. However, the Resource's `meta` sub-object's `modifiedat` and `epoch` attributes MUST be updated.

review.note: Six pointer-only transitions preserve every Version attribute except the computed isdefault projection; Meta epoch increments exactly once, modifiedat uses an advanced clock and createdat remains unchanged. Exact Version snapshots and pointers survive restart; each operation emits only a Resource update.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionid` Attribute

requirements.text: For clarity, when processing a request that results in `defaultversionsticky` being `false`, then any existing `defaultversionid` value, or value specified in the request, MUST be ignored for the purpose of setting its final value.

review.note: An explicit old defaultversionid with sticky false is not selected; output uses newest semver. Null-pointer clearing and later publication independently verify automatic selection.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionid` Attribute

requirements.text: Any attempt to set `defaultversionid` to a non-existing Version, after all Version processing for the current operation is completed, MUST generate an error ([unknown_id](#unknown_id)).

review.note: PATCH and full Meta replacement reject unknown_id for missing and wrong-case target IDs. Exact Meta/Version state and event count remain unchanged through rejection and restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionurl` Attribute

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

review.note: API Meta exposes the exact default URL for document-bearing and documentless Resources before and after publication, read-only input attempts and persisted restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionurl` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be an absolute URL to the default Version of the Resource, and MUST be the same as that Version's `self` attribute.

review.note: API Meta URLs equal the selected Version metadata self for document-bearing and documentless Resources, including URI-escaped IDs, newer publication and persisted restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionurl` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a read-only attribute.

review.note: Meta PATCH and replacement cannot override the computed default URL with null, an object or a forged URL. The authoritative URL remains equal to Version self after restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionurl` Attribute

requirements.text: - If the Resource type's [`hasdocument` aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument) is set to `true`, then this URL MUST reference the xRegistry metadata view of the Version, not the domain-specific document view. In the HTTP protocol case, this means using the `$details` suffix.

review.note: Document-bearing default URLs include $details and equal metadata self; documentless URLs omit the suffix. Both retain the correct metadata target after newer publication and restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionurl` Attribute

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

review.note: Both full document export and document view with only Meta inlined expose the required default URL for document-bearing and documentless Resources after restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionurl` Attribute

requirements.text: - If the default Version is inlined in the document, then this attribute MUST be a relative URL of the form `#JSON-POINTER` where the `JSON-POINTER` locates the default Version within the current document. See [Doc Flag](#doc-flag) for more information.

review.note: Full export uses a relative JSON Pointer to the exact inlined default Version. The legal ID v~:@ proves tilde escaping separately from API URI escaping for both Resource document settings.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionurl` Attribute

requirements.text: - If the default Version is not inlined in the document, then this attribute MUST be an absolute URL per the API view constraints listed above.

review.note: Document view with only Meta inlined has no Versions collection and retains the absolute default metadata URL, including $details only for document-bearing Resources.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionsticky` Attribute

requirements.text: - Description: A value of `true` means that `defaultversionid` has been explicitly set and its value MUST NOT automatically change if other Versions are added or removed. A value of `false` means the default Version MUST be the newest Version, as defined by the Resource's [`versionmode`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringversionmode) algorithm.

review.note: Sticky selections remain fixed after newer publication and unrelated Version deletion; nonsticky selections follow newest semver. Existing deletion-of-default control clears sticky and selects newest remaining Version.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionsticky` Attribute

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

review.note: Meta always exposes the sticky Boolean at initial publication and after every pointer transition, including after persisted restart and null clearing.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionsticky` Attribute

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.

review.note: Creating two semver Versions with no sticky input yields false and selects the newest. Subsequent branches independently establish and clear sticky without changing this default policy.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionsticky` Attribute

requirements.text: - When specified, it MUST be a case-sensitive `true` or `false`.

review.note: PATCH and Meta replacement accept JSON true and false, clear sticky through null, and reject quoted Boolean spellings, numbers, objects and arrays with invalid_attribute. Rejection preserves exact Meta/Version state and event count; accepted values survive restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionsticky` Attribute

requirements.text: - When specified in a request, a value of `null` MUST be interpreted as a request to delete the attribute, implicitly setting it to `false`.

review.note: Null sticky input clears an established sticky value, restores false and selects newest semver; resulting Meta state survives restart for all six transition origins.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionsticky` Attribute

requirements.text: - When a Resource type's `maxversions` is set to `1`, any attempt to set this attribute to `true` MUST generate an error ([setdefaultversionsticky_false](#setdefaultversionsticky_false)) since setting a default/sticky Version is unnecessary when there can only be one Version.

review.note: One-Version Resources reject explicit sticky true through PATCH and Meta replacement and implicit sticky selection through PATCH. Exact Meta/Version state and events survive rejection and restart; subsequent publication replaces the sole Version, retains automatic selection and repairs ancestry.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionsticky` Attribute

requirements.text: If a Resource type definition wishes to turn off the ability for clients to select the "default" Version (or to set the `defaultversionsticky` attribute to `true`), this MAY be done by modifying the definition of this attribute in the Resource type's model. For example, in the `metaattributes` section use the following definition:

review.note: The declared false-only enum/default keeps newest semver selection and rejects explicit true through PATCH and Meta replacement, including implicit true from pointer PATCH. Exact Meta/Version collection and event count remain unchanged through rejection and restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Meta Entity / `defaultversionsticky` Attribute

requirements.text: Likewise, forcing all Resource instances to have "sticky" Versions MAY be achieved via the same mechanism by using `true` instead of `false` in the `enum` and `default` aspects.

review.note: Resource creation and Meta completion honor the declared true default instead of injecting false. Later publication preserves the selected Version; opposite Boolean input rejects atomically. PATCH preserves the pointer, while Meta replacement without a pointer freezes the newest Version. Both states survive restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity

requirements.text: When a Version is serialized as xRegistry metadata it MUST adhere to the following:

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity

requirements.text: - [`<RESOURCE>id`](#singularid-id-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views. OPTIONAL in requests. MUST be the `<RESOURCE>id` of the owning Resource.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity

requirements.text: - [`versionid`](#versionid-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views. OPTIONAL in requests.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity

requirements.text: - [`self`](#self-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views. OPTIONAL/ignored in requests. MUST be a URL to this Version, not the owning Resource.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity

requirements.text: - [`shortself`](#shortself-attribute) - OPTIONAL in API and document view, based on the `shortself` capability. OPTIONAL/ignored in requests.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity

requirements.text: - [`xid`](#xid-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views. OPTIONAL/ignored in requests. MUST be the `xid` of this Version, not the owning Resource.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity

requirements.text: - [`epoch`](#epoch-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views. OPTIONAL in requests. MUST be the `epoch` value of this Version, not the owning Resource.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity

requirements.text: - [`name`](#name-attribute) - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity

requirements.text: - [`description`](#description-attribute) - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity

requirements.text: - [`documentation`](#documentation-attribute) - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity

requirements.text: - [`icon`](#icon-attribute) - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity

requirements.text: - [`labels`](#labels-attribute) - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity

requirements.text: - [`createdat`](#createdat-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views. OPTIONAL in requests.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity

requirements.text: - [`modifiedat`](#modifiedat-attribute) - REQUIRED in API and document views. OPTIONAL in requests.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `versionid` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be `<SINGULAR>id` of the Version.

review.note: Explicit Version routes expose exact Root and Child Version identities with the owning noteid. API and document export preserve those identities after accepted matching updates, ignored membership input and restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `versionid` Attribute

requirements.text: - REQUIRED in API and document views.

review.note: Selected and nonselected Versions expose their exact versionid in API responses and full document export after metadata replacement, ignored membership inputs and persisted restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `versionid` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST NOT use a value of `null` or `request` due to these being reserved for use by the [SetDefaultVersionID Flag](#setdefaultversionid-flag).

review.note: Both reserved spellings reject malformed_id on explicit Version replacement, Resource POST, Version collection PATCH and new Resource replacement. Full export and events remain unchanged through restart; differently cased Null and Request are accepted exact identities.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `versionid` Attribute

requirements.text: - If present in a request operation's serialization of a Resource's default Version attributes, then it MUST match the Resource's current `meta.defaultversionid` value (if defined), otherwise an error ([mismatched_id](./spec.md#mismatched_id)) MUST be generated.

review.note: Resource PATCH and replacement reject an older, wrong-case or missing Version ID with mismatched_id. Full exported state and event count survive rejection and restart; the exact current Child ID accepts the intended metadata update.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `isdefault` Attribute

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

review.note: Both selected and nonselected Versions always expose a Boolean membership value in API metadata and document export, regardless of submitted read-only values; output survives restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `isdefault` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a [read-only](#read-only-changed) attribute.

review.note: PATCH and replacement ignore supplied isdefault true, false, null, quoted Boolean, object and number inputs on both selected and nonselected Versions. Actual Meta selection controls membership in API and document export after restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `isdefault` Attribute

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `isdefault` Attribute

requirements.text: - When specified, MUST be either `true` or `false`, case-sensitive.

review.note: Authoritative isdefault output is a JSON Boolean for both membership states in API and document views. Read-only client input is ignored rather than subjected to mutable-value admission, including quoted and non-Boolean values.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `ancestorid` Attribute

requirements.text: The `ancestorid` attribute MUST be set to the case-sensitive `versionid` of this Version's ancestor. If this Version is a root of an ancestor hierarchy tree then it MUST be set to its own `versionid` value.

review.note: Server-assigned and explicit roots use their own exact Version identity. Child points to Root; lowercase root does not resolve that distinct identity. Root and child relationships persist across restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `ancestorid` Attribute

requirements.text: If a create operation asks the server to choose the `versionid` when creating a root Version, the `versionid` is not yet known and therefore cannot be specified in the `ancestorid` attribute as part of the request. In those cases a value of `request` MUST be used as a way to reference itself.

review.note: Creating a Resource without a chosen versionid and with ancestorid=request assigns a non-empty Version identity, replaces request with that same identity, and persists the self-root relationship across restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `ancestorid` Attribute

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

review.note: Assigned roots and explicitly linked child Versions expose ancestorid; reparented and deletion-repaired roots retain the required field across restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `ancestorid` Attribute

requirements.text: - The `ancestorid` attribute MUST NOT be set to a value that creates circular references between Versions and it is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED that the server generate an error ([ancestor_circular_reference](#ancestor_circular_reference)) if a request attempts to do so. For example, an operation that makes Version A's ancestor B, and Version B's ancestor A, would generate an error.

review.note: Root-to-child back edge rejects ancestor_circular_reference and preserves exact Version collection metadata and event count. Existing multiple-root controls remain separate.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `ancestorid` Attribute

requirements.text: - When absent in an update operation request, it MUST be interpreted as the same as if it were present with its existing value.

review.note: PATCH and full Version replacement omit ancestorid while changing name; both retain the exact existing Root relationship, including after persisted restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `ancestorid` Attribute

requirements.text: - Any attempt to set an `ancestorid` attribute to a non-existing `versionid` MUST generate an error ([unknown_id](#unknown_id)).

review.note: Missing ancestor and wrong-case spelling of an existing Root both reject unknown_id without changing Version collection metadata or events.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `ancestorid` Attribute

requirements.text: - Any modification to the `ancestorid` attribute MUST result in the owning Version's `epoch` and `modifiedat` attributes be updated appropriately, regardless of whether the change to `ancestorid` was explicitly part of a request or indirectly changed due to changes to other Versions.

review.note: Explicit reparenting to self and indirect repair after ancestor deletion each increment Child epoch exactly once and set modifiedat to the advanced deterministic clock while preserving createdat. Exact resulting metadata persists across restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `contenttype` Attribute

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `contenttype` Attribute

requirements.text: - SHOULD be compliant with [RFC9110](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#media.type).

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `contenttype` Attribute

requirements.text: - This attribute MAY be specified even for Versions that use the `<RESOURCE>url` attribute. While this specification cannot guarantee that this attribute's value will match the media type value returned by a request to retrieve the document at the `<RESOURCE>url`, it is expected that they will match.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `format` Attribute

requirements.text: - Description: Identifies what the Version represents. For example, in the case of a Schema Registry, this value would identify the schema format of the Version's domain-specific document. However, it MAY also be used to identify the xRegistry metadata definitions/values for the Version. For example, it could be used to indicate that the Versions are [Message definitions](../message/spec.md).

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `format` Attribute

requirements.text: Managers of the xRegistry instance MAY enforce validation of the data within the Registry by modifying the model to make this a mandatory attribute or by defining a default value.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `format` Attribute

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `format` Attribute

requirements.text: - If present, MUST be a non-empty case-insensitive string.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `format` Attribute

requirements.text: - SHOULD follow the naming convention `<NAME>/<VERSION>`, whereby `<NAME>` is the name of the format and `<VERSION>` is the version of the format used by this Version.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `format` Attribute

requirements.text: - RECOMMENDED that the same `<NAME>` be used for all Versions of a Resource.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `format` Attribute

requirements.text: - When not present, `format` validation MUST NOT be performed for that Version irrespective of the [`validateformat`](model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringvalidateformat) attribute's value.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `formatvalidated` Attribute

requirements.text: A value of `true` indicates that the server has validated the Version and it adheres to the `format` attribute's rules. When `true` the Version's [`formatvalidatedreason`](#formatvalidatedreason-attribute) MUST NOT be present.

review.note: Successful syntax checks omit format reasons. Local-to-external-to-local reversal removes prior unchecked reasons and restores true flags without acquiring external bytes.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `formatvalidated` Attribute

requirements.text: When [`strictvalidation`](model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringstrictvalidation)` is `true`, the above conditions MUST generate an error ([format_unknown](#format_unknown) or [format_external](#format_external)) and reject the update request instead.

review.note: Strict unsupported-format publication rejects format_unknown with no Group or event. Strict external publication and local-to-external replacement reject format_external and retain previously valid local bytes.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `formatvalidated` Attribute

requirements.text: When `false`, the [`formatvalidatedreason`](#formatvalidatedreason-attribute) MUST be present with an explanation as to why the server was unable to perform validation of the Version. Additionally, when `false`, if `compatibility` validation is enabled, the Version's [`compatibilityvalidated`](#compatibility-attribute) attribute MUST also be `false`.

review.note: Non-strict unsupported formats with a compatibility mode produce false format and compatibility flags with non-empty reasons. External publication and replacement prove the same coupled unchecked state.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `formatvalidated` Attribute

requirements.text: Note that `"false"` MUST NOT be used for validation failure. In those cases the write operation MUST generate an error ([format_violation](#format_violation)) and reject the request regardless of the value of the [`strictvalidation`](model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringstrictvalidation)` model aspect.

review.note: Invalid syntax rejects creation and replacement with format_violation under both strictness settings. Failed creation leaves no Group/event; failed replacement preserves valid bytes, true flag, absent reason, epoch and event count.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `formatvalidated` Attribute

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `formatvalidated` Attribute

requirements.text: - When specified, MUST be either `true` or `false`, case-sensitive.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `formatvalidated` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a [read-only](#read-only-changed) attribute.

review.note: Default-Resource and exact-Version creation/PATCH ignore forged validation flags, including null, invalid types and opposite outcomes. Valid, unsupported and absent-format cases retain authoritative results and exact bytes after restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `formatvalidated` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be present if the Resource model's `validateformat` attribute is `true` and the Version's `format` attribute is present.

review.note: Enabled format validation with a declared format produces true flags for supported syntax and false flags for unchecked unsupported or external Documents.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `formatvalidated` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST NOT be present if the Resource model's `validateformat` attribute is `false` or the Version's `format` attribute is absent.

review.note: False or omitted format validation leaves flags absent despite recognized format and otherwise invalid bytes. Independently absent format skips all checks even with compatibility mode present; removal clears prior results under both strictness settings.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `formatvalidatedreason` Attribute

requirements.text: - Description: When [`formatvalidated`](#formatvalidated-attribute) has a value of `false`, this attribute MUST provide information as to why the format validation check was not performed.

review.note: Unchecked unsupported syntax reports format.unsupported; unresolved explicit references report reference.unresolved without automatic acquisition. External Documents also retain a non-empty explanation.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `formatvalidatedreason` Attribute

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `formatvalidatedreason` Attribute

requirements.text: - When specified, MUST be a non-empty string.

review.note: Unsupported-format diagnostics are retrieved as strings containing format.unsupported. External unchecked results separately require non-empty string reasons.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `formatvalidatedreason` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a [read-only](#read-only-changed) attribute.

review.note: Forged format-validation reasons at creation and PATCH cannot replace server explanations or survive when the flag is true or absent. Both default-Resource and exact-Version paths retain the authoritative reason state across restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `formatvalidatedreason` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be present when [`formatvalidated`](#formatvalidated-attribute) is present with a value of `false`.

review.note: Unsupported and external Documents with false format flags require their format reasons at publication and local-to-external replacement.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `formatvalidatedreason` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST NOT be present when [`formatvalidated`](#formatvalidated-attribute) is absent or has a value of `true`.

review.note: Successful syntax checks omit reasons; disabled/omitted format validation and independently absent format omit both flag and reason. External-to-local reversal clears old unchecked reasons.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `compatibilityvalidated` Attribute

requirements.text: When [`strictvalidation`](model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringstrictvalidation)` is `true`, the above conditions MUST generate an error ([format_unknown](#format_unknown), [compatibility_unknown](#compatibility_unknown) or [format_external](#format_external)) and reject the update request instead.

review.note: With compatibility enabled and mode present, strict unsupported format rejects format_unknown, unsupported selected mode rejects compatibility_unknown, and external Document rejects format_external. Rejected mutations retain prior state and bytes.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `compatibilityvalidated` Attribute

requirements.text: When `false`, the [`compatibilityvalidatedreason`](#compatibilityvalidatedreason-attribute) MUST be present with an explanation as to why the server was unable to perform validation of the Version.

review.note: Unchecked compatibility flags retain non-empty reasons for unsupported format, unsupported selected mode and external Document. Changed non-Avro schema bytes identify compatibility.policy rather than claiming a violation.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `compatibilityvalidated` Attribute

requirements.text: Note that `false` MUST NOT be used for validation failure. In those cases the write operation MUST generate an error ([compatibility_violation](#compatibility_violation)) and reject the request regardless of the value of the [`strictvalidation`](model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringstrictvalidation)` model aspect.

review.note: Proven Avro incompatibility rejects new Versions, candidate/ancestor replacements, lineage reparenting and policy reversal with compatibility_violation under both strictness settings. Existing policy, Version metadata/count, exact bytes, true validation flags, absent reasons and event count survive rejection and restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `compatibilityvalidated` Attribute

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `compatibilityvalidated` Attribute

requirements.text: - When specified, MUST be either `true` or `false`, case-sensitive.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `compatibilityvalidated` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a [read-only](#read-only-changed) attribute.

review.note: Forged compatibility flags cannot certify unchecked Versions, erase successful results or create a flag without required format/mode. Creation and PATCH through default-Resource and exact-Version surfaces preserve server outcomes and exact bytes after restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `compatibilityvalidated` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be present if the Resource model's `validatecompatibility` attribute is `true`, the Version's `format` value is present, and the Resource's `meta.compatibility` attribute is present.

review.note: Enabled compatibility with both format and mode produces true flags for checked ancestry and false flags for unsupported selected mode. Adding a mode creates results for both existing Versions.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `compatibilityvalidated` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST NOT be present if the Resource model's `validatecompatibility` attribute is `false`, or the Version's `format` value is absent, or the Resource's `meta.compatibility` attribute is absent.

review.note: False/omitted compatibility validation, independently absent format with mode retained, and independently absent mode with format retained each omit compatibility flags. Removing a mode clears results for both Versions under both strictness settings.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `compatibilityvalidatedreason` Attribute

requirements.text: - Description: When [`compatibilityvalidated`](#compatibilityvalidated-attribute) has a value of `false`, this attribute MUST provide information as to why the compatibility validation check was not performed.

review.note: Changed non-Avro syntax identifies compatibility.policy and unqualified ancestry depth identifies limit.history. Selected unsupported modes and external Documents separately require non-empty compatibility explanations.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `compatibilityvalidatedreason` Attribute

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `compatibilityvalidatedreason` Attribute

requirements.text: - When specified, MUST be a non-empty string.

review.note: Selected unsupported mode and external Documents require non-empty string reasons. Conservative changed-schema compatibility also supplies a string containing compatibility.policy.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `compatibilityvalidatedreason` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a [read-only](#read-only-changed) attribute.

review.note: Forged compatibility reasons at creation and PATCH cannot replace server explanations or survive when the flag is true or absent. Both default-Resource and exact-Version paths retain authoritative values through restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `compatibilityvalidatedreason` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be present when [`compatibilityvalidated`](#compatibilityvalidated-attribute) is present with a value of `false`.

review.note: False compatibility flags require reasons for unsupported format, unsupported selected mode and external Document; no unchecked outcome is returned without an explanation.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `compatibilityvalidatedreason` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST NOT be present when [`compatibilityvalidated`](#compatibilityvalidated-attribute) is absent or has a value of `true`.

review.note: Successful ancestry checks omit compatibility reasons. Disabled/omitted compatibility, absent format and absent/removed mode omit reasons with their flags; external-to-local reversal removes earlier unchecked reasons.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>url` Attribute

requirements.text: - Description: If the Version's domain-specific document is stored outside of the current Registry, then this attribute MUST contain a URL to the location where it can be retrieved. If the value of this attribute is a well-known identifier that is readily understood by Registry clients, and resolves to a common representation of the Version, or an item in some private store/cache, rather than a networked document location, then it is RECOMMENDED for the value to be a uniform resource name ([URN](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8141)).

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>url` Attribute

requirements.text: - REQUIRED if the Version's document is not stored inside of the current Registry.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>url` Attribute

requirements.text: - If the document is stored in a network-accessible endpoint then the referenced URL MUST support a query to this URL to retrieve the contents. There is no requirement for the server to validate this URL.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>url` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST NOT be present if the Resource type's [`hasdocument` aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument) is set to `false`.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>` Attribute

requirements.text: - Description: This attribute is a serialization of the corresponding Version's domain-specific document's contents. If the document's bytes "as is" (without any additional processing such as escaping) allows for them to appear as the value of this JSON attribute, then this attribute MUST be used if the request asked for the document to be [inlined](#inline-flag) in the response.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>` Attribute

requirements.text: The model Resource attribute [`typemap`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringtypemap) MAY be used to help the server determine if the document is in the same format. If a Version has a matching `contenttype` attribute but the contents of the Version's document do not successfully parse (e.g. it's `application/json` but the JSON is invalid), then `<RESOURCE>` MUST NOT be used and `<RESOURCE>base64` MUST be used instead.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>` Attribute

requirements.text: - If the Version's document is to be serialized and is not empty, then either `<RESOURCE>` or `<RESOURCE>base64` MUST be present.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST only be used if the Version's document (bytes) is in the same format as the serialization of the Version entity.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST NOT be present if `<RESOURCE>base64` is also present.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST NOT be present if the Resource type's [`hasdocument` aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument) is set to `false`.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>base64` Attribute

requirements.text: - Description: This attribute is a base64 encoding of the corresponding Version's domain-specific document. If the Version's document (which is stored as an array of bytes) is not conformant with the format being used to serialize the Version (e.g. as a JSON value), then this attribute MUST be used instead of the `<RESOURCE>` attribute.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>base64` Attribute

requirements.text: - If the Version's document is to be serialized and it is not empty, then either `<RESOURCE>` or `<RESOURCE>base64` MUST be present.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>base64` Attribute

requirements.text: - If the Version's document is to be serialized but it is empty, then `<RESOURCE>base64` MUST be present with an empty string (`""`) value.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>base64` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST be a base64 encoded string of the Version's document.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>base64` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST NOT be present if `<RESOURCE>` is also present.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>base64` Attribute

requirements.text: - MUST NOT be present if the Resource type's [`hasdocument` aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument) is set to `false`.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>base64` Attribute

requirements.text: When accessing a Version's xRegistry metadata, often it is to view or update the xRegistry metadata and not the document, as such, including the potentially large amount of data from the Version's document in request and response messages could be cumbersome. To address this, the `<RESOURCE>` and `<RESOURCE>base64` attributes do not appear by default as part of the serialization of the Version. Rather, they MUST only appear in responses when the [Inline Flag](#inline-flag), with a value of `<RESOURCE>`, is used. Likewise, in requests, these attributes are OPTIONAL and would only need to be used when a change to the document's content is needed at the same time as updates to the Version's metadata. However, the `<RESOURCE>url` attribute MUST always appear if it has a value, just like any other attribute.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>base64` Attribute

requirements.text: Note that the serialization of a Version MUST only use at most one of these 3 attributes at a time.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / `<RESOURCE>base64` Attribute

requirements.text: Client and server implementations MUST be prepared for any of these 3 attributes to be used. In the case of `<RESOURCE>` or `<RESOURCE>base64`, implementations can not assume that a previous use of one means that all subsequent interactions with that entity will use the same attribute. For example, a client can use `<RESOURCE>` to populate the value, but the server is free to use `<RESOURCE>base64` when returning the data.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / Version IDs

requirements.text: If a server does not support client-side specification of the `versionid` of a new Version (see the [`setversionid` aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringsetversionid) in the [Registry Model](./model.md#registry-model)), or if a client chooses to not specify the `versionid`, then the server MUST assign new Versions a `versionid` that is unique within the scope of its owning Resource.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / Version IDs

requirements.text: Servers MAY have their own algorithm for the creation of new Version `versionid` values, but the default algorithm is as follows:

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / Version IDs

requirements.text: - `versionid` MUST be a string serialization of a monotonically increasing (by `1`) unsigned integer starting with `1` and is scoped to the owning Resource.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / Version IDs

requirements.text: - Each time a new `versionid` is needed, if an existing Version already has that `versionid` then the server MUST generate the next `versionid` value and try again.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / Version IDs

requirements.text: - The search for the next value does not restart with `1` each time, it MUST continue from the highest previously generated value.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / Version IDs

requirements.text: With this default versioning algorithm, when semantic versioning is needed, it is RECOMMENDED to include a major version identifier in the Resource `<RESOURCE>id`, like `"com.example.event.v1"` or `"com.example.event.2024-02"`, so that incompatible, but historically related Resources can be more easily identified by users and developers. The Version's `versionid` then functions as the semantic minor version identifier.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / Default Version of a Resource

requirements.text: 1. Default = Newest. The newest Version (based on the Resource's [`versionmode`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringversionmode) algorithm) MUST become the "default" Version. This is the default choice.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / Default Version of a Resource

requirements.text: 1. Client explicitly chooses the "default". In this option, a client has explicitly chosen which Version is the "default" and it MUST NOT change until a client chooses another Version - this is referred to as the default Version being "sticky". When the current default Version is deleted and the client did not specify which Version is to become the next default Version (see below), then the server MUST revert back to option 1 (default = newest).

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Version Entity / Default Version of a Resource

requirements.text: A client MAY choose the "default" Version two ways:

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Deleting Entities

requirements.text: When deleting multiple entities, the list of entities to delete MUST be specified as a map. There will be 3 possible ways in which the map will be serialized:

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Deleting Entities

requirements.text: Since each entity has an `epoch` value associated with it, the server MUST perform `epoch` value checking and reject the entire request if any fail. This is similar to what an "update" operation would look like.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Deleting Entities

requirements.text: Since a Resource's `epoch` value is part of its `meta` entity, and not a top-level Resource attribute, for consistency with what the retrieval of a Resource would look like, the `epoch` value in this case MUST appear under a `meta` entity within the Resource. And then normal `epoch` value checking rules would apply.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Deleting Entities

requirements.text: If an `epoch` value only appears at the top-level (and not within `meta`) then an error ([misplaced_epoch](./spec.md#misplaced_epoch)) MUST be generated. If `epoch` appears in both places then the top-level one MUST be silently ignored.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Deleting Entities

requirements.text: - A map with no entities MUST NOT delete any entities.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Deleting Entities

requirements.text: - Each key of the map MUST be the `<SINGULAR>id` of the entity to be deleted.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Deleting Entities

requirements.text: - If the request body is absent (does not include a map), then all entities in the collection MUST be deleted.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Deleting Entities

requirements.text: - If the entity's `<SINGULAR>id` is present in the request, then it MUST match its corresponding `<KEY>` value, otherwise a [mismatched_id](#mismatched_id) MUST be generated.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Deleting Entities

requirements.text: - Any other entity attributes that appear in the request MUST be silently ignored, even if their values are invalid.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Deleting Entities

requirements.text: - If one of the referenced entities cannot be found, then the server MUST silently ignore this condition and not treat it as an error.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Deleting Entities

requirements.text: - If the entity cannot be found, then an error ([not_found](./spec.md#not_found)) MUST be generated.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Deleting Entities

requirements.text: - Deleting an entity MUST delete all children entities as well.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / Deleting Entities

requirements.text: - Any error MUST result in the entire request being rejected.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags

requirements.text: Implementations of this specification SHOULD support all specification-defined flags.

review.note: The Server advertises the complete Core flag set when capabilities requests all flags; focused behavior tests cover each supported flag.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Binary Flag

requirements.text: The `binary` flag MAY be used on requests to indicate that the server MUST use the `<RESOURCE>base64` attribute instead of the `<RESOURCE>` attribute when serializing any Resource's domain-specific document in the response message. Note, the presence of this flag does not change when the document is inlined, just how it is serialized if it is inlined.

review.note: The server emits the document as base64 rather than the domain-specific JSON attribute for both Resource and Version document views while preserving inlining.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Binary Flag

requirements.text: This flag MAY be used on any request but will only influence the serialization of Resource and Version entities that have a domain-specific document.

review.note: The flag is accepted on a Group read without changing its representation and changes document encoding only for inlined Resource and Version entities.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Collections Flag

requirements.text: The `collections` flag MAY be used on requests directed to the Registry itself, or to Group instances, to indicate that the response message MUST NOT include any attributes from the top-level entity (Registry or Group), but instead MUST include only all of the nested xRegistry Collection maps that are defined at that level. Specifying it on a request directed to some other part of the Registry MUST generate an error ([bad_flag](#bad_flag)). Use of this flag MUST implicitly turn on [inlining](#inline-flag) within a value of `*`.

review.note: The flag is restricted to Registry and Group targets, projects only nested collection maps, and recursively inlines their descendants; other targets return bad_flag.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Collections Flag

requirements.text: Servers MAY choose to include, or exclude, the sibling `<COLLECTION>url` and `<COLLECTION>count` attributes for those top-level collections.

review.note: The Server omits sibling collection URL/count attributes in collections-only output, an allowed choice; tests assert only collection maps remain at each requested level.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Doc Flag

requirements.text: The `doc` flag MAY be used to indicate that the response MUST use "document view" when serializing entities and MUST be modified to do the following:

review.note: The document-view projection is exercised across response roots, Resource/Version serialization, validation-field removal, cross-reference exclusion, and relative-versus-absolute link behavior; the detailed clauses are mapped separately.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Doc Flag

requirements.text: - MUST remove the default Version attributes from a Resource's serialization.

review.note: The document Resource is built without the inherited default-Version projection; direct assertions cover inherited name/version identity and document content while the selected Version remains separately inlined.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Doc Flag

requirements.text: - MUST remove the Version `formatvalidated` and `compatibilityvalidated` attributes from Version serializations.

review.note: A validating Version retains both validation booleans and their reasons in API view; document view removes all four fields without changing the underlying API representation.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Doc Flag

requirements.text: - MUST remove the `shortself` attribute from all entity serializations.

review.note: ShortSelf tests cover Resource, Meta and Version entity planes, verify document view removes the attribute, and preserve opaque domain-document fields and API behavior.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Doc Flag

requirements.text: - When a Resource (source) uses the `xref` feature, the target Resource's attributes MUST be excluded from the source's serialization.

review.note: Document aliases remain source-local: output preserves local identity and xref but excludes target metadata, default-Version projection, and Versions.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Doc Flag

requirements.text: - Resources and Versions MUST be serialized in their [xRegistry metadata view](#resource-metadata-vs-resource-document) and not as any potential domain-specific document.

review.note: Document view returns xRegistry Resource/Version metadata, keeps raw document bytes out of the metadata projection, and includes domain content only when the corresponding Version is explicitly inlined.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Doc Flag

requirements.text: - MUST convert the following attributes into relative URLs if, and only if, the entities that they reference are included in the response output: `self`, `<COLLECTION>url`, `metaurl`, `defaultversionurl`.

review.note: Server and bridge tests cover included and excluded targets for collection URLs, metaurl and defaultversionurl, plus response-local self links; included targets become JSON Pointers and excluded targets retain absolute URLs.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Doc Flag

requirements.text: All of the relative URLs mentioned in the last bullet above MUST begin with `#` and be followed by a [JSON Pointer](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6901) reference to the entity within the response, e.g. `#/endpoints/e1`. This means that they are relative to the root of the document (response) generated, and not necessarily relative to the root of the Registry. Additionally, when those URLs are relative and reference a Resource or Version, any protocol-specific modifications to the URLs (e.g. the HTTP `$details` suffix) MUST NOT be present despite the semantics of the suffix being applied (as noted below).

review.note: Generated pointers use the response root, escape JSON Pointer tokens, omit protocol-specific details suffixes, and encode the empty root pointer as `#`.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Doc Flag

requirements.text: When a relative URL references the root of the response, it MUST be `#`, which represents an empty JSON Pointer selecting the whole document, not `#/`, which selects an object member with an empty name.

review.note: The empty JSON Pointer is `#`; `#/` denotes a different target. Verified root self links for Registry, Group, Resource, Meta, Version, and alias document views against the pinned wording.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Doc Flag

requirements.text: For clarity, the serialization of a Resource (when using `?inline=meta`) in document view MUST adhere to the following:

review.note: The Server document-view serializer keeps Resource identity at the response root, places metadata under meta, uses relative pointers only for inlined targets, and excludes target-owned metadata from a cross-reference Resource's meta view.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Doc Flag

requirements.text: Note that the `meta` entity's attributes `epoch` through `defaultversionsticky` MUST be excluded if `xref` is set because those would appear as part of the target Resource's `meta` entity. Also notice the default Version's attributes do not appear.

review.note: Document alias Meta includes source identity and xref but omits target-owned metadata and default-Version attributes.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Doc Flag

requirements.text: If this flag is used on a request directed to a Resource's `versions` collection, or to one of its Versions, but the Resource is defined as an `xref` to another Resource, then the server MUST generate an error ([cannot_doc_xref](#cannot_doc_xref)) and SHOULD indicate that using this flag on this part of the hierarchy is not valid - due to those entities not technically existing in document view.

review.note: Document view rejects an alias Versions request with the Core `cannot_doc_xref` error instead of traversing a target hierarchy absent from the source document.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Epoch Flag

requirements.text: The `epoch` flag MAY be used on any delete operation directed to a single entity if the protocol being used doesn't normally include the serialization of the "to be deleted" entity in the request. In those cases, this flag is used to request that the entity's current `epoch` value matches this flag's value for the purpose of the server's [`epoch` conflict checking algorithm](#epoch-attribute).

review.note: The Server accepts an epoch query flag for single Group, Resource, and Version deletions, checks the current value for mismatches, and rejects non-delete, collection, and null-value uses.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: The `filter` flag MAY be used to indicate that the response MUST include only those entities that match the specified filter criteria expressions. This means that any Registry Collection's `<COLLECTION>*` attributes will be modified to match the resulting subset. In particular:

review.note: Exact result IDs, filtered collection maps, AND intersections, and repeated-filter unions are asserted against the query result.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - If the collection is inlined, it MUST only include entities that match the filter expression(s).

review.note: A filtered request omits unrequested inline data; when inline is requested, assertions restrict collections to selected leaves and include descendants of matching parents.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - The collection `url` attribute MAY include the appropriate filter expression(s) such that a query to that URL would return the same subset of entities, if the protocol supports including the filter flag value as part of the URL.

review.note: The collection URL preserves the selected subset and is followed from root and Group-relative filtered requests; empty selections use excludeall.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - The collection `count` attribute MUST only count the entities that match the filter expression(s).

review.note: Root and nested collection counts are asserted against the exact filtered members, including an empty result.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - For expressions that are AND'd together, only entities that satisfy both expressions MUST be returned.

review.note: Comma-separated predicates intersect on the same entity or matching subtree; tests reject matches witnessed only by different sibling Resources.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - For expressions that are OR'd together, only entities that satisfy either expression MUST be returned.

review.note: Repeated filter values form a union, and assertions verify matching parents retain descendants while the child collection remains filtered.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - `<PATH>` MUST be an [xRegistry dot (`.`) notation](#xregistry-dot--notation) traversal of the Registry to the entity of interest, or absent if at the top of the Registry request.

review.note: Nested filters traverse dot-notation paths through collections, objects, maps, and arrays; IDs are omitted from data paths.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - The `<PATH>` value MUST be based on the requesting URL and not the root of the Registry. Meaning, if the URL targets a Group then the `<PATH>` value would be relative to the Group and not the root of the Registry. See the examples below.

review.note: The Group request filters its child collection with `items.itemid=x`; the emitted URL is followed and returns that same child.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - `<ATTRIBUTE>` MUST be the attribute in the entity to be examined.

review.note: Filters name model attributes and nested attributes explicitly; invalid literals and unsupported attribute paths produce bad_filter.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - A non-`null` `<VALUE>` MUST only be used when referencing scalar attributes.

review.note: A non-null comparison against an object value is rejected as bad_filter; scalar and nested scalar comparisons are exercised separately.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - A reference to a nonexistent attribute SHOULD NOT generate an error and SHOULD be treated the same as a non-matching situation. For example, a filter expression of `myobj.myattr=5` would not match if: `myobj` is missing, `myattr` is missing, or `myattr` is not `5`.

review.note: Unknown attributes return no matches without an error; nested object paths also skip entities whose parent object is absent.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - No operator: - When no operator is specified then the response MUST include all entities that have the `<ATTRIBUTE>` present with any non-`null` value.

review.note: The no-operator rank filter returns every entity with a present non-null rank and excludes the entity without one.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - `=` operator: - When `<VALUE>` is `null` then only entities without the specified `<ATTRIBUTE>` MUST be included in the response. - When a non-`null` `<VALUE>` is specified then `<VALUE>` MUST be the desired value of the attribute being examined. Only entities whose specified `<ATTRIBUTE>` with this `<VALUE>` MUST be included in the response. - When `<VALUE>` is absent then the implied `<VALUE>` is an empty string and the matching MUST be done as specified in the previous bullet.

review.note: The empty-string `description=` filter matches the entity with an empty description; explicit `null` matches entities where the attribute is absent.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - `!=`, `<>` operators: - When `<VALUE>` is `null` then it MUST have the same semantics as a filter expression of `<ATTRIBUTE>` as specified above (meaning, present with any non-`null` value). - When `<VALUE>` is non-`null` then only entities without the specified `<ATTRIBUTE>` and `<VALUE>` MUST be included in the response. This MUST be semantically equivalent to `NOT(<ATTRIBUTE>=<VALUE>)`, and this also means that if `<ATTRIBUTE>` is missing then that attribute will match the filter.

review.note: Both `!=` and `<>` include the entity with a missing rank when compared with a non-null value; their `null` form matches present non-null ranks.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` operators: - `<VALUE>` MUST NOT be `null`. - Only entities with the specified `<ATTRIBUTE>` and `<VALUE>` that matches the comparison operator's semantics MUST be included in the response. - `<` refers to "less than". - `<=` refers to "less than or equal to". - `>` refers to "greater than". - `>=` refers to "greater than or equal to".

review.note: Numeric and boolean vectors exercise all four relative operators; null comparison operands are rejected as bad_filter.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - For boolean attributes, comparisons MUST be an exact case-sensitive match (`true` or `false`). For relative comparisons, `false` is less than `true`.

review.note: Direct vectors check exact-case boolean literals, reject uppercase TRUE, and verify false is less than true.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - For numeric attributes, standard numeric comparisons rules apply. Note that numerics MUST NOT be treated as strings for comparison.

review.note: Direct numeric vectors cover >= at its boundary and distinguish values above 2^53, exponent-equivalent values, and long decimal fractions.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - The strings MUST be compared in a case-insensitive manner.

review.note: Direct string vectors match Alpha and ALPHA with the same case-insensitive equality filter.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - It is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED to use Unicode collation based on en-US.

review.note: String filter equality, relative comparison, wildcard matching, and sorting use case-insensitive en-US Unicode collation; invariant comparison is used only when the runtime disables named cultures.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: Additionally, wildcards (`*`) MAY be used in string `<VALUE>`s with the following constraints:

review.note: Direct vectors cover substring and escaped stars, empty-string existence, permitted equality and inequality operators, and rejection for relative or non-string comparisons.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - They MUST only be used when the comparison operator is `=`, `!=` or `<>`.

review.note: A relative-comparison wildcard is rejected, and both inequality operators are exercised with wildcard string values.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - The presence of a wildcard indicates that any number of characters MAY appear at that location in the `<VALUE>`.

review.note: The substring wildcard vector matches text with arbitrary characters between the literal prefix and suffix.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - The wildcard MAY be escaped via the use of a backslash (`\\`) character (e.g. `abc\*def`) to mean that the `*` is to be interpreted as a normal character and not as a wildcard.

review.note: An escaped star is matched as a literal character rather than as a wildcard.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - A `<VALUE>` of `*` MUST be equivalent to checking for the existence of the attribute, with any value (even an empty string). In other words, the filter will only fail if the attribute has no value at all.

review.note: The sole-star vector matches the explicitly present empty description and excludes entities without that attribute.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: As previously specified, when a query includes a filter expression, any nested xRegistry collections in the response SHOULD result in the specification of a `<COLLECTION>url` attribute that allows clients to easily traverse into that collection with the appropriate sub-filter expression to yield the same results as the original filter, but just for that nested collection. However, if a collection has zero entities (regardless of whether the empty list is due to the filter or due to the collection being empty), server MUST use a special filter expression, `excludeall`, to indicate no results are to be returned for that URL.

review.note: Root-relative and Group-relative nested collection URLs are followed to verify their selected members. Empty selected collections use excludeall.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: URLs with the `excludeall` filter expression MUST adhere to the following:

review.note: Direct assertions cover an empty collection result, not_found for an entity URL, and bad_filter when excludeall is combined with another filter.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - If the URL references a collection then an empty collection (`{}`) MUST be returned.

review.note: The excludeall collection request returns an empty JSON object.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: - If the URL references an entity, then an error ([not_found](#not_found)) MUST be generated.

review.note: An excludeall request to an entity is asserted to return not_found.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag
