requirements.text: - If any other filter expression appears at the same time, then an error ([bad_filter](#bad_filter)) MUST be generated.

review.note: Combining excludeall with another filter is asserted to return bad_filter.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: If the request references an entity (not a collection), and the filter expression references an attribute in that entity (i.e. there is no `<PATH>`), then if the expression does not match the entity, that entity MUST NOT be returned. In other words, a `404 Not Found` would be generated in the HTTP protocol case.

review.note: A nonmatching filter on a requested entity is asserted to return not_found.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: Invalid filter expressions MUST generate an error ([bad_filter](#bad_filter)).

review.note: Invalid literals, unsupported wildcard comparisons, and malformed paths are asserted to return bad_filter.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Filter Flag

requirements.text: Specifying a filter does not imply inlining. Inlining MAY be used at the same time but MUST NOT result in additional entities being included in the results unless they are children of a matching leaf entity.

review.note: Filtering does not imply inlining; when inline is requested, assertions restrict collections to selected leaves and include descendants of matching parents.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Ignore Flag

requirements.text: The `ignore` flag MAY be used on any write operation to indicate that certain parts of the request message MUST be ignored by the server. This flag is designed for cases where a user wants to import data into a Registry without going through the (potentially tedious) process of removing certain parts of the data in advance. Typically, in an "export->import" scenario.

review.note: Direct tests cover root import fields, nested IDs, epoch and readonly guards, default-version selection/stickiness, ignored-resource omission, repeated and wildcard forms, and unsupported or malformed values across Replace, Patch, Post, and Delete.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Ignore Flag

requirements.text: This value indicates that any `capabilities` attribute included in the request MUST be ignored.

review.note: Direct import assertions show root ID/epoch/capabilities/modelsource ignored while nested IDs remain guarded; repeated/bulk ignores preserve independent guards and do not grant new authorization. Collection targets do not strip member IDs.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Ignore Flag

requirements.text: This value indicates that any `defaultversionid` attribute included in the request MUST be ignored.

review.note: Changing defaultversionid to another existing version with ignore=defaultversionid leaves the selected default and URL unchanged.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Ignore Flag

requirements.text: This value indicates that any `defaultversionsticky` attribute included in the request MUST be ignored.

review.note: Clearing defaultversionsticky with ignore=defaultversionsticky leaves the sticky default-selection state true.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Ignore Flag

requirements.text: This value indicates that any `epoch` attribute included in the request MUST be ignored.

review.note: Direct import assertions show root ID/epoch/capabilities/modelsource ignored while nested IDs remain guarded; repeated/bulk ignores preserve independent guards and do not grant new authorization. Collection targets do not strip member IDs.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Ignore Flag

requirements.text: When this value is used then any `<SINGULAR>id` present in the root entity MUST be ignored, and any validation to ensure it matches the targeted entity's existing `<SINGULAR>id` value MUST NOT be performed.

review.note: Direct import assertions show root ID/epoch/capabilities/modelsource ignored while nested IDs remain guarded; repeated/bulk ignores preserve independent guards and do not grant new authorization. Collection targets do not strip member IDs.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Ignore Flag

requirements.text: This feature MUST only apply in cases where the request is targeted to a single entity not a collection.

review.note: Direct import assertions show root ID/epoch/capabilities/modelsource ignored while nested IDs remain guarded; repeated/bulk ignores preserve independent guards and do not grant new authorization. Collection targets do not strip member IDs.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Ignore Flag

requirements.text: Note that any nested entities in the request MUST retain their `<SINGULAR>id` values.

review.note: Direct import assertions show root ID/epoch/capabilities/modelsource ignored while nested IDs remain guarded; repeated/bulk ignores preserve independent guards and do not grant new authorization. Collection targets do not strip member IDs.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Ignore Flag

requirements.text: In cases where the target entity is a Version, then the flag MUST apply to both the Resource's `<SINGULAR>id` and the `versionid`.

review.note: A direct Version PATCH with mismatching Resource and Version IDs and ignore=id updates the target while preserving its path-bound IDs.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Ignore Flag

requirements.text: This value indicates that any `modelsource` attribute included in the request MUST be ignored.

review.note: Direct import assertions show root ID/epoch/capabilities/modelsource ignored while nested IDs remain guarded; repeated/bulk ignores preserve independent guards and do not grant new authorization. Collection targets do not strip member IDs.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Ignore Flag

requirements.text: This value indicates that any attempt to modify a read-only Resource MUST be silently ignored as if the Resource in question was never included in the request. Usage of this value in situations where removing the Resource from the request would invalidate the syntax or semantics of the request MUST generate an error ([bad_flag](#bad_flag)).

review.note: Readonly bulk ignore preserves the locked subtree and processed-result membership, but sole-target or invalidating cascade use rejects bad_flag. Unsupported ignore values and malformed selected entries reject without partial state.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Ignore Flag

requirements.text: Implementations MAY define additional values.

review.note: Additional ignore values are an implementation extension point, not mandatory. This profile rejects unoffered values and does not assert future/custom ignore behavior.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Ignore Flag

requirements.text: Specifying an invalid, or unsupported, value for this flag MUST generate an error ([bad_ignore](#bad_ignore)).

review.note: Readonly bulk ignore preserves the locked subtree and processed-result membership, but sole-target or invalidating cascade use rejects bad_flag. Unsupported ignore values and malformed selected entries reject without partial state.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: The `inline` flag MAY be used on requests to indicate whether nested collections/objects, or certain (potentially large) attributes, are to be included in the response message.

review.note: Bridge tests directly exercise model-relative collections, Meta, Documents and explicit Registry configuration in server responses. This establishes server support only; producer and client behavior are not qualified here.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: The `inline` flag on a request indicates that the response MUST include the contents of all specified inlineable attributes. Inlineable attributes include:

review.note: The server tests exercise each listed inlineable category: Registry configuration, Registry collections, Resource and Version documents, and Resource metadata. Producer and client behavior are not qualified by these tests.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: While the `<RESOURCE>` and `<RESOURCE>base64` attributes are defined as two separate attributes, they are technically two separate "views" of the same underlying data. As such, the usage of each will be based on the content type of the Resource, and specifying `<RESOURCE>` in the `inline` flag value MUST be interpreted as a request for the appropriate attribute. In other words, `<RESOURCE>base64` is not a valid `inline` value.

review.note: The bridge selects the appropriate file or filebase64 view from content type, preserves JSON domain values, and rejects filebase64 as an inline selector. These tests qualify the server path only.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: The value of the `inline` flag is a list of `<PATH>` values where each is a string indicating which inlineable attribute to show in the response. References to nested attributes are represented using an [xRegistry dot (`.`) notation](#xregistry-dot--notation) where the xRegistry collection names along the hierarchy are concatenated. For example: `endpoints.messages.versions` will inline all Versions of Messages.  Non-leaf parts of the `<PATH>` MUST only reference xRegistry collection names and not any specific entity IDs since `<PATH>` is meant to be an abstract traversal of the model.

review.note: Bridge view tests exercise dotted nested collection paths and reject a specific entity ID in a non-leaf position before opening the source. This qualifies server path handling.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: There MAY be multiple `<PATH>`s specified in a single request and each protocol binding specification will indicate how the list is specified.

review.note: The HTTP server accepts comma-separated inline paths; DocumentViewUsesResponseLocalPointersWithoutDefaultVersionDuplication requests two paths and asserts the resulting document. This evidence qualifies server support only.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: The `*` value MAY be used to indicate that all nested inlineable attributes at that level in the hierarchy (and below) MUST be inlined - except `model`, `modelsource` and `capabilities` at the root of the Registry. These three are excluded since the data associated with them are configuration related. To include their data the request MUST include `<PATH>` values of `model`, `modelsource` or `capabilities` explicitly. Use of `*` MUST only be used as the last part of the `<PATH>` (in its entirety). For example, `foo*` and `*.foo` are not valid `<PATH>` values, but `*` and `endpoints.*` are.

review.note: BridgeRootInlineIsExplicitAndDoesNotAddSourceRequests verifies root wildcard expansion, configuration exclusions and explicit inclusion; InvalidInlineAndCollectionsInputsFailBeforeAnySourceAcquisition rejects internal, prefixed and suffixed wildcard forms. This qualifies server behavior only.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: An `inline` flag without any value MAY be supported and if so it MUST have the same semantic meaning as a value of `*`.

review.note: An explicitly present inline flag with no value is equivalent to `inline=*`; the test checks nested collections and an inlined document in both responses.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: The specific value of `<PATH>` will vary based on where the request is directed. For example, a request to the root of the Registry MUST start with a `<GROUPS>` name, while a request directed at a Group would start with a `<RESOURCES>` name.

review.note: EveryEntityAndCollectionUsesItsActualResponseRoot asserts paths relative to Registry, Group collection, Group, Resource collection and Resource request targets.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: When specifying a collection to be inlined, it MUST be specified using the plural name for the collection in its defined case.

review.note: The server accepts valid plural paths and rejects both the singular collection name and a case-variant plural name before source acquisition. Producer rejection behavior is not established by this test.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: A request to inline an unknown, or non-inlineable, attribute MUST generate an error ([bad_inline](#bad_inline)).

review.note: The HTTP server returns bad_inline for an unknown inline path; the separate known non-inlineable error clause requires inline_noninlineable. Because the source assigns overlapping errors to non-inlineable values, this qualifies only the unknown server path; producer behavior is not established.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: Note: If the Registry cannot return all expected data in one response because it is too large then it MUST generate an error ([too_large](#too_large)). In those cases, the client will need to query the individual inlineable collection attributes in isolation so the Registry can leverage a pagination type of feature to iteratively retrieve the entities.

review.note: OversizedInlineDocumentResponseCanBeReadByIndividualCollection verifies too_large for the aggregate inline document response and successful retrieval of an individual Versions collection. The client paging loop and producer behavior are not qualified here.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: The `setdefaultversionid` flag MAY be used on any write operation directed to a single Resource, its `meta` sub-object or its Versions. The primary use case is one in which the current default Version is being deleted and the client wishes to choose a new default Version at the same time - to avoid an incorrect one being chosen temporarily.

review.note: Direct Resource, Meta, Version and Version collection writes select the exact flagged target. Deleting the current default selects another Version in the same persisted event batch; collection creation can select a target created by that operation.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: Use of this flag on an operation that allows for modifying multiple Resources MUST generate an error ([bad_flag](#bad_flag)).

review.note: Registry, Group collection, Group and Resource collection PATCH reject the flag with bad_flag. Exact exported state and event count remain unchanged, including after restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: This flag MUST include a single parameter, a string containing the case-sensitive `versionid` of the Version that is to become the new default Version.

review.note: Missing, empty and malformed values reject bad_defaultversionid; repeated values reject bad_flag. A wrong-case target rejects unknown_id, while exact target selection succeeds and persists.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: - A value of `null` indicates that the client wishes to switch to the ["default = newest" algorithm](#default-version-of-a-resource). In other words, the "sticky" aspect of the current default Version will be removed and `meta.defaultversionsticky` MUST be set to `false`.

review.note: The null flag overrides an older pointer and sticky true in Meta input, selects newest semver, exposes false and preserves that selection after restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: - If during a Version create operation the server is asked to choose the `versionid` value for the new Version, then including that value as the `setdefaultversionid` value is not possible. In those cases a value of `request` MAY be used as a way to reference that new Version.

review.note: With client Version IDs disabled, Resource POST assigns ID 2 and request selects exactly that new Version. Later publication leaves the sticky selection and exact selected metadata intact through restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: - A value of `request` MUST only be used on APIs that allow the creation of only a single new Version. In the case of HTTP, that is the `POST` API directed to a Resource. This is because no other operation allows for the creation of a single Version without specifying its `versionid`. Using it when more than one Version is created MUST generate an error ([too_many_versions](#too_many_versions)).  Other uses of this value on an inappropriate API MUST generate an error ([bad_flag](#bad_flag)).

review.note: Resource POST with a generated ID succeeds; read/head/options, Meta PATCH, Version replacement and Version collection POST reject request with bad_flag. The multi-created-Version too_many_versions branch has no direct evidence in this slice, so the composite obligation remains pending.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: - If a value of `request` was used but no Version was created for the request, then an error ([defaultversionid_request](#defaultversionid_request)) MUST be generated.

review.note: Resource POST replacing an existing Version with request rejects defaultversionid_request. The attempted Version metadata change leaves no persisted state or event change.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: - If a non-`null` and non-`request` value does not reference an existing Version of the Resource, after all Version processing is completed, then an error ([unknown_id](#unknown_id)) MUST be generated.

review.note: Missing and wrong-case target flags reject unknown_id after a valid attempted Meta mutation. Exact export and event count are unchanged after each rejection and restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: - Setting the `meta.defaultversionid` to a non-empty value via this flag MUST also set the `meta.defaultversionsticky` attribute to `true`.

review.note: Exact target flags set sticky true despite false Meta input and during deletion of the previous default. The assigned-Version request flag also sets true and prevents later publication from moving the default.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: - Use on a request that updates more than one Resource MUST generate an error ([bad_flag](#bad_flag)).

review.note: Multi-Resource-capable write paths reject the flag before mutation. The full export and event count are preserved across Registry, Group and collection attempts and restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: - Use of this flag MUST override any `meta.defaultversionid` and `meta.defaultversionsticky` values that are present in the request.

review.note: An explicit older target overrides newer pointer and false sticky Meta values. The null flag reverses that policy despite older pointer and true sticky input; both results persist.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: Any other invalid usage of this flag MUST generate an error ([bad_defaultversionid](#bad_defaultversionid)).

review.note: Missing parameter, empty parameter and illegal identifier syntax reject bad_defaultversionid. Separate invalid operation and duplicate-parameter controls assert the more specific bad_flag contract.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Sort Flag

requirements.text: When a request is directed to a collection of Groups, Resources or Versions, the `Sort` flag MAY be used to indicate the order in which the entities of that collection are to be returned (i.e. sorted). Use of the `sort` flag on a non-collection result MUST generate an error ([sort_noncollection](#sort_noncollection)).

review.note: The shared query planner accepts sort only for Group, Resource and Version collection paths and returns sort_noncollection for entity paths.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Sort Flag

requirements.text: This flag MUST include a single parameter, a string containing the attribute (`<ATTRIBUTE>`) name to use as the "sort key" plus an OPTIONAL indication of whether the results are to be sorted in ascending or descending order.

review.note: The parser rejects repeated sort parameters; the query accepts one scalar path with an optional asc/desc order.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Sort Flag

requirements.text: - `<ATTRIBUTE>` MUST be a [dot (`.`) notation](#xregistry-dot--notation) path to one of the attributes defined in collection's entities that will be the primary sort key for the results. The attribute MUST only reference a scalar attribute within the top-level collection, it MUST NOT attempt to traverse into a nested xRegistry collection even if that nested collection is inlined.

review.note: Sort projections are compiled against model-known scalar fields and reject unknown, complex, wildcard, or nested-collection paths.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Sort Flag

requirements.text: - An OPTIONAL "sort order" (`asc` for ascending, `desc` for descending) MAY be specified to indicate whether the first entity in the returned collection MUST be the "lowest" values (`asc`) or whether it MUST be the "highest" value (`desc`). When not specified, the default value MUST be `asc`.

review.note: Sort tests exercise the default ascending order and explicit descending order for scalar keys.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Sort Flag

requirements.text: When a pagination type of feature is used to return the results, but the `sort` flag is not specified, then the server MUST sort the results on the entities' `<SINGULAR>id` value in ascending order. When pagination is not used, it is RECOMMENDED that servers still sort the results by `<SINGULAR>id` (asc) for consistency.

review.note: Pagination without an explicit sort orders entity IDs ascending across page boundaries; the shared query engine also sorts an unsorted source by ID.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Sort Flag

requirements.text: Sorting MUST be done using the data type comparison rules as specified in the [filter Flag](#filter-flag) section. However, there are certain situations that might introduce ambiguity between implementations. For example, not all persistent stores support `NaNs` (Not-a-Number values), or if the data type of an attribute changes on a per-instance basis, then consistent sorting across implementations on that attribute might be challenging. While interoperability is critical, requiring consistency in these edge cases could be excessively burdensome for implementations. To that end, this specification does not mandate the exact ordering in these situations, aside from the requirement that an implementation MUST sort the result the same way each time.

review.note: Sorting uses the same typed comparison implementation as filtering; direct tests cover timestamp normalization, conditional per-instance types, string collation, and deterministic results across source order.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Sort Flag

requirements.text: Entities that do not have a value for the specified attribute MUST be treated the same as if they had the "lowest" possible value for that attribute. If more than one entity shares the same attribute value then the `<SINGULAR>id` MUST be used as a secondary sorting key, using the same `asc`/`desc` value specified for the primary sorting key.

review.note: Tests verify missing values sort lowest and tied values use the entity ID in the primary sort direction.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Sort Flag

requirements.text: An invalid usage of, or value for, the `sort` flag MUST generate an error ([bad_sort](#bad_sort)).

review.note: Unknown and unsupported projections, invalid directions, and repeated sort parameters return bad_sort; entity targets return sort_noncollection.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SpecVersion Flag

requirements.text: The SpecVersion flag MAY be used to indicate the xRegistry specification version that the response MUST adhere to. The parameter value of this flag MUST be a case-insensitive string.

review.note: The flag accepts case variations of the supported version; its parser normalizes the parameter before matching the supported major/minor and suffix.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SpecVersion Flag

requirements.text: If the specified version is not supported, then an error ([unsupported_specversion](#unsupported_specversion)) MUST be generated. When not specified, the default value MUST be the newest version of this specification supported by the server.

review.note: Unsupported major/minor and suffix values return unsupported_specversion. Omission selects the newest supported version, currently 1.0-rc4.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SpecVersion Flag

requirements.text: When comparing `specversion` strings, the server MUST silently ignore the "patch" version number and only consider the "major.minor" version numbers. This is because any "patch" version updates will only contain clarifications and ought not require any code changes for server implementations. Therefore, all patch versions of the same "major.minor" version MUST be forwards and backwards compatible.

review.note: A numeric patch component is ignored when matching the supported 1.0-rc4 version; both 1.0.7-rC4 and the unpatched form return identical representations.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SpecVersion Flag

requirements.text: However, due to the potential for semantics changes of versions with suffix values (e.g. `v2.0.0-rc1`), the suffix value MUST be part of the comparison checking.

review.note: Suffix changes are significant: rc3 and rc5 variants of 1.0 are rejected as unsupported_specversion while rc4 is accepted case-insensitively.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: If an error occurs during the processing of a request, even if the error was during the creation of the response (e.g. an invalid `inline` value was provided), then an error MUST be generated and the entire request MUST be undone.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: In general, when an error is generated, it SHOULD be sent back to the client. However, this MAY not happen if the server determines there is a good reason to not do so - such as due to security concerns.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: Each protocol binding specification will define how the error structure SHOULD be returned back to clients.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: | Type  | REQUIRED. MUST be a URI to the error definition/specification. |

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: | Code  | REQUIRED. MUST be the HTTP response code and status text. |

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: | Title | REQUIRED. MUST be a short (non-empty) human-readable summary of the error. This SHOULD be sufficiently detailed for most users to determine what is the cause of the error. See the text below about substitution strings. |

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: | Detail | OPTIONAL. While "Title" conveys the critical error information, if additional details might be useful to users, such as hints as to how to fix the error, then this field SHOULD be used. |

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: | Subject | OPTIONAL. If present, MUST be a reference to the entity being processed when the error occurred. In the case of a Registry entity, it MUST be the XID of the entity. If no specific value is appropriate then this field MAY be excluded. MUST start with "/" when referencing an xRegistry entity or collection. |

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: | Args | OPTIONAL. A map of the substitution strings that were used when generating the "Title" text. |

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: | Instance | OPTIONAL. This is a non-empty string that can be used by servers to identify details related to the request/error processing. For example, a request or transaction ID of the request that generated the error. This information is not meant to be useful to clients directly, but can be provided to server administrators to help debugging if necessary. This specification places no restriction on the format of this value. |

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: | Source | OPTIONAL. A non-empty string representing the component that raised the error. Similar to "Instance", this is not meant to be used by clients, rather it is for debugging purposes. |

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: The definition of each error's "Title" field MAY include substitutable placeholders that allows for situational specific data to be included. Each placeholder will be denoted as `<...>` in the "Title" text, where "..." MUST be of the form `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`, no longer than 63 characters, and used as the key in the "Args" map. At runtime, each placeholder MUST be replaced with the appropriate value from "Args", and "Args" (if non-empty) MUST appear in the error structure returned to the client. As an optimization, if "<subject>" is used then it MUST NOT be included "Args" as it MUST already appear as a stand-alone field in the error structure.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: The "Type", "Code", and "Subject" values MUST be as specified in error's specification. The "Title" field MAY be modified as needed based on the context in which the implementation is running. This includes being specified in a language other than English, however it MUST still include the same substitution values (possibly in a different order).

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: Most of the error conditions mentioned in this specification will include a reference to one of the errors listed in this section. While it is RECOMMENDED that implementations use those errors (for consistency), they MAY choose to use a more appropriate one. Implementations MAY define additional extension fields, as well as new error definitions. For new errors, it is RECOMMENDED that the "Subject" value appears within the "Title" field, when appropriate.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: While not a requirement, it is RECOMMENDED that custom errors adhere to the following rules for consistency:

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / action_not_supported

requirements.text: In the case of using the HTTP protocol binding, this error MUST include the HTTP `Allow` header in the response indicating which HTTP methods the API supports, if any.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / bad_request

requirements.text: This error is purposely generic and can be used when there isn't a more condition-specific error that would be more appropriate. Implementations SHOULD attempt to use a more specific error when possible. Notice, the `Title` field is just a substitution value and MUST NOT be empty.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / not_found

requirements.text: Note, this SHOULD only be used when the request was directed to an entity that does not exist. For cases where the target entity does exist, but there is an invalid attempt to reference one that doesn't, the [unknown_id](#unknown_id) error SHOULD be used instead.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / parsing_data

requirements.text: This is a fairly generic error, so if a more focused one (e.g. [invalid_attribute](#invalid_attribute)) can be used instead, then it SHOULD be. `<data_description>` is meant to be a phrase, or identifier, of the data being parsed; e.g. `/model`.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / server_error

requirements.text: This error MAY be used when it appears that the incoming request was valid but something unexpected happened in the server that caused an error condition.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / unknown_group_type

requirements.text: Attempts to reference an unknown Group type MUST generate an error ([unknown_group_type](#unknown_group_type)).

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / unknown_resource_type

requirements.text: Attempts to reference an unknown Resource type MUST generate an error ([unknown_resource_type](#unknown_resource_type)).

For Resource/Version attributes, this applies for both levels - e.g. a Version-level extension MUST NOT use a name that conflicts with its Resource-level attribute names.

requirements.text: - A list of possible values for this attribute. Each item in the array MUST be of the type defined by `type`. When not specified, or an empty array, there are no restrictions on the value set of this attribute. This MUST only be used when the `type` is a scalar. See the `strict` attribute below.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.enum`

requirements.text: When specified without `strict` being `true`, this list is just a suggested set of values and the attribute is NOT REQUIRED to use one of them.

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

requirements.text: - Indicates whether the attribute restricts its values to just the array of values specified in `enum` or not. A value of `true` means that any values used that are not part of the `enum` set MUST generate an error ([invalid_attribute](./spec.md#invalid_attribute)). This attribute has no impact when `enum` is absent or an empty array.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.strict`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `true`.

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

requirements.text: - The type of entity that this attribute points to when `type` is set to `url`, `uri` or `xid`. `target` MUST NOT be used for any other type of attribute.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - The value of this model attribute MUST be an "xid template" of one of the following forms:

requirements.text: - `/<GROUPS>/<RESOURCES>` - a plural Resource type name. An entity attribute of this type/target MUST reference an instance of this Resource type, not a specific Version of the Resource.

requirements.text: - `/<GROUPS>/<RESOURCES>[/versions]`. An entity attribute of this type/target MUST reference either an instance of this Resource type or an instance of a Version of this Resource type. Note the `[/versions]` portion of the `target` value is that exact string, including the square brackets.

requirements.text: - An `xid` entity attribute that includes a `target` value as part of its model definition MUST match the `target` entity type specified. An `xid` attribute that does not include a `target` definition has no such restriction and MAY be any valid `xid` value.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - A URI/URL entity attribute MAY include `target` as part of its definition. If so, then any runtime value that is a relative URI/URL (begins with `/`) MUST be an `xid` and MUST adhere to the `target` entity type specified, if specified. Absolute URIs/URLs are not constrained by the presence of a `target` value.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL, and MUST only be used when `type` is `object`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: - Specifies the name of the character set that defines the allowable characters that can be used for the object's top-level attribute names. Any attempt to define a top-level attribute for this object that does not adhere to the characters defined by the character set name MUST generate an error ([invalid_attribute](./spec.md#invalid_attribute)).

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: - Per the [Attributes and Extensions](./spec.md#attributes-and-extensions) section, attribute names are normally limited to just the set of characters that ensure they can reliably be used in cases such as code variable names without the need for some escaping mechanism. However, there are situations where object-typed attribute names need to support additional characters, such as a dash (`-`), and it is known that they will never be used in those restricted character set situations. By setting the `namecharset` aspect to `extended` the server MUST allow for an extended set of valid characters in attribute names for this object.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: The allowed character set for attribute names within an `object` MUST also apply to the top-level `siblingattributes` of any `ifvalues` defined for those attributes.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `strict`.

requirements.text: - The value of this attribute MUST be case-insensitive.

There is currently no mechanism defined by this specification to discover the list (or definition) of additional `namecharset` values supported by an implementation. Implementations SHOULD use their documentation to advertise this extension.

Unless otherwise stated, during creation, or update, of an entity if this attribute is specified, then its value MUST be silently ignored by the server even if the value is invalid. Note that there are some readonly attributes that are examined by a server during a write operation (e.g. `epoch` and IDs).

As such, it is only for informational purposes for clients.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.immutable`

requirements.text: Once set, any attempt to update the value MUST be silently ignored by the server.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.immutable`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - Indicates whether this attribute is REQUIRED to have a non-null value.

requirements.text: - When set to `true`, this specification does not mandate how this attribute's value is populated (i.e. by a client, the server or via a default value), just that by the end of the server's processing of any request it MUST have a non-null value, and generate an error ([invalid_attribute](./spec.md#invalid_attribute)) if not. Note that this implies that a REQUIRED attribute does not mean that clients are mandated to include that attribute in their requests. If the attribute will automatically be populated by the server (e.g. it has a default value defined) the client MAY omit it.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - When not specified the default value MUST be `false`.

Attempts to define a `default` value for a non-scalar type MUST generate an error ([model_scalar_default](./spec.md#model_scalar_default)).

By default, attributes have no default values.

In other words, a new default value MUST only apply to new or subsequent updates (when set to `null`, which would reset it to the current default value) of existing instances of the attribute.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.maxversions`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be zero (`0`).

review.note: The retention boundary test directly asserts compiled BigInteger zero for omitted maxversions in all four supported modes, alongside explicit zero/one/two controls. Omission behaves like explicit zero through first, second and third publications and restart; all Version identities, names, ancestry, membership, export and event counts are checked.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.maxversions`

requirements.text: - A value of zero (`0`) indicates there is no stated limit, and implementations MAY prune non-default Versions at any time. This means it is valid for an implementation to only support one (`1`) Version when `maxversions` is set to `0`.

review.note: Zero states no retention limit and permits, rather than requires, discretionary pruning. This engine chooses no automatic count pruning at zero. RetentionBoundariesPreserveExactNewestChainAcrossVersionModes explicitly retains all three published Versions and their exact chain/default membership through restart for every supported mode. No infinite resource-budget claim or mandatory history guarantee is inferred.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.maxversions`

requirements.text: - When the limit is exceeded, implementations MUST prune Versions by deleting the oldest root Version first (see the [`versionmode`](#groupsstringresourcesstringversionmode) section for how oldest is determined). If the chosen Version is the current default Version, then for the purposes of determining which to delete, the default Version is removed from the collection of Versions, the list of "root" ancestors is recalculated and the "oldest root Version" algorithm is reapplied.

review.note: The successor requires root recalculation, not skipping the default in an ordered list. The sole sticky-root regression reproduced incorrect descendant pruning and is fixed by temporary selection-only exclusion. Manual tests prove sole/independent recalculated roots, oldest timestamps, case-insensitive ties and repeated deletion. All-mode boundary tests prove no pruning before a positive limit is crossed, exact oldest deletion at two and repaired retained chains; uppercase/mixed-case lifecycle cases preserve a sticky oldest default in every mode. SemVer, createdat and modifiedat lifecycle tests add modeled limit reductions and repeated pruning; modifiedat repair reaches a stable final order. Exact default metadata, ancestry, event counts and restart are asserted.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.maxversions`

requirements.text: - An attempt to change `maxversions` to `1` when there are existing Resource instances that have their `defaultversionsticky` attribute set to `true` MUST generate an error ([setdefaultversionsticky_false](spec.md#setdefaultversionsticky_false)). See [`defaultversionsticky` Attribute](spec.md#defaultversionsticky-attribute) for additional information.

review.note: FinalizeResource rejects a modeled limit of one with setdefaultversionsticky_false before pruning a sticky Resource. ReducingMaxVersionsToOneRejectsAnyStickyResourceAtomically places the sticky Resource before and after a nonsticky Resource in traversal order, checks the exact diagnostic, unchanged authored/compiled models, full export, persistence generation and event count through restart, then clears sticky and proves accepted model replacement prunes both Resources to their newest Version with repaired ancestry and persisted state.

These tests demonstrate manual support without treating all mode-specific ordering clauses as complete.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

review.note: VersionModeCaseVariantsPreservePublicationRetentionAndRestart compiles uppercase and mixed-case manual, createdat, modifiedat and semver values to their canonical mode. Each variant proves two-Version newest selection and ancestry, sticky-default retention after a third publication, mode-appropriate deletion repair, unchanged selected Version metadata, exact exported state and event count through restart. The separate manual test retains omitted/default and mixed-case branching/tie evidence.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - The "newest" Version MUST be determined by finding all "leaf" Versions (ones that are not referenced as an ancestor of any other Version), and choosing the one with the newest `createdat` timestamp. If there is more than one, then the one with the highest alphabetically case-insensitive `versionid` value MUST be chosen.

review.note: ManualNewestUsesOnlyLeavesThenTimestampAndCaseInsensitiveId proves selection among multiple manual leaves, excluding a newer-timestamp nonleaf and resolving both distinct and tied timestamps by case-insensitive ID. The createdat and modifiedat lifecycle tests prove ordered chains and newest membership after timestamp-based reordering. The SemVer lifecycle test proves the semver chain's sole leaf is the highest-precedence Version. Default membership and persisted state are asserted across these modes.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - The "oldest" Version MUST be determined by finding all "root" Versions (ones that have an `ancestorid` value that points to itself), and then choosing the one with the oldest `createdat` timestamp. If there is more than one, then the one with the lowest alphabetically case-insensitive `versionid` value MUST be chosen.

review.note: ManualRetentionUsesRootTimestampsThenCaseInsensitiveIds proves selection among multiple independent roots, oldest createdat ordering, case-insensitive ties and root recalculation when the sticky default is excluded. Createdat and modifiedat lifecycle tests prove the oldest Version is the sole root of their ordered chain; SemVer lifecycle proves the lowest-precedence Version is its chain's sole root. Retention boundary tests assert exact identities, ancestry, default and persisted state across all supported modes.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - `manual` - Ancestor Processing: typically provided by clients. During a "create" operation, all new Versions that do not have an `ancestorid` value provided MUST be sorted/processed by `versionid` (in case-insensitive ascending order) and the `ancestorid` value of each MUST be set to the current "newest Version" per the above semantics. Note that as each new Version is processed, it will likely become the "newest" but it might not if its `createdat` timestamp is in the past. If there is no existing Version then the new Version becomes a root and its `ancestorid` value MUST be its own `versionid` attribute value. - Deleted Ancestor: if a Version's ancestor is deleted, then it MUST become a root, and its `ancestorid` MUST be set to its own `versionid` value. - The name of this versionmode is a bit of a misnomer in that it is not 100% "manual". As stated above, as a convenience, by default new Versions will point to the "newest" Version as their ancestor. If this behavior is not desired, then during the "create" operation, the `ancestorid` can be set to point to itself (or any other Version).

review.note: Both collection PATCH and Resource replacement sort a reverse-authored implicit batch by case-insensitive Version ID and self-root the first Version. The branched batch test creates a newer leaf, then a backdated child that makes its parent a nonleaf; the next implicit Version correctly chooses the other branch's newest leaf rather than the last-created Version. Explicit self-root input is preserved. A missing ancestor rejects the complete batch without changing export or events; deleting the successful batch's parent reroots only its direct child. Exact ancestry, selected default and event counts survive restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - `createdat` - Ancestor Processing: The `ancestorid` value of each Version MUST be determined via examination of the `createdat` timestamp of each Version and the Versions sorted in ascending order, where the first one will be the "root" (oldest) Version and its `ancestorid` value MUST be its `versionid`. If there is more than one Version with the same `createdat` timestamp then those MUST be ordered in ascending case-insensitive order based on their `versionid` values. - When this `versionmode` is used, the `singleversionroot` aspect MUST be set to `true`.

review.note: SingleVersionRootDefaultsFalseAndAutomaticModesRequireTrue proves automatic modes reject an omitted or false setting and accept true. CreatedAtAncestryReordersTiesUpdatesDeletionAndRetentionAtomically proves every predecessor in an out-of-order batch, equivalent timestamp fractions and case-insensitive A/b ties. Moving Z's createdat ahead of the original root rebuilds the full chain and selects b; middle deletion reconnects it. A batch containing a valid reorder and invalid timestamp rolls back export/events. Later publication and retention to two preserve the oldest sticky default and newest Version with repaired ancestry. Exact chain and default membership survive restart at every stage.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - `modifiedat` - This is the same as the `createdat` algorithm except that the `modifiedat` attribute of each Version MUST be used instead of the `createdat` attribute.

review.note: SingleVersionRootDefaultsFalseAndAutomaticModesRequireTrue proves automatic modes reject an omitted or false setting and accept true. ModifiedAtAncestryUsesTimestampTiesAndPersistsRepairedOrdering uses a fixed clock and createdat values opposite the modifiedat ordering. It asserts every predecessor for equivalent modifiedat timestamps and case-insensitive ID ties, explicit timestamp reordering, rejected mixed batch rollback, deletion reconnect, later publication and sticky retention. Retention repair touches the remaining child's modifiedat to the fixed request time without changing createdat, and the final chain/export persist through restart. ModifiedAtOrderingReachesAStableAncestryAfterIndirectTimestampTouches additionally proves repeated repair when an ancestry change alters ordering.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - `semver` - Ancestor Processing: The `ancestorid` value of each Version MUST either be its `versionid` value (if it is the oldest Version), or the `versionid` of the next oldest Version per the [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) specification's "precedence" ordering rules. - When this `versionmode` is used, the `singleversionroot` aspect MUST be set to `true`.

review.note: SingleVersionRootDefaultsFalseAndAutomaticModesRequireTrue proves automatic modes reject an omitted or false setting and accept true. SemverAncestryUsesPrecedenceThroughBatchDeletionRetentionAndRestart asserts every predecessor in a reverse-authored fifteen-Version batch: numeric prerelease ordering, numeric before nonnumeric, ASCII lexical ordering, longer prerelease lists, release precedence, patch/minor/major and arbitrary-precision components. Authored self-root ancestors are replaced by the SemVer chain. Invalid numeric components and prerelease syntax reject without changing export/events. Middle deletion reconnects the chain; reducing retention to three preserves the oldest sticky default and the two greatest Versions. Exact ancestry, default membership and event counts persist through restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.singleversionroot`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: ManualSingleRootDefaultsAllowIndependentRootsAndRejectInvalidModelTightening proves a Resource model can omit this aspect. SingleVersionRootDefaultsFalseAndAutomaticModesRequireTrue proves automatic version modes require an explicitly authored true value.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.singleversionroot`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.

review.note: ManualSingleRootDefaultsAllowIndependentRootsAndRejectInvalidModelTightening proves omitted and explicit false compile to a multiple-root manual policy, admits two authored self-roots and preserves them through restart. SingleVersionRootDefaultsFalseAndAutomaticModesRequireTrue confirms the common false default and that automatic modes reject that effective value unless true is explicitly authored. Tightening to true rejects without changing model/export/events, then succeeds after joining the roots.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.singleversionroot`

requirements.text: - A value of `true` indicates that only one Version of the Resource can be a root, and the server MUST generate an error ([multiple_roots](./spec.md#multiple_roots)) if any request results in a state where more than one Version of a Resource is a root of an ancestor tree.

review.note: SingleRootPolicyRejectsCreationUpdateAndDeletionRepairWithoutPartialState rejects a new independent root, rerooting an existing child, a mixed batch with a valid candidate edit, and deleting a branched parent whose children would become independent roots. Every failure reports multiple_roots and retains export, persistence generation and event count through restart. Deleting one branch first allows parent deletion and leaves the sole child self-rooted. The model-tightening test also proves rejection of existing multiple roots and acceptance after joining them.

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validateformat`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.

review.note: The merged successor retains the false format-validation default. Omitted and explicit false cases assert the compiled flag, zero validator calls, exact bytes and absent results under both strictness modes.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validateformat`

requirements.text: - Validators MUST treat a Resource with its `hasdocument` model attribute set to `false`, a Version with no domain-specific document even though `hasdocument` is `true`, and a Version with an empty domain-specific document as 3 variants of "the domain-specific document is empty (zero bytes in length)" and MUST yield the same semantic results.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validateformat`

requirements.text: - When `hasdocument` is `true`, and a Version uses the `<RESOURCE>url` attribute to reference the document in an external datastore, the resulting [`formatvalidated`](spec.md#format-attribute) attribute on the Version MUST be `"false"`.

review.note: The merged successor preserves the external-Document rule. Relaxed publication and local-to-external replacement return false flags with reasons and never fetch the Document; reversal restores validated local bytes. Strict mode rejects atomically with format_external.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validateformat`

requirements.text: - A value of `true` indicates that the server MUST generate an error ([format_violation](spec.md#format_violation)) if any Version of a Resource instance of this Resource type does not adhere to the `format` value of that Version. An absent `format` value on a Version MUST be treated as a request to disable both "format" and "compatibility" verification logic for that Version.

review.note: The merged successor preserves invalid-format rejection and the absent-format exemption. Direct tests reject invalid publication/replacement atomically and prove zero validator calls with absent format and a present compatibility mode, including strict mode.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validateformat`

requirements.text: - A value of `false` indicates that the server MUST NOT perform any `format` checking for Versions of Resources of this Resource type.

review.note: The merged successor retains the prohibition. Recognized formats with false or omitted model validation cause zero validator calls across publication, replacement and new Versions, with exact bytes and no result flags.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validatecompatibility`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validatecompatibility`

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validatecompatibility`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.

review.note: The merged successor retains the false compatibility-validation default. Omitted and explicit false cases assert the compiled flag while syntax validation remains enabled; real dependency counts isolate skipped compatibility passes under both strictness modes.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validatecompatibility`

requirements.text: - A value of `true` indicates that the server MUST generate an error ([compatibility_violation](spec.md#compatibility_violation)) if any Version of a Resource instance of this Resource type does not adhere to the rules of the `meta.compatibility` value for that Resource's `format` value. See [`strictvalidation`](#groupsstringresourcesstringstrictvalidation) for exceptions to this requirement.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validatecompatibility`

requirements.text: - When a Version does not have a `format` value then compatibility verification MUST NOT be done.

review.note: The merged successor retains the exemption. With compatibility mode present, missing-format Versions publish, replace bytes and create another Version without validator calls or result flags under both strictness modes.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validatecompatibility`

requirements.text: - When this model attribute is `true` then its sibling `validateformat` attribute MUST also be `true`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validatecompatibility`

requirements.text: - A value of `false` indicates that the server MUST NOT perform any `compatibility` checking for instances of this Resource type.

review.note: The merged successor retains the prohibition. Actual dependency acquisition counts distinguish syntax-only passes from enabled compatibility passes, with format and mode present and both strictness settings.

requirements.text: - In cases where this attribute is `false`, but there is a desire to advertise the external entity that has performed the validation, a `label` MAY be added to the Resource's model or to the Resource instance itself with this information.

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.strictvalidation`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.strictvalidation`

requirements.text: - The `format` validation logic MUST generate an error ([format_unknown](spec.md#format_unknown)) if the Version's `format` is an unsupported value.

review.note: The merged successor corrects the historical format_violation reference to format_unknown, matching Core's formatvalidated contract. Direct strict-mode publication tests assert format_unknown and no persisted entities for an unsupported format; relaxed controls return false flags with reasons.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.strictvalidation`

requirements.text: - The `compatibility` validation logic MUST generate an error ([compatibility_unknown](spec.md#compatibility_unknown)) if the Resource's `meta.compatibility` value is an unsupported value.

review.note: The merged successor corrects the historical compatibility_violation reference to compatibility_unknown. A valid backward mode excluded by the selected capability profile rejects a strict Meta update with compatibility_unknown and preserves the previous mode, validated results and exact bytes. Invalid enum values are rejected earlier by model validation.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.strictvalidation`

requirements.text: - If the Version's `format` value is absent, then format and compatibility validation logic MUST NOT be performed for that Version.

review.note: The merged successor retains this relaxed-mode exemption. Direct engine tests with missing format and present compatibility mode prove no validator calls and no result flags, including byte replacement and additional Versions.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.strictvalidation`

requirements.text: - If the Version's `format` value is not supported, then the `format` validation logic MUST NOT generate an error. Instead, the Version's `formatvalidated` and `compatibilityvalidated` attributes MUST be set to `false`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.strictvalidation`

requirements.text: - If the Resource's `meta.compatibility` value is unsupported, then the Version's `compatibilityvalidated` attribute MUST be set to `false`.

review.note: The merged successor preserves the relaxed-mode rule. A valid backward mode excluded by the selected capability profile is retained as metadata while compatibilityvalidated is false with a reason; syntax remains validated and exact bytes are unchanged.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.strictvalidation`

requirements.text: - Regardless of the value of this aspect, if the Version's `format` value is absent, then format and compatibility validation logic MUST NOT be performed for that Version.

review.note: The merged successor retains the unconditional exemption. Both strictness modes with model validation enabled and a present compatibility mode accept missing-format Versions without validator calls or invented results, preserving exact bytes.
