requirements.text: When a client sends a request to a server which is meant to result in a set of records being returned, the client MAY include extra attributes to control how those records are to be returned if the results can not fit within one response message.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Client Request / Client Attributes

requirements.text: The following list of attributes MAY be included in a client's request for a set of records from a server. The client MUST only specify these on the initial request for the set and their presence (and values) in any subsequent request to the server to retrieve additional records for the same pagination sequence is dictated by the server - the client MUST NOT add or modify them.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Client Request / Client Attributes

requirements.text: While this specification defines a mechanism by which clients can initiate the pagination of a result set, servers MAY automatically initiate it themselves, typically if the result set is very large. How the server knows that the client supports pagination, or how clients are made aware of this possibility, is out of scope for this specification.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Client Request / Client Attributes / limit

requirements.text: - Description: Indicates the maximum number of records per message that the client is willing to accept. If the server is unable to meet this criterion then it MUST generate an error.

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Client Request / Client Attributes / limit

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Server Response

requirements.text: When a server returns a subset of records, it MAY include additional attributes to help the client retrieve the additional subsets of records.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Server Response / Server Attributes

requirements.text: The following list of attributes MAY be included in a server's response to a client's request for a set of records. The location and syntax of how these attribute appear in response messages will be defined by the protocol binding being used.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Server Response / Server Attributes / link

requirements.text: - Description: A URI-Reference to another subset of records. The relationship of the subset to the current subset MUST be specified by the [`rel` attribute](#rel). This value is meant to be treated as an opaque value by the client. If a client uses this value in a subsequent request then it MUST use it as it was provided by the server. Any attempt to modify its value, or attributes (such as query parameters), is not defined by this specification and the results from the server are undefined.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Server Response / Server Attributes / link

requirements.text: - REQUIRED if any pagination metadata is included in a response message.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Server Response / Server Attributes / link

requirements.text: - MUST be a URI-Reference as defined in [RFC3986](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986).

requirements.text: - If the size of the entire result set can fit in one response message then the `self` Link attribute SHOULD still be included, however no other Link attribute SHOULD be present.

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

requirements.text: - Description: Indicates the maximum number of records per message that the server will send. requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / HTTP Binding / Iterating over the record set

requirements.text: Once the record set retrieval has started, the client MAY use the Links returned from the server to iterate through the full set of records. Typically, the client will use the `next` Link from each response to retrieve the next subset of records until a response is returned without a `next` Link - indicating that it has reached the end.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / Abstract

requirements.text: This specification defines a Registry-of-Registries domain for xRegistry. Its catalog stores versioned descriptions of independently administered Registries and human-facing websites, with OPTIONAL federation advertisements. A Consumer can discover an entry without fetching or copying the contents it describes.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 1. Overview / 1.1. Scope

requirements.text: The catalog MAY advertise HTTP, OCI, Git, File, OPC UA or extension bindings. [Shared federation][Federation] defines the read operations and Registry context established after selection. A catalog does not have to implement those bindings, serve an HTTP facade for them, proxy their contents or provide a materialized view.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 1. Overview / 1.1. Scope

requirements.text: A catalog's own `category` Groups and `registry` Resources MAY be federated using the shared federation rules and a compatible catalog model. The resulting view combines catalog descriptions; it does not combine the contents of every Registry they describe. A resolver still needs an initial access context and composition policy for the catalog view. An advertised Registry is not automatically added to that view, nor does its advertisement authorize another traversal. Federation policy and cycle limits continue to apply.

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119][RFC2119].

requirements.text: The authoritative xRegistry extension model in [model.json](model.json) defines the catalog as a compact `modelsource`. An implementation MUST apply both that model and this specification's semantic constraints. Core remains authoritative for entity IDs, navigation, labels, Version management and Meta attributes.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 3. Registry Model / 3.1. Hierarchy

requirements.text: A catalog-description Version appends `/versions/<versionid>`. Its Meta entity appends `/meta` to the entry XID. All identifiers MUST follow [Core ID rules][Core IDs]. IDs MUST be unique case-insensitively within their parent scope, but lookups MUST be case-sensitive. For example, `Catalog` and `catalog` MUST NOT identify different siblings. A lookup using the wrong case MUST be treated as not found, not normalized to an existing ID.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 3. Registry Model / 3.1. Hierarchy

requirements.text: IDs MUST contain 1 to 128 ASCII characters. The first character MUST be a letter, digit or `_`. Subsequent characters MUST be letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `~`, `:`, `@` or `-`. Storage mappings MUST preserve the original IDs and their scopes without weakening this grammar or introducing case-only duplicate siblings. For example, `schema:main` is a valid Core ID even on a platform that prohibits `:` in a filename: an ID is not a raw filesystem name. Equal IDs in distinct parent or model-type scopes do not imply identity.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 3. Registry Model / 3.1. Hierarchy

requirements.text: Every catalog entry MUST belong to a Category. Category IDs are open-ended. A producer MUST NOT assume that a Category ID selects a protocol, grants trust or proves a target model. Empty Categories are valid. A catalog MAY host other Group types in addition to this domain.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 3. Registry Model / 3.1. Hierarchy

requirements.text: Registry Resources MUST have `hasdocument: false`, so their metadata is their document. There is no separate `registry` document, `registrybase64` content or `registryurl` document locator in this domain. The `xregurl` domain attribute does not replace a Core document locator.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 3. Registry Model / 3.2. Versions and References

requirements.text: Each non-alias entry MUST have at least one catalog-description Version. Core determines its default Version through `meta.defaultversionid`. A consumer MUST NOT select a description by sorting Version IDs, endpoint tags or timestamps instead.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 3. Registry Model / 3.2. Versions and References

requirements.text: An endpoint, authority, type assertion or relationship is description data. Core permits changing that data by updating a Version or creating another Version. This domain requires neither immutable descriptions nor a target snapshot for every catalog Version. When a consumer needs a stable snapshot, it MUST use the selected binding's revision rules.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 5. Federation Advertisements / 5.7. Extensions

requirements.text: The model's advisory `enum` permits extension `binding` values. An extension SHOULD use a collision-resistant name under its publisher's control and document its endpoint, parameters, version rules, security properties and conformance requirements.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 5. Federation Advertisements / 5.7. Extensions

requirements.text: Unknown profiles remain valid catalog descriptions when their common fields are valid. A consumer that does not implement their semantics MUST exclude them from supported resolution candidates. It MUST NOT infer a known binding from their endpoints. Parameters in an extension profile are owned by that extension. Their names do not activate built-in semantics.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 6. Discovery and Selection / 6.1. Entry Selection

requirements.text: A consumer MUST select the containing catalog, Category and catalog entry before interpreting advertisements. XIDs are resolved within that catalog only. When selecting by a label, the consumer MUST name the collection and use [Core string matching][Core filter] and the [shared selector rules][Selectors].

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 6. Discovery and Selection / 6.1. Entry Selection

requirements.text: Label values are literal strings, including the empty string. An absent label does not match. String matching is case-insensitive under Core. This domain MUST NOT impose NFC normalization, language-key selection or a case-sensitive alternate default. A consumer MUST examine every necessary page before claiming a unique match. Zero matches yield `not_found`. Multiple matches yield `ambiguous`, not an arbitrary first entry.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 6. Discovery and Selection / 6.1. Entry Selection

requirements.text: The consumer MUST select an explicit catalog-description Version if the caller supplied one. Otherwise it MUST use the Core default Version. In document view, the consumer obtains that Version through the entry's Meta entity and Versions collection. It MUST NOT merge advertisements from different description Versions.

Otherwise the entry is contradictory and resolution MUST fail. Comparison here is exact string comparison, not URI normalization or a global identity rule.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 6. Discovery and Selection / 6.2. Advertisement Selection

requirements.text: Repeated advertisements are permitted. Exact duplicates do not create ambiguous Registry selection: the first equally ranked candidate wins. Candidates with the same endpoint but different parameters or priorities MUST retain those distinctions. In particular, a matching explicit HTTP advertisement does not change the implicit candidate's zero priority. Map iteration order MUST NOT be used to rank advertisements.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 6. Discovery and Selection / 6.3. Consistency and Failure

requirements.text: An entry's advertisements assert access to a common logical target; its contents can differ between access methods at a given instant. A consumer MUST record the chosen catalog entry, description Version, advertisement and binding revision separately from target entity IDs. It MUST NOT equate two target snapshots solely because their endpoint URLs, labels or `registryid` values match.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 6. Discovery and Selection / 6.3. Consistency and Failure

requirements.text: A consumer MUST check the target's model, Core version and applicable capabilities. Neither `registrytypes` nor a successful endpoint connection replaces those checks. If advertisements demonstrably identify different logical Registries, the consumer MUST report an inconsistent selection rather than silently merge them.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 6. Discovery and Selection / 6.3. Consistency and Failure

requirements.text: An integrity error, policy rejection, unsupported version, ambiguous selection or inconsistent snapshot MUST NOT trigger silent fallback to a different candidate. A caller MAY initiate a new operation with an explicit alternative after inspecting the failure. This specification does not authorize automatic retries through weaker trust or integrity mechanisms.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 7. Descriptive Relationships

requirements.text: A relationship contains REQUIRED `type` and `target` fields and OPTIONAL Core `labels`. No other fields are defined in the relationship object.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 7. Descriptive Relationships / 7.1. `type`

requirements.text: - REQUIRED and MUST be nonempty.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 7. Descriptive Relationships / 7.1. `type`

requirements.text: - Defined values MUST be recognized case-sensitively. Other values remain valid extensions and MUST NOT acquire a built-in meaning.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 7. Descriptive Relationships / 7.1. `type`

requirements.text: `mirrors` MUST NOT be treated as proof of matching bytes, revision, completeness or freshness. `supersedes` MUST NOT automatically redirect selection, and `depends-on` does not enumerate all transitive dependencies.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 7. Descriptive Relationships / 7.2. `target`

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 7. Descriptive Relationships / 7.2. `target`

requirements.text: - An absolute URI MUST identify a catalog entry in another catalog, not merely a target Registry's serving endpoint.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 7. Descriptive Relationships / 7.2. `target`

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 7. Descriptive Relationships / 7.3. `labels`

requirements.text: - Keys and values MUST follow [Core label rules][Core labels], including permitting an empty string value.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 7. Descriptive Relationships / 7.3. `labels`

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 7. Descriptive Relationships / 7.3. `labels`

requirements.text: Relationships MAY contain cycles and duplicate assertions. Consumers MUST NOT traverse them automatically as part of ordinary entry selection. An application explicitly traversing them MUST apply access policy, cycle detection and finite depth and size limits, and MUST report limits rather than presenting truncated results as complete.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 8. Error Handling

requirements.text: Catalog writers and servers MUST apply Core model, attribute and entity errors. For example, a value that violates an attribute constraint generates Core `invalid_attribute`. A field not permitted by the model generates `unknown_attribute`. This domain does not add Core error codes.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 9. Security Considerations

requirements.text: A catalog is untrusted input unless independently authenticated. A URI, `authority`, label or relationship is an assertion, not authorization. Consumers MUST establish endpoint trust and credentials independently. Producers MUST NOT store credentials in URLs, parameters, labels or other catalog metadata.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 9. Security Considerations

requirements.text: Consumers MUST apply policy to the selected scheme, destination and operation before resolving an advertisement or explicitly following a relationship. They MUST protect against requests to unintended local or private services, filesystem escape, redirect loops and resource exhaustion. Redirects MUST NOT cause credentials to be forwarded to an unauthorized destination.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 9. Security Considerations

requirements.text: Names, descriptions, labels and websites MUST be treated as untrusted display data. Consumers MUST NOT execute catalog strings, repository hooks or commands derived from them. Merely displaying `weburl` does not authorize fetching it.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 9. Security Considerations

requirements.text: Digest and commit pins establish particular published bytes or repository objects, not publisher authorization. Consumers MUST validate integrity and publisher trust separately, including native OPC UA application and certificate checks. Catalog mutation, mutable tags and changing endpoints can make previously observed descriptions stale.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 10. Conformance / 10.1. Base Catalog

requirements.text: A base catalog implementation MUST conform to Core 1.0-rc4, implement the authoritative domain model and preserve this specification's hierarchy, metadata-only Resources and Version semantics. It MUST accept conforming entries without labels, `registrytypes`, `authority`, `relationships`, `federationprofiles`, `xregurl` or `weburl`.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 10. Conformance / 10.1. Base Catalog

requirements.text: When a domain attribute is supplied, its types and semantic constraints apply. Unknown `binding` values and relationship types MUST remain valid catalog data if their common fields are valid. A base catalog is not REQUIRED to implement any advertised transport or reachability check.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 10. Conformance / 10.1. Base Catalog

requirements.text: A base entry MAY describe only a website, or have no endpoint at all. Failure to resolve such an entry MUST NOT retroactively invalidate its base catalog conformance.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 10. Conformance / 10.2. Federation-Resolvable Entry

requirements.text: A federation-resolvable entry MUST first be a conforming base entry. In its selected description Version it MUST provide at least one valid advertisement for a binding supported by the consumer, either explicitly or through `xregurl`, with all parameters needed to identify the target. Any xregurl/explicit HTTP consistency constraint MUST also hold.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 10. Conformance / 10.3. Catalog Consumer

requirements.text: A catalog consumer claiming resolution conformance MUST implement the selection procedure. It MUST preserve origin and revision distinctions. It MUST conform to [shared federation][Federation] and each binding it claims to support. It MUST report unsupported operations and failures explicitly. It is not REQUIRED to implement every built-in binding.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 10. Conformance / 10.3. Catalog Consumer

requirements.text: Read-only federation consumption does not prohibit independent, authorized catalog editing under Core. Such editing MUST NOT cause write-through to a target Registry.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 11. Examples and Derived Schemas

requirements.text: Derived artifacts MUST NOT override Core or this specification when a generator omits a constraint or produces an incompatible description. Current limitations and reproduction commands are documented alongside the generated files rather than changing the domain model to accommodate them.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.2. Relationship to Other xRegistry Specs

requirements.text: - A schema plugin's generated schema declares USD prim types. Where those types are also described in an xRegistry Schema Registry, the two MAY be cross-referenced. See [Section 5.5](#55-openusd-registry-to-schema-registry).

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.2. Relationship to Other xRegistry Specs

requirements.text: - A scene whose attributes are driven by live data has that data delivered by some endpoint, which MAY be managed by an xRegistry Endpoint Registry. See [Section 5.6](#56-openusd-registry-to-endpoint-registry).

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.2. Relationship to Other xRegistry Specs

requirements.text: These cross-references are informative. An implementation MAY validate them, but this specification does not require all referents to resolve.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.2. Relationship to Other xRegistry Specs

requirements.text: An externally defined OPC Unified Architecture (OPC UA) projection represents the same model in an OPC UA AddressSpace and retrieves each artifact through the OPC UA file-transfer interface. This specification is its wire-format peer. The two projections share collection names, attribute names and the identifier rules of [Section 5.1](#51-asset-identifiers-and-xids). A Consumer MAY move between them without re-resolving anything. This specification does not depend on the OPC UA projection.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: A `usdassetid` MUST NOT be derived from the artifact's bytes. Such an id would change with each revision and create a separate Resource for each Version of one logical artifact.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: A Consumer that does not select a Version explicitly MUST receive the Resource's [default Version][xRegistry default version]. An `xid` that addresses a specific Version MUST NOT be used as an asset identifier.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: A change that violates the Resource's [`compatibility`][xRegistry compatibility] policy MUST result in a new Resource, not a new Version. For example, a layer can be re-authored to reference assets absent from its previous revision. When the Registry's policy classifies this as incompatible, the rule applies: a Consumer using the cached old closure would otherwise silently compose an incomplete scene.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.1. Notational Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2119).

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.1. Notational Conventions

requirements.text: For clarity, OPTIONAL attributes (specification-defined and extensions) are OPTIONAL for clients to use, but the servers' responsibility will vary. Server-unknown extension attributes MUST be silently stored in the backing datastore. Specification-defined, and server-known extension, attributes MUST generate an error if the corresponding feature is not supported or enabled.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.1. Notational Conventions

requirements.text: In the pseudo JSON format snippets `?` means the preceding attribute is OPTIONAL, `*` means the preceding attribute MAY appear zero or more times, and `+` means the preceding attribute MUST appear at least once. The presence of the `#` character means the remaining portion of the line is a comment. Whitespace characters in the JSON snippets are used for readability and are not normative.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.2. Terminology / 2.2.1. USD Asset

requirements.text: Per the definition of the [`compatibility`][xRegistry compatibility] attribute, all Versions of a single USD asset MUST adhere to the rules defined by the `compatibility` attribute. Any breaking change MUST result in a new USD asset Resource being created.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry

requirements.text: Implementations of this specification MAY include additional extension attributes, including the `*` attribute of type `any`.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.1. Asset Container Groups

requirements.text: Every USD asset (the `usdasset` Resource) MUST reside inside either an Asset Container Group or a Schema Plugin Group.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.1. Asset Container Groups

requirements.text: The `usdassetgroupid` is the asset container identifier. This specification does not define a separate attribute for it. An implementation MUST NOT treat the Group id as a prefix of its members' `assetidentifier` values — member identifiers are already normalized relative to the Group. Where the container identifier is not already a legal xRegistry id, the `usdassetgroupid` MUST be its symbolic identifier ([Section 5.1.1](#511-the-symbolic-identifier-construction)).

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.1. Asset Container Groups

requirements.text: Already legal Core container IDs remain verbatim. An implementation MUST reject a case-insensitive collision for such an ID, and MUST NOT repair it by switching it to a symbolic ID. The sibling assignment rules apply where symbolic construction is needed.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.1. Asset Container Groups

requirements.text: An Asset Container Group MUST set the Core [`name`][xRegistry Core] attribute to the asset container identifier verbatim. This preserves the exact string after id normalization for people browsing the Registry, including through generic third-party tools that display only the id and name.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.1. Asset Container Groups

requirements.text: - **`rootlayer`** — OPTIONAL, type `string`. The `assetidentifier` of this container's single `RootLayer` USD asset. When present, its value MUST equal the `assetidentifier` of a `usdasset` in this Group whose `assetkind` is `RootLayer`. It exists so a Consumer can find the composition entry point without enumerating and inspecting the whole collection.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.2. USD Asset Resources

requirements.text: The `usdassetid` MUST be the assigned symbolic identifier of the Resource's `assetidentifier`. See [Section 5.1](#51-asset-identifiers-and-xids). The `assetidentifier`, not the id, is authoritative. It is REQUIRED: a layer authors it, and a Consumer matches an authored `@...@` reference against it.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.2. USD Asset Resources

requirements.text: A `usdasset` MUST set the Core [`name`][xRegistry Core] attribute to its `assetidentifier` verbatim. People browsing the Registry then see the string the layer authors, unchanged by id normalization, even in generic third-party tools that display only the id and name.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.2. USD Asset Resources

requirements.text: - **`assetidentifier`** — REQUIRED, type `string`. The authored USD asset identifier, normalized relative to its Group as defined in [Section 2.2.2](#222-asset-identifier). An implementation MUST NOT invent an identifier that no layer authors.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.2. USD Asset Resources

requirements.text: - **`assetkind`** — REQUIRED, type `string`, one of `RootLayer`, `SubLayer`, `Reference`, `Payload`, `Texture`, `Package`, `MaterialX`, `Volume`, `SchemaPlugin`, `GeneratedSchema` or `Manifest`. It records the artifact's role in the composition closure, which is independent of its document format: a `SubLayer` and a `Reference` are both USD layers.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.2. USD Asset Resources

requirements.text: An Asset Container Group MUST contain exactly one `usdasset` whose `assetkind` is `RootLayer`.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.2. USD Asset Resources

requirements.text: - **`dependson`** — OPTIONAL, type `array` of `string`. The asset identifiers this artifact directly references, in the order they are authored. These are asset identifiers, not `xid`s, so a resolver can match them directly against the `@...@` references it encounters. See [Section 5.2](#52-the-dependency-closure).

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.2. USD Asset Resources

requirements.text: - **`digest`** — OPTIONAL, type `string`. The lower-case hexadecimal digest of the exact document bytes a Consumer retrieves. When a `usdasset` is served by reference (`usdasseturl`) the digest covers the bytes at that URL. When both a package and its members are present, a member's `digest` covers the extracted member bytes, not the package.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.2. USD Asset Resources

requirements.text: - **`digestalg`** — OPTIONAL, type `string`, one of `Sha256`, `Sha384` or `Sha512`. REQUIRED when `digest` is present. A Consumer that finds a `digest` with no `digestalg` MUST interpret the digest as `Sha256`. This is a processing rule rather than a model default, because an artifact that declares no `digest` has no algorithm to record.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.2. USD Asset Resources

requirements.text: A Consumer that has retrieved an artifact for which a `digest` is declared MUST verify it. A Consumer MUST NOT use an artifact whose digest does not match. A digest establishes integrity, not authenticity: it proves that the bytes match the Registry's description, not that the Registry is entitled to describe them.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.2. USD Asset Resources

requirements.text: All Versions of a single `usdasset` MUST adhere to the semantic rules of the Resource's [`compatibility`][xRegistry compatibility] attribute, if specified. Implementations SHOULD use the xRegistry default algorithm for generating new `versionid` values and for determining which is the latest Version. See [Core Version IDs][xRegistry version-ids] and [default-Version rules][xRegistry default version].

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.3. Schema Plugin Groups

requirements.text: The `usdschemaplugingroupid` is the plugin name, normalized: it MUST be the symbolic identifier of the plugin name declared by the `SchemaPlugin` document the Group contains ([Section 5.1.1](#511-the-symbolic-identifier-construction)). An implementation MUST reject a Group whose id does not match.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.3. Schema Plugin Groups

requirements.text: A Schema Plugin Group MUST set the Core [`name`][xRegistry Core] attribute to the plugin name verbatim, which is non-empty by construction.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.3. Schema Plugin Groups

requirements.text: A Schema Plugin Group SHOULD contain exactly two `usdasset` Resources: one whose `assetkind` is `SchemaPlugin` and one whose `assetkind` is `GeneratedSchema`. A Consumer requires both to register the schema. A Group offering only one document cannot be used to register the schema.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.4. Schema Plugin Resources

requirements.text: The `assetkind` of the plugin manifest MUST be `SchemaPlugin` and its `format` MUST be `USD-PlugInfo/1.0`. The `assetkind` of the generated schema MUST be `GeneratedSchema` and its `format` MUST be `USD-GeneratedSchema/1.0`.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.4. Schema Plugin Resources

requirements.text: `rootlayer` is not defined for Schema Plugin Groups, and a Schema Plugin Group MUST NOT contain a `usdasset` whose `assetkind` is `RootLayer`: a schema plugin is not composed, it is registered.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.5. Formats

requirements.text: This specification refines the [core specification's `format`](https://xregistry.io/xreg/xregistryspecs/core-v1/docs/spec.html#format-attribute) for use in an OpenUSD Artifact Registry by defining the format identifiers such a registry MUST recognize. Implementations MAY define extension format identifiers for other artifact classes, but MUST NOT use the identifiers below for any document that is not conformant with the corresponding specification.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.5. Formats / 4.5.1. USD Layer

requirements.text: - `contenttype` SHOULD be `model/vnd.usda`, `model/vnd.usdc` or `model/vnd.usd` as appropriate.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.5. Formats / 4.5.2. USD Package

requirements.text: - `contenttype` SHOULD be `model/vnd.usdz+zip`.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.5. Formats / 4.5.4. USD Plugin Manifest

requirements.text: - The containing Group's `usdschemaplugingroupid` MUST be the symbolic identifier of the manifest's `Plugins[0].Name` ([Section 5.1.1](#511-the-symbolic-identifier-construction)), and the Group's `name` MUST be that plugin name verbatim.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.5. Formats / 4.5.5. USD Generated Schema

requirements.text: - Although a generated schema is syntactically a USD layer, a Producer MUST publish it with this format identifier rather than `OpenUSD/1.0`, because it is registered rather than composed.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. OpenUSD Registry / 4.5. Formats / 4.5.6. Opaque

requirements.text: - `contenttype` carries the meaningful type discrimination for such artifacts, and an implementation MUST NOT attempt format validation on them.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Relationships and Cross-References / 5.1. Asset Identifiers and `xid`s

requirements.text: > A `usdasset`'s `assetidentifier` MUST be its authored USD asset identifier, > normalized relative to its Group. Its `usdassetid` MUST be the **assigned symbolic > identifier** of that `assetidentifier` (Section 5.1.1). Its `xid` is > consequently `/usdassetgroups/<usdassetgroupid>/usdassets/<usdassetid>`. > The `assetidentifier` attribute is REQUIRED on every `usdasset` and is the > authority: an implementation MUST NOT recover an asset identifier by > attempting to invert the construction.

source.section: OpenUSD Artifact Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Relationships and Cross-References / 5.1. Asset Identifiers and `xid`s / 5.1.1. The Symbolic Identifier Construction

requirements.text: 1. A Producer MUST retain an existing binding for the same exact source, even if the sibling that caused the collision is later deleted. It MUST NOT rename an existing entity to make room, and MUST NOT rebind an existing ID to another source.

requirements.text: Request-response is the primary use case, not a restriction on every operation in a stored document. Native descriptions can include streaming, one-way, and callback operations. Registration does not assert that a service is deployed or reachable. Its invocation addresses, where present, come from the native description or from separate deployment configuration, not from the registry's `self` URL.

requirements.text: An API Version identifies an entry document. Dependencies use the native language's `$ref`, import, include, or equivalent constructs. Resolvers MUST apply that language's base-URI and import rules. The initial base is the document retrieval URL for an embedded document and the effective retrieval URL after redirects for an external document, unless a native identifier establishes another base. Publishers MUST account for relative references when relocating documents. Protobuf and Thrift include paths require explicit resolver configuration; namespace names and Smithy shape IDs are not retrieval URLs.
