source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats

requirements.text: The following profiles define registry `format` identifiers and operation selectors. Implementations MAY support additional profiles. Resolvers MUST report unknown profiles as unsupported rather than infer their syntax.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / OpenAPI

requirements.text: The API document is an OpenAPI Description in JSON or YAML. The root `openapi` field MUST match the selected feature set; it is independent of `info.version`. JSON and YAML representations MUST be distinguished by `contenttype`.

review.note: The bounded JSON operation selector checks that root openapi identifies the selected 3.0/3.1 feature set with a numeric patch component before operation-ID or JSON Pointer selection and dependency acquisition. Arbitrary patch numbers and publisher-schema hyphen suffixes are accepted independently of info.version. JSON content types are checked, but YAML and complete OpenAPI Description validation remain unsupported. Keep this combined obligation pending.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / OpenAPI

requirements.text: For OpenAPI, `operations/{operationId}` resolves an Operation Object with that `operationId` in the API described by the entry document, including referenced path items and operations. Publishers SHOULD supply `operationId`; when present it MUST be unique as specified by the native specification. An ambiguous match MUST fail.

review.note: The bounded JSON selector scans path operations, OpenAPI 3.1 webhooks and reachable nested OpenAPI callbacks with exact case-sensitive operation IDs. Caller-supplied Callback, Path Item and Operation references use their containing source base. Duplicate operation occurrences are ambiguous; malformed operations and unavailable or denied required references fail even after an earlier match. Callback graphs and reference chains have finite depth/work limits and explicit cycle failures. Bare and embedded callback runtime expressions check native source forms, HTTP header tokens and body JSON Pointer escapes without percent-decoding pointer text or evaluating runtime values/URLs. Malformed reachable expressions prevent earlier matches; literal callback text is not URL validation. Webhook and callback map names, including x- names, remain native keys; Callback Object x- extensions are ignored. YAML and complete OpenAPI validation remain unsupported, so this obligation stays pending without native qualification.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / OpenAPI

requirements.text: If an operation has no `operationId`, its reference MUST use a JSON Pointer to the operation object:

review.note: The bounded JSON selector accepts exact inline Operation Objects under paths, OpenAPI 3.1 webhooks, nested callbacks, OpenAPI 3.1 reusable Path Items and OpenAPI 3.0/3.1 reusable Callbacks, including methods without operationId. Native version/object positions and each selected callback expression's runtime syntax are enforced; pointers never dereference Callback, Path Item or operation references. Unused component definitions can be selected explicitly without becoming operation-ID candidates. YAML and complete document validation remain unsupported, so the obligation remains pending without native qualification.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / OpenAPI

requirements.text: The preceding pointer selects `paths["/users/{userId}"].get` in the parsed entry document. JSON Pointer evaluation does not traverse `$ref`. A pointer MUST target an Operation Object; pointing at a Reference Object does not select the referenced operation. Externally defined operations can be selected by their operation ID through the resolved API, or by a pointer on the external document's own retrieval reference where that document is registered as an API.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / Swagger

requirements.text: The `format` identifier for Swagger is `Swagger`. `Swagger/2.0` identifies a [Swagger 2.0 document][swagger] in JSON or YAML. The root `swagger` value MUST be `2.0`, independent of `info.version`. JSON and YAML representations MUST be distinguished by `contenttype`.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / gRPC

requirements.text: `gRPC/descriptor-set` requires a serialized `google.protobuf.FileDescriptorSet` with at least one service descriptor. Descriptor dependencies needed for resolution MUST be included or supplied by an explicitly configured resolver. Descriptor validation MUST account for each file's syntax or edition; unrecognized editions MUST NOT be treated as checked. Binary descriptors use `apibase64` in an embedded JSON representation, not a JSON rendering of the descriptor messages.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / gRPC

requirements.text: The service token MUST be its protobuf package followed by `.` and the service name, without a leading dot. Without a package it is the service name alone. Descriptor-set service names MUST resolve uniquely across the set. The method token is its case-sensitive RPC name. Request and response types and client/server streaming flags come from the selected method declaration.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / Apache Thrift

requirements.text: The `format` identifier for Apache Thrift is `Thrift`. The API document is text conforming to the [Thrift IDL grammar][thrift], which has no document-level language-version field. A validator MUST identify the compiler or grammar revision it supports. Thrift target-language namespaces do not define a universal service namespace.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / Apache Thrift

requirements.text: The method is selected from that service after resolving its `extends` chain. Inherited methods are selectable; ambiguous declarations MUST fail. A service declared only in an included IDL document requires a reference to that document's own API Resource. The registry does not invent a target-language namespace for included services. `oneway` and declared exceptions retain their native meaning.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / Apache Avro Protocol

requirements.text: The `format` identifier for Apache Avro Protocol is `AvroProtocol`. The version identifies the Apache Avro release used to define the protocol. `AvroProtocol/1.12.0` identifies a JSON document conforming to the [Avro 1.12.0 protocol rules][avro]. The document MUST contain a protocol declaration; Avro data schemas are outside this API profile.

review.note: The JSON operation resolver requires a protocol declaration and selects exact native message names with bounded parsing and declaration guards. Protocol/type fullnames and effective namespace collisions are checked; a qualified name overrides a supplied namespace. The shared Avro parser binds all named types and request/response/error schemas in declaration order, rejects forward or unknown references, and checks distinct declared error identities. Request fields and bound defaults are validated; Avro 1.12 union defaults use the first matching branch while older data-schema profiles retain their first-branch rule. Unused malformed types, invalid later messages and defaults prevent an earlier selection or a missing-operation result. Recursive default expansion is bounded. Native message JSON and schemas remain unchanged. Protocol logical-type annotations use underlying wire schemas without conversion or logical comparison, including unknown names and invalid logical parameters; underlying schema/default checks remain enforced. Data-schema compatibility policy is unchanged. Complete Avro 1.12.0 protocol conformance and native qualification are not established. SupportsApiDocumentValidation remains false. Keep this format requirement pending.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / Apache Avro IDL

requirements.text: The `format` identifier for Apache Avro IDL is `AvroIDL`. The version identifies the Apache Avro release used to define the IDL. `AvroIDL/1.12.0` identifies text conforming to the [Avro 1.12.0 IDL rules][avroidl]. The IDL MUST produce a protocol, not only a data schema. Schema-only IDL is outside this API profile.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / GraphQL

requirements.text: GraphQL SDL MUST define a valid schema under the September 2025 specification. For this draft's introspection profile, the document MUST be a JSON response object with `data.__schema` and no `errors`. It MUST describe all root operation types and named types, including deprecated fields, enum values, arguments, and input fields. Type references MUST include the full `kind`, `name`, and `ofType` chains. Descriptions can be omitted. Missing information needed to reconstruct the schema makes the representation incomplete and MUST cause validation or operation resolution to fail; a partial introspection query result is not a complete schema document.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / GraphQL

requirements.text: The operation kind MUST be `query`, `mutation`, or `subscription`. The field MUST exist on the corresponding root type identified by the schema definition or introspection data; that type need not be named `Query` or `Mutation`. The locator identifies a root schema field, not a named executable GraphQL operation or a complete selection set. A subscription retains its streaming semantics.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / WSDL

requirements.text: For WSDL, an interface token MUST use the expanded QName `{namespace}local`, independent of XML prefix choices. Apply token escaping and percent encoding to the entire expanded name. For a WSDL 1.1 port type in `urn:example:users`:

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / WSDL

requirements.text: WSDL 1.1 uses the operation's local name. A name-only selector MUST fail if operations are overloaded. An overload can be selected using both effective input and output names, including the defaults specified by WSDL 1.1 section 2.4.5. Use the token `!` for an absent input or output; `!` is not a valid XML NMTOKEN. WSDL 1.1 input and output names are NMTOKENs, not NCNames.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / WSDL

requirements.text: For WSDL 2.0, both the interface and operation tokens MUST be expanded QNames. An inherited operation retains its declaring namespace. Equivalent inherited components with the same QName identify one operation; conflicting components make the document invalid under WSDL's component rules. The input/output overload suffix is only defined for WSDL 1.1. Neither form chooses a service endpoint or binding; those are separate native WSDL components.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / OpenRPC

requirements.text: The token MUST match the `name` of exactly one resolved Method Object in `methods`. Parameters, result, and errors come from that object, not from an example JSON-RPC request.

review.note: The optional OpenRPC/1.4 document resolver selects one resolved Method Object by exact name and retains its native parameters, result, errors and references without inlining. Every resolved method requires params and checks paramStructure, annotations, resolved parameter/result descriptor shape, unique exact parameter names and required-before-optional order. An absent result retains notification semantics. Resolved errors require exact integer codes and string messages; numeric aliases are duplicates, with a bounded 256-character number spelling. Content Descriptor/Error/Tag/Link/Example Pairing/Example references use their containing source base and caller-authorized bounded retrieval; missing, denied, cyclic or malformed later contracts prevent an earlier selection. Supplied link method names must identify exactly one occurrence after the complete Method array resolves, including forward references; link graphs are not invoked. Supplied method servers/variables, link server overrides, resolved tags and method/tag externalDocs have required-property and type checks. Documentation, terms-of-service, contact and license URLs also require well-formed absolute URL syntax, rejecting raw whitespace/control characters and malformed escapes without acquisition or normalization. Server templates/defaults/enum values and link parameters remain native without substitution or inferred endpoints, and URL fields are never invoked; full template/linked-parameter validation and URL reachability checks are not claimed. Example pairings require name strings and params arrays; examples require name strings and literal values, with null retained and value/externalValue conflicts rejected. Missing example results remain notification examples. Nested ref-shaped literal values remain data; example schema-instance validation is not claimed. Descriptor schema objects remain opaque and do not cause acquisition. Full format/schema validation, API-Version acquisition and native qualification remain separate obligations.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / Smithy

requirements.text: Smithy uses IDL `$version` or the AST `smithy` field. Values `2` and `2.0` select the Smithy 2 model. `contenttype` MUST distinguish IDL text from JSON AST. The model MUST include an operation shape; resolving a shape MUST NOT infer a deployment address or protocol binding that the model does not supply.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / API Registry / API Formats / Smithy

requirements.text: The ID MUST resolve to an operation shape in the assembled model, not a service, resource, or data shape. Assembly MUST resolve the model files needed for that operation. Input, output, errors, and traits retain their Smithy meaning.

review.note: The bounded JSON selector resolves an exact absolute operation shape ID in a caller-assembled Smithy 2 AST and checks its transitive data/custom-trait dependencies without treating shape IDs as retrieval URLs. Public tests cover native shape preservation, wrong-kind rejection, missing dependencies, traversal limits and recursive validity within the selected closure: container-only cycles and types without finite values are rejected while terminating recursion is preserved. Reached operation input/output/errors references permit only target; aggregate members can also declare traits. Extra properties are rejected, including empty trait maps on plain references, and error diagnostics identify array occurrences. These property checks do not inspect unrelated references or literal trait payloads. Selected enum definitions require Unit targets and unique nonempty string or signed-32-bit integer values, including implicit string values and exact numeric equivalence. EnumValue applies only to enum/intEnum members. Reachable documentation/error traits check their native string values, and recognized annotation/idempotent/trait markers require object values, including member and custom-trait definition declarations. Explicit prelude target rules restrict required to structure members, input/output/error to structures, readonly/idempotent to operations and trait markers to simple/aggregate roots. Declared readonly/idempotent, input/output/error and error/trait-definition conflicts are rejected independent of property order. Idempotent exists/notFound properties are mutually exclusive arrays of absolute root shape IDs that must exactly match operation-level error declarations, whose referenced definitions retain the normal error checks. Empty hints preserve native success semantics without adding declarations or executing requests. For reachable input/output-marked structures, recognized AST reference positions across the assembled model permit only the matching slot of one operation; other references and sharing invalidate selection. Applied trait IDs count as references, while literal trait payloads, metadata and service rename entries do not. Unmarked structures retain sharing semantics. Reachable defaults check applicability, root-null rejection, member null overrides, explicit root-default repetition using exact numeric comparison, scalar types, integer ranges, finite float/double numbers and exact special-value strings, base64 blobs, enum membership and empty containers. Implicit PrimitiveBoolean/Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double retain their scalar kinds and false/zero root defaults: structure members must repeat the default or override it with null; list/map/union members need no repetition. Primitive names are exact and do not synthesize unspecified types. No defaults are inserted or acquired. Timestamp and string-encoded bigInteger/bigDecimal defaults report Unsupported; applied constraints and full default validation remain open. Reachable trait-marker selector/conflicts/structurallyExclusive properties have shape checks. Declared custom-trait conflicts are enforced on reachable roots, members and trait definitions independent of property order and without requiring definitions for unapplied conflict IDs. Structural exclusivity is enforced per reachable structure and trait ID: member mode limits direct member markings and target mode limits members whose target carries the trait, including repeated uses of one target. Different structures and trait IDs retain separate limits; union alternatives are not constrained. Reachable breakingChanges declarations require a nonempty rule array, exact change/severity enum values, string messages and RFC 6901 pointer syntax. Omitted defaults remain omitted; schema-path resolution and semantic model comparison remain open. Unreachable specializations and unrelated shape constraints remain unchecked. General selectors and other trait members remain unchecked. Full model assembly, mixins/apply processing, IDL parsing, complete prelude and trait/schema validation remain unsupported. Keep this obligation pending; partial selection is not complete Smithy conformance.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / Security Considerations

requirements.text: Documents, operation names, and dependency links are untrusted input. Registry write access does not grant permission to contact the described API. Resolvers MUST NOT invoke operations while validating or resolving a description.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / Security Considerations

requirements.text: External retrieval MUST require explicit policy authorization, including each redirect target. Resolvers MUST enforce limits on document size, retrieval count, recursion depth, and duration, and detect dependency cycles. Local file access and private network access MUST be denied unless explicitly authorized. Credentials MUST NOT be forwarded automatically across origins. XML parsers MUST disable external-entity expansion; YAML parsers MUST NOT construct native objects from document tags. These are requirements of this working-draft extension, not additional claims about the cited description languages.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / Security Considerations

requirements.text: Registry authentication and authorization are separate from the API's security requirements. API documents SHOULD describe security schemes without embedding passwords, access tokens, or private keys. Consumers MUST apply their own trust policy to servers and authorization URLs found in a document.

source.section: API Registry Service - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / Conformance

requirements.text: A registry implementing this extension MUST implement the group/resource model and the applicable Core document, metadata, and validation rules. It is not REQUIRED to implement every language parser or an operation resolver. A resolver claiming support for a profile MUST implement that profile's identity, escaping, dependency, and failure rules; storage support alone is not locator support.

source.section: Media Endpoints Compatibility and Validation - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119][rfc2119].

review.note: RFC 2119 interpretation for this working draft, not an independently executable media operation. Reviewed with the complete retained W26 validation-boundary draft and its model-aligned vectors.

source.section: Media Endpoints Compatibility and Validation - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / Scope

requirements.text: Codec identifiers are open-vocabulary, case-sensitive strings. Implementations MUST preserve their spelling and MUST NOT normalize their case when comparing identifiers.

review.note: MaterializeMedia preserves exact codec strings. Lowercase and mixed-case spellings of known opposite-kind identifiers remain unrecognized instead of being normalized into forbidden codecs. Focused managed tests pass on both frameworks; a temporary uppercase-normalization mutation fails these opposite-kind cases on both frameworks. No native or receiver-carriage qualification is claimed.

source.section: Media Endpoints Compatibility and Validation - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / Scope

requirements.text: An endpoint provider MUST ensure that its producer-only codec and `streamformat` declarations describe the media it provides. A receiving implementation MUST decide whether it can consume those declarations. Successful xRegistry validation does not establish that a receiver supports the advertised media.

review.note: Actual media accuracy and receiver acceptance require endpoint-provider and receiving-path evidence. Registry metadata validation cannot observe either. Keep this obligation pending; accepting a metadata declaration is not evidence that a protocol carries or consumes it.

source.section: Media Endpoints Compatibility and Validation - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / Validation

requirements.text: An xRegistry validator MUST enforce the types and enumerations declared by the Media Endpoints model. When the selected protocol defines `streamformat`, the validator MUST accept only values in that protocol's declared enumeration and MUST reject other values.

review.note: The focused public tests cover every declared streamformat value for all eight producer protocols. The pinned model drives a matrix for all 30 directly declared protocol-option fields, rejecting every nonstring JSON kind through both public validation paths and checking required-field absence and empty values. WebRTC signaling tests check the complete strict enum, exact spelling, direction and external-reference rules. Separate URI and binding cases check description references and post-expansion constraints. The opt-in packaged Media model resolves its exact Endpoint/Message snapshots and common options without network access; compiled tests check all eleven protocol branches and strict streamformat enums. Inherited-option tests cover deployment booleans/defaults, endpoint and authorization array/item/known-member types across all eleven protocols, ordered address preservation, open extensions, absent/empty collections and deferred authorization/address obligations. The complete inherited Endpoint metadata matrix beyond these common protocol options has not been reviewed. Keep the whole block pending.

source.section: Media Endpoints Compatibility and Validation - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / Validation

requirements.text: A validator that recognizes a codec identifier MUST reject it when its known media kind conflicts with the attribute: a video codec in `audiocodec` or an audio codec in `videocodec`. The open vocabulary does not require a validator to recognize every codec identifier. A validator MUST NOT reject an unrecognized codec identifier solely because it does not recognize it.

review.note: Public tests reject each recognized opposite-kind video/audio identifier and accept unknown identifiers in both codec fields, including exact-case near matches. The runtime compares the finite recognized sets ordinally and otherwise retains the open vocabulary. This does not claim support for native encoding, carriage or receiver compatibility.

source.section: Media Endpoints Compatibility and Validation - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / Validation

requirements.text: A validator MUST NOT infer codec/protocol/`streamformat` incompatibility beyond the media-kind check and the protocol's declared `streamformat` enumeration. This draft defines no codec/format compatibility matrix. Its validation vectors exercise only the media-kind and declared `streamformat` checks; they do not assert cross-property codec/format compatibility.

review.note: The public materializer accepts independent AV1/PCMU declarations with all ten declared streamformat values across eight producer protocols, without a codec/format compatibility table. Recognized media-kind rejection and protocol-specific streamformat enums remain enforced separately. Acceptance proves only the Registry validation boundary, not that any receiver supports this media.

source.section: Media Endpoints Compatibility and Validation - Version 0.1 (Working Draft) / Runtime Compatibility

requirements.text: Compatibility depends on the receiving implementation's support for the advertised media and on protocol-specific behavior. A receiver MUST NOT treat successful xRegistry validation as proof that it can consume an endpoint. The provider is responsible for making its declarations accurate, and the receiver is responsible for deciding whether it supports them. This draft does not prescribe negotiation or failure signaling.

review.note: This constrains the actual receiver's interpretation of successful validation. Materialized Media Endpoints explicitly retain native session setup, producer input compatibility and supplied description interpretation as bounded deferred obligations, including absent addresses and undeployed declarations. Tests cover every defined protocol role, shared HTTP opt-in isolation, post-binding description checks and exact diagnostic limits. The Registry does not open media sessions or establish actual receiver support. No independent receiver execution establishes the required decision here; keep this obligation pending.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Notations and Scope

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" are to be interpreted as described in [RFC2119][rfc2119].

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Notations and Scope

requirements.text: Core defines entity types, IDs, labels and [default Versions](../../core/spec.md#default-version-of-a-resource). It also defines [`xref`](../../core/spec.md#cross-referencing-resources), [document view](../../core/spec.md#doc-flag), errors and request flags. The [HTTP binding](../../core/http.md#resource-metadata-vs-resource-document) defines methods, paths, `$details`, HTTP metadata headers and the wire representation of flags. [HTTP Semantics][http] and [HTTP Caching][cache] define HTTP processing. This document's requirements apply to federation resolvers; they neither require servers to implement an OPTIONAL Core API nor redefine CRUD operations.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Advertisement and Bootstrap

requirements.text: An HTTP advertisement has `name: "http"`, an absolute HTTP(S) Registry-root `endpoint`, and no parameters in this version. Its endpoint MUST NOT have embedded credentials, a query or a fragment. Unknown parameters on the selected advertisement MUST produce `unsupported_operation`.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Advertisement and Bootstrap

requirements.text: Selection, priorities, ties and implicit `xregurl` handling follow [Federation discovery](../federation/spec.md#discovery-and-binding-selection). If explicit HTTP advertisements coexist with `xregurl`, one endpoint MUST match `xregurl` exactly. `weburl` is a website, not an API fallback.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Advertisement and Bootstrap

requirements.text: A resolver bootstrapping from a catalog MUST read its model before interpreting the `categories` / `registries` collections. These catalog Resources have `hasdocument: false`: `xregurl`, `weburl` and any `federationprofiles` belong to their Version metadata. They are not a domain document to download.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Advertisement and Bootstrap

requirements.text: The chosen advertisement establishes a new Registry context. The resolver MUST discover the target's version, model and capabilities independently of the catalog. The resolver MUST NOT transfer catalog credentials, compatibility assumptions or label requirements to that target.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Registry Root and Version Discovery

requirements.text: The advertised root can have an arbitrary base path. For example, XID `/documents/main/assets/item` at `https://first.example.com/services/xreg/` is below `/services/xreg/documents/main/assets/item`, not `/documents/main/assets/item`. The root request uses the advertised root itself. Descendant construction MUST retain its complete base path, preserve case-sensitive Core IDs and encode URI path segments without double encoding. A resolver MUST NOT derive global entity identity by splitting an arbitrary URL.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Registry Root and Version Discovery

requirements.text: The HTTP binding's [`Link` with `rel=xregistry-root`](../../core/http.md#xregistry-root-http-header) identifies the serving Registry root when provided. A resolver MUST interpret it in the response context and apply the same locator policy as for other links. A relocated root does not silently authorize access to a different origin.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Registry Root and Version Discovery

requirements.text: Before interpreting model-dependent entities, the resolver MUST obtain `specversion` from the Registry representation. The version needs to be known and explicitly supported; successful JSON parsing does not establish compatibility. An unsupported version MUST produce `unsupported_version`. Where supported, Core's [`specversion` flag](../../core/spec.md#specversion-flag) requests a compatible representation. The resolver MUST verify the returned version and MUST NOT treat a silently ignored query parameter as successful negotiation.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Registry Root and Version Discovery

requirements.text: `GET B/capabilities` retrieves [enabled capabilities](../../core/spec.md#registry-capabilities). A resolver MAY use already inlined capabilities or request supported inlining. It MUST NOT assume that `filter`, `inline`, pagination, `/export` or writes are enabled.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Registry Root and Version Discovery

requirements.text: Before composing the selected view, the resolver MUST apply the shared [resolution-owner signal](../federation/spec.md#signaling-who-performs-resolution). `federation.resolution: "producer"` means read the view directly without traversing its catalog. An absent signal defaults to consumer resolution.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Registry Root and Version Discovery

requirements.text: When an OPTIONAL read API is unavailable, a resolver MAY use an equivalent already obtained representation, a supported inline request, or an advertised Core `/export` document. It MUST preserve the requested view and completeness. If no equivalent read exists, it MUST return `unsupported_operation`, not an invented empty entity or collection.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Native Read Mapping

requirements.text: The existing `GET B/export` convenience path, if supported, is precisely `GET B?doc&inline=*,capabilities,modelsource` with Core's flag semantics. It is not a federation-specific snapshot API. A resolver consuming an export MUST resolve document-local pointers within that returned document.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Metadata, Documents and Versions

requirements.text: Resource metadata, the Meta entity and Version metadata serve different purposes. A Resource's API-view `versionid` projects the default Version; [`meta.defaultversionid`](../../core/spec.md#defaultversionid-attribute) records which Version was selected. A resolver MUST NOT substitute lexical order, modification time, enumeration order or the greatest Version identifier for that default choice.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Metadata, Documents and Versions

requirements.text: An explicit Version target MUST select that exact, case-sensitive Version.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Metadata, Documents and Versions

requirements.text: When a multi-request operation needs both default metadata and bytes, the resolver SHOULD record the selected default Version ID and use its explicit Version URLs for subsequent requests.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Metadata, Documents and Versions

requirements.text: When claiming a consistent capture, the resolver MUST detect changes to the selection. A live Version can change without its Version ID changing.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Metadata, Documents and Versions

requirements.text: For document-bearing types, body `self` links to Resource/Version metadata include `$details` in API view, as specified by Core HTTP. Metadata-only types' `self` links MUST NOT include it. In document view, pointers are relative to the returned JSON and never include `$details`. The resolver MUST preserve Core navigation semantics rather than replace `self` with an endpoint label.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Metadata, Documents and Versions

requirements.text: Raw document reads use the domain media type and bytes. Core's `xRegistry-` headers carry accompanying metadata. `Content-Location`, when present on a default read, identifies the default Version as Core specifies. A zero-byte document is a successful empty byte sequence, not a missing document. Absent content and metadata-only types MUST remain distinguishable.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Metadata, Documents and Versions

requirements.text: Core `meta.xref` remains same-Registry, same Resource model type and one hop. Source IDs and navigation remain source-relative. A dangling target or a target that is itself an alias keeps Core's minimal source serialization. Document view MUST NOT expand an alias. Document-view requests below its `versions` preserve `cannot_doc_xref`. Federation MUST NOT reinterpret an absolute remote URL as `xref`.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Literal Label Selection

requirements.text: The common selector looks up an exact label key and compares its string value using Core's case-insensitive comparison. Labels are OPTIONAL, and their values can be empty. An absent label does not match an empty value. The resolver MUST NOT require a language label, impose NFC normalization, infer a locale from a category, or interpret the caller's `*` as a wildcard.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Literal Label Selection

requirements.text: A supported [HTTP filter](../../core/spec.md#filter-flag) can reduce the candidate set. The resolver MUST construct [Core dot notation](../../core/spec.md#dot-notation-in-filters) relative to the requested collection while preserving the selector's literal meaning. It MUST escape a literal wildcard using Core's backslash escape before URI encoding. It MUST quote label keys containing dot-notation operators using Core bracket notation. For example:

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Literal Label Selection

requirements.text: The common selector is narrower than Core's filter language. For example, the literal string `null` is not Core's missing-attribute expression. If literal commas, quotes, backslashes or other syntax cannot be represented unambiguously by a supported filter, the resolver MUST use local selection over an unfiltered collection rather than invent an escaping extension. URI encoding alone does not escape Core expression syntax.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Literal Label Selection

requirements.text: Even after requesting a filter, the resolver MUST apply the same literal comparison to the returned candidates. Core permits a server to ignore unsupported query flags, so a nonempty response does not establish that the server applied the filter.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Pagination and No-Filter Fallback

requirements.text: A resolver MUST process collection pages according to the [pagination specification](../../pagination/spec.md). It MUST follow each necessary `Link` with `rel=next`, resolve a relative link against the response request URL, and then use that link without editing its query. The resolver MUST NOT synthesize page numbers, reattach the original filter, or add `limit` to subsequent links. Pagination links are subject to the same credential and locator policy checks as redirects.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Pagination and No-Filter Fallback

requirements.text: To establish a unique label match, the resolver needs the complete relevant candidate set. A first-page match alone is insufficient. Complete enumeration with no match yields `not_found`; a second match yields `ambiguous`. An unavailable later page or a traversal limit MUST NOT become either a unique result or `not_found`. The resolver MUST report conflicting duplicates, changed declared totals or an incomplete capture, and MUST NOT silently merge them.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Pagination and No-Filter Fallback

requirements.text: If filtering is unavailable, the resolver MUST enumerate the relevant unfiltered collection and apply the common selector locally. This applies to no-code endpoints as well as API servers. It SHOULD use metadata already present in collection responses and avoid unrelated document downloads. Neither filtering nor inlining is a prerequisite for HTTP federation.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Pagination and No-Filter Fallback

requirements.text: An endpoint that advertises `pagination: false` normally supplies its complete collection in one response. If a next link is nevertheless returned, the resolver MUST NOT claim completeness until it has handled that link or reported the conflicting behavior. A collection `count` alone is not a replacement for the members or next links.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / HTTP Validators and Partial Content

requirements.text: An ETag validates one representation. It is opaque and supplies neither an XID, a Core epoch, a global content digest nor a Registry-wide revision pin. Metadata and document URLs, query variants and content codings can have different validators. The resolver MUST use the selected representation's validator with that representation, respecting `Vary`, cache directives and authorization scope.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / HTTP Validators and Partial Content

requirements.text: Conditional `GET` with `If-None-Match` uses HTTP's weak comparison to revalidate a cached response. A `304 Not Modified` response supplies no replacement body. The resolver MUST use an applicable stored response and update it according to RFC 9111 section 4.3.4. If no such response is available, the resolver needs an unconditional read or an explicit failure. `If-Modified-Since` and `Last-Modified` follow HTTP semantics and precedence, independently of Core timestamp semantics.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / HTTP Validators and Partial Content

requirements.text: `If-Match` uses strong comparison. A resolver MUST NOT use a weak ETag where a strong validator is needed.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / HTTP Validators and Partial Content

requirements.text: A resolver assembling partial bytes MUST apply RFC 9110 sections 13.1.5 and 14, validate `Content-Range` and representation identity, and account for every byte.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / HTTP Validators and Partial Content

requirements.text: A weak ETag is not valid for `If-Range`. An HTTP-date is usable there only under HTTP's strong-validator conditions. If an `If-Range` request returns a complete `200` response, the resolver MUST replace, not append to, its partial bytes.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / HTTP Validators and Partial Content

requirements.text: A `206` response is not a complete document merely because the transfer ended successfully. Missing ranges, truncation, changed validators or unverified joins MUST NOT produce a complete snapshot. A failed conditional read used to hold a capture stable, including `412`, yields `inconsistent_snapshot`.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / HTTP Validators and Partial Content

requirements.text: If a gateway transforms a representation, it MUST NOT forward the upstream strong ETag unchanged as the validator for different bytes. The gateway either preserves HTTP validator semantics for its own representation or omits that validator. Federation does not require preservation of the upstream ETag.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Redirects and Authorization Boundaries

requirements.text: Redirect processing follows RFC 9110 section 15.4 and Core HTTP. In particular, a Core external document can yield `303 See Other` with an empty body and `Location` matching `<RESOURCE>url`. The destination is domain content, not another Registry root. Other redirects can relocate an endpoint or representation. The resolver MUST distinguish these cases.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Redirects and Authorization Boundaries

requirements.text: Every redirect, advertised endpoint, next link and external document URL MUST pass caller policy. That policy includes scheme, destination, network access and redirect limits.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Redirects and Authorization Boundaries

requirements.text: The resolver MUST reject embedded credentials and MUST NOT automatically forward Authorization, cookies, client credentials or origin-specific conditional headers across a trust boundary.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Redirects and Authorization Boundaries

requirements.text: `401` and `403` MUST NOT cause silent retries against another advertisement, a public mirror, or a weaker authentication mode. Redirect loops and bounded traversal exhaustion produce `limit_exceeded`. Trust rejection produces `policy_denied`.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Live Capture and Errors

requirements.text: A source implementing the OPTIONAL [publication extension](../publication/spec.md#open-context-and-discovery) exposes a snapshot-specific Core root and an HTTP `Link` to its open-context record. Its absolute relation URI is `https://xregistry.io/workingdrafts/publication/context`. A pin-aware resolver MUST validate that record and its manifest, and keep subsequent URLs/pages in the same selected view. The extension does not add HTTP advertisement parameters or change the ordinary root/version discovery rules.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Live Capture and Errors

requirements.text: A context link identifies the snapshot but does not prove that API responses match it. A conforming producer MUST serve the checked graph, and a consumer claiming verified equivalence MUST check that correspondence.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Live Capture and Errors

requirements.text: Without this extension or another explicit snapshot guarantee, the resolver reports live access. It MUST NOT interpret an absent link as a frozen Registry.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Live Capture and Errors

requirements.text: A capture MUST record the following separately from Core IDs:

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Live Capture and Errors

requirements.text: It MUST distinguish a live, best-effort observation from a producer-guaranteed snapshot.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Live Capture and Errors

requirements.text: A resolver requiring a stronger guarantee MUST fail explicitly when the endpoint cannot provide it. If the necessary capture operation is unsupported, the outcome is `unsupported_operation`. If an attempted capture is inconsistent or incomplete, the outcome is `inconsistent_snapshot`.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Live Capture and Errors

requirements.text: For a multi-request capture, the resolver SHOULD recheck the default selection and the representations on which the capture depends.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Live Capture and Errors

requirements.text: If a default or representation changes, membership conflicts, or a page/byte sequence is interrupted, the capture can no longer be claimed as consistent. The resolver MUST report `inconsistent_snapshot` and discard that claim. It MAY start a new, separately identified operation; that fresh capture does not continue the previous operation with mixed old and new state.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Live Capture and Errors

requirements.text: The resolver MUST retain the HTTP status and any Core error detail. `api_not_found` is not an absent entity. The resolver MUST NOT use a generic `404` without enough context to invent an empty collection.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Scope and Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Scope and Conventions

requirements.text: Both schemas use JSON Schema Draft 2020-12. Their URNs identify this draft's schemas. They are not network retrieval endpoints. Producers and consumers MUST also implement the semantic constraints below. Schema validity alone does not establish Core model compliance or graph completeness.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Root and Storage Paths

requirements.text: The selected directory MUST contain `registry.json`. Its record MUST have `kind: "registry"` and `entity.xid: "/"`. Git's `parameters.path` and File's endpoint select this same directory. Neither adds an implicit extra directory.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Root and Storage Paths

requirements.text: Paths MUST be nonempty, normalized root-relative strings with `/` separators. They MUST NOT be absolute, contain empty components, `.` or `..` components, backslashes, NUL/control characters or surrogate code points. A consumer MUST NOT apply URI decoding. It MUST reject percent encodings that could be interpreted as separators or parent-path components, such as `%2f`, `%5c` and `%2e%2e`, as described in [Security and Conformance](#security-and-conformance). Portable paths MUST NOT contain `<>:"|?*`, end a component with a space or period, or use Windows device names such as `CON` and `NUL`. Other Unicode names and spaces within components are permitted. Platform path-length and access limits produce explicit errors.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Root and Storage Paths

requirements.text: Only external references allocate paths. An inline object occupies no path of its own. Metadata files describing different records or indexes MUST have distinct paths. Paths whose spellings differ only by case MUST NOT designate different mapping objects, because such mappings are ambiguous on case-insensitive filesystems. Several Versions MAY reference the same local document file using the same path and identical size/digest values. A producer MUST NOT also allocate a document path to a metadata record or index.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Root and Storage Paths

requirements.text: An ID MUST match the entire string against `[A-Za-z0-9_](?:[A-Za-z0-9_.~:@-]){0,127}`. Whitespace and trailing line terminators are not part of an ID. This grammar is independent of native filename rules.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Root and Storage Paths

requirements.text: If an implementation cannot represent the total path length or object count, it MUST report `limit_exceeded`. It MUST NOT truncate, normalize or replace an entity ID.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Record and Index Documents

requirements.text: All record and index documents MUST be UTF-8 JSON objects without a byte order mark, duplicate keys or non-JSON numbers. An inline record or index is part of its containing file and follows that file's JSON rules. Each record and index has `format: "xregistry-document-tree"` and `formatversion: "1"`, including an inline one. An unknown version MUST produce `unsupported_version`.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Record and Index Documents

requirements.text: | Kind | REQUIRED metadata in `entity`, in addition to `xid` |

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Record and Index Documents

requirements.text: All identifiers MUST agree with the full typed XID and model singular names. For example, `/documents/main/assets/item/versions/v1` identifies Version `v1` of asset `item`, not a Version globally named `v1`. `meta` and `versions` are literal Core path components. Group and Resource type names MUST be validated against the captured model. Resource and Version extension metadata MUST stay on the entity to which the model assigns it.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Record and Index Documents

requirements.text: Storage metadata MUST omit `self`, `shortself`, `metaurl` and `defaultversionurl`. It MUST also omit collection navigation/counts, nested entity collections, and Version `formatvalidated`, `compatibilityvalidated`, and their reason attributes. For a Resource model with `hasdocument: true`, it MUST NOT contain inlined `<RESOURCE>` or `<RESOURCE>base64` document content.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Record and Index Documents

requirements.text: An external reference has exactly `kind`, `xid`, `href`, `size` and `sha256`. An inline reference has exactly `kind`, `xid` and `inline`. A reference MUST use exactly one form. A reference that mixes fields of both forms, or an external reference that lacks `href`, `size` or `sha256`, is `invalid_package`. The external form names a file inside the selected root. It is unrelated to the `external` document descriptor kind.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Record and Index Documents

requirements.text: The reference's kind and XID MUST equal the referenced object's kind and XID. This metadata determines the object's role independently of its directory name, file extension or nesting position. Both `size` and `sha256` are REQUIRED in an external reference, including for zero-byte content.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Record and Index Documents

requirements.text: An inline target is a complete record or index document. It MUST have the same `format` and `formatversion` as the object that contains it. A mismatch is `invalid_package`. Inline references nest: an inline record or index can itself contain inline or external references. The root of this nesting is always the Registry record in `registry.json`, which is never an inline object. A complete Registry can therefore be stored in `registry.json` alone. Neither form can point outside the selected root. A metadata or collection reference has no URI form.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Record and Index Documents

requirements.text: `count` MUST equal the array length. An empty collection has `count: 0` and `entries: []`.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Record and Index Documents

requirements.text: Each entry MUST name an immediate member of this collection with the correct kind. References in both `entries` and `collections` MUST be strictly sorted by unsigned UTF-8 bytes of the full XID. Duplicate XIDs, case-insensitive sibling ID collisions and conflicting metadata storage allocations are invalid. These rules apply to inline and external references alike.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Record and Index Documents

requirements.text: Version indexes MUST include all locally owned Versions. An ordinary Resource MUST have at least one Version. Exactly one MUST have `isdefault: true`, matching its Meta's `defaultversionid`. Ancestors MUST exist in that same index and MUST NOT form cycles other than a root's self-reference. An alias MUST NOT own a Version index, including a fabricated empty index.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: The Registry's `entity.modelsource` MUST preserve the captured source, including `ximportresources` provenance. `entity.model`, when supplied, MUST be the actual full Core model, not a compact source relabeled as a full model. It MUST agree with the source, its resolved includes and the captured data.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: If the source contains [`$include` or `$includes`](../../core/model.md#includes-in-the-xregistry-model-data), the Registry record MUST also contain `resolvedmodelsource`. That object is the compact source after those includes were evaluated at capture time, but before implicit Core definitions and `ximportresources` expansion.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: This object MUST be self-contained and preserve [Resource type sharing](../../core/model.md#reuse-of-resource-definitions). `modelbase` MUST record the absolute base of the original source. Consumers MUST NOT re-fetch mutable includes during a read.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: The producer MUST establish equivalence between the captured source, resolved source and full model, when present. The original include directives remain available through [`entity.modelsource`](../../core/spec.md#modelsource-attribute). The resolved copy supplies storage context without establishing a second authoritative domain model.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: When includes are absent, `resolvedmodelsource` is OPTIONAL and, if present, MUST equal `entity.modelsource`. Model reads expose the original source, available resolved source and available full model.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: When interpreting a compact source, the consumer MUST apply Core defaults. It MUST NOT silently infer type sharing from structural similarity.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: Model results MUST preserve `modelbase` when present. Registry metadata envelopes retain `snapshot` and available `source` outside `entity`. These are capture context, not new Core attributes.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: `entity.capabilities` MUST describe access to this snapshot, not copy claims of upstream writes or filtering that the selected binding cannot implement. It MUST include Core's `available` map. The bindings are read-only.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: Captured source information MAY appear in the Registry record's `source` object with an absolute, credential-free `uri` and OPTIONAL `revision`. This is provenance, not the operation's Git pin, an entity XID, or an implicit base for document links.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: Each Version record MUST have exactly one `document` descriptor:

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: | `document.kind` | REQUIRED fields | Meaning |

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: For a local document, OPTIONAL `base` supplies the base URI used to resolve relative links inside that document. If the file was copied from an external location, OPTIONAL `origin` records that original location. The copied Version no longer has a `<RESOURCE>url`, because its document is now local.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: Both `base` and `origin`, when present, MUST be absolute URIs without embedded credentials.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: For `external`, `uri` MUST equal the Version's `<RESOURCE>url` exactly. A relative URI MUST have an explicit absolute `base` on this descriptor. Neither the containing file, catalog URL, Git repository URL nor `source.uri` is an implicit base.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: Known integrity is recorded in OPTIONAL paired `size` and `sha256` fields. If those fields are present and a consumer retrieves the content, it MUST check both. An external locator does not create a metadata alias.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: A Version referencing a document MUST identify either local bytes or an explicit external location. A missing referenced local file is an `invalid_package` error, not an empty document.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: A zero-byte local document MUST reference an actual zero-byte file, with `size: 0` and SHA-256 `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855`.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: Consumers MUST NOT decode, reserialize, newline-convert or replace binary and JSON bytes with an empty JSON wrapper. The Version's `contenttype`, if present, describes the bytes independently of the file's extension.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: For `hasdocument: false`, `document.kind` MUST be `none`. The Core document attributes do not apply. Consumers MUST preserve and validate ordinary model-admitted metadata named `<RESOURCE>`, `<RESOURCE>base64` or `<RESOURCE>url` as metadata. Consumers MUST NOT decode or dereference it as document content.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: A document request for such a Resource MUST produce `unsupported_operation`. A present zero-byte document is a different case.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: An exact read starts at the Registry record and follows the necessary typed collection indexes and selected child records. A Version read MUST NOT require unrelated domain bytes. A consumer MAY scan a collection index in memory; the format defines one complete index per collection, without pagination. Inline objects require no read beyond their containing file. Each followed external reference requires one read of its file.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: If a configured limit prevents a consumer from reading the complete index or the records needed for its request, the consumer MUST return `limit_exceeded`. It MUST NOT return the subset already read as a complete collection or use that subset to claim a unique match. The inline nesting depth within one file and the cumulative number of decoded metadata objects are such limits, in addition to file count and byte limits.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: Every materialized entity's `self` MUST be a JSON Pointer fragment locating that entity in the returned envelope. For example, a standalone Version has `self: "#/entity"`. Collection members begin at `#/entities/<ID>`. JSON Pointer tokens MUST escape `~` as `~0` and `/` as `~1`. URI-fragment encoding also applies. XIDs are not rewritten.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: Navigation MUST use a `#` JSON Pointer if and only if the referenced entity or collection is included in the output. A pointer into another record file is not document-local navigation.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: Registry and Group results inline all child metadata. Ordinary Resource results inline `meta` and all Version metadata. `metaurl`, `versionsurl`, and the Meta's `defaultversionurl` MUST point at those actual objects. Collection URLs and counts, when included, MUST describe the materialized maps, including empty maps. A producer MUST NOT also copy Default-Version attributes onto the Resource. No response in this format invents an API `self`.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: A standalone ordinary Meta result includes its selected default Version metadata in an envelope sibling, `related.defaultversion`. Its `defaultversionurl` MUST be `#/related/defaultversion`, and that Version's `self` MUST locate the same object. This explicit navigation closure avoids an absolute URL to an undefined native API or a dangling local pointer. An alias Meta has no such sibling and no default-Version attributes.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: Core [`xref`](../../core/spec.md#cross-referencing-resources) remains one-hop, same-Registry and same-Resource-model-type. Document-view Resource and Meta reads MUST leave aliases unexpanded, including dangling aliases and aliases whose targets are themselves aliases. Document-view alias Versions and alias Version collections MUST produce `unsupported_operation`, retaining Core's `cannot_doc_xref` diagnostic. No materialized target metadata can replace the source IDs.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: A logical document request to an alias MAY read the one-hop target's selected document, independently of document-view metadata. It MUST NOT follow a second alias. If no one-hop target document exists, the document request returns `not_found`. That does not make the source's minimal metadata invalid.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: Resource document requests use `meta.defaultversionid`. Explicit Version requests use exactly the requested Version ID. A snapshot revision, index position or highest Version string MUST NOT override the Core default.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: Resource label selection uses effective default-Version metadata, applying one-hop alias semantics where applicable. It does not inspect only the reduced storage Resource object. Selection MUST use the common literal comparator and complete collection, and return `not_found` or `ambiguous` as appropriate. The selected metadata result still obeys document-view alias suppression.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Completeness and Integrity

requirements.text: The root's `snapshot` object MUST contain `scope: "/"` and `completeness`, either `linked` or `offline-complete`. Both classes MUST contain the complete internal record/index/document graph. An `offline-complete` snapshot MUST NOT contain external-only domain documents. Captured resolved model material MUST permit offline interpretation in both classes.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Completeness and Integrity

requirements.text: A full-graph validator is OPTIONAL and checks every referenced object. A selective read validates only its visited path and MUST NOT claim an independent audit of unvisited graph closure.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Completeness and Integrity

requirements.text: Consumers MUST verify length and SHA-256 before parsing or returning each internally referenced file. An inline object has no separate size or digest. The bytes of its containing file cover it. Root bytes are captured once per operation. Their SHA-256 identifies that root serialization, not universal semantic identity or publisher authenticity.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Completeness and Integrity

requirements.text: Every external descendant is pinned transitively by its parent's reference, and every inline descendant by its containing file. Newly published states MUST be complete without replaying a prior snapshot. Shared content reuse does not relax closure.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Completeness and Integrity

requirements.text: Missing indexed objects, invalid kinds, invalid model types and inconsistent defaults are `invalid_package`. A requested absent XID is `not_found`. Descriptor mismatch is `integrity_error`. Observed mutation during a File read or loss of already selected Git objects is `inconsistent_snapshot`. Consumers MUST NOT return empty collections or retry another profile to hide these failures.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Security and Conformance

requirements.text: Producers MUST use regular files and real directories. They MUST NOT use symlinks, reparse points, parent paths, device names, alternate data streams or OS aliases.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Security and Conformance

requirements.text: Consumers MUST enforce selected-root containment before reading bytes.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Security and Conformance

requirements.text: Bindings define access to the selected root and race protection. Consumers MUST impose explicit file, byte and traversal limits. Traversal limits cover inline nesting depth, counted within each containing file, and the cumulative number of decoded metadata objects. Integrity checks do not ensure authorized filesystem access or establish publisher trust. Before retrieving an external URI, the consumer MUST check that destination against its access policy and use only credentials authorized for that destination.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Executable Example

requirements.text: [`mapping_examples.py`](tools/mapping_examples.py) provides offline parsing, schema/semantic validation, selective reads, document-view assembly and an OPTIONAL local Git object-store reader. It uses the common `FederationError`, XID validation, label selection and Resource type helper. It does not fetch repositories or external documents.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Scope and Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Advertisement and File URI

requirements.text: `binding` MUST be `file`. The `endpoint` MUST be an absolute [RFC8089](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8089) file URI identifying the selected directory. It MUST NOT contain credentials, a query or fragment. An absent authority or `localhost` means local access. Other authorities, including UNC (Universal Naming Convention) servers, MUST produce `policy_denied` in this binding. A separately named extension can define a remote filesystem access policy. An implementation MUST NOT infer such a policy from this profile.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Advertisement and File URI

requirements.text: | `layout` | REQUIRED, exactly `document-tree` or `oci-layout`. |

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Advertisement and File URI

requirements.text: | `reference` | REQUIRED for `oci-layout`, forbidden for `document-tree`. An OCI tag or `sha256` digest under the OCI binding. |

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Advertisement and File URI

requirements.text: An unknown selected parameter MUST produce `unsupported_operation`. The resolver MUST NOT infer a layout from the directory's files or switch layouts after a failure. When an OCI layout contains several snapshots, `reference` selects the root; directory-entry order does not.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Advertisement and File URI

requirements.text: The first example selects an absolute Windows drive path; the second selects an absolute POSIX path. If a host cannot interpret the selected native path, it MUST report `unsupported_operation` rather than reinterpret the path as a different filesystem root. Windows drive-relative paths and older `C|` spellings are not accepted.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Advertisement and File URI

requirements.text: URI parsing MUST:

requirements.text: After decoding, URI parsing MUST reject:

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Advertisement and File URI

requirements.text: These rejections apply where applicable. A single terminal slash is permitted for a directory URI. Decoding a second time MUST NOT turn a literal percent sequence into traversal.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Layout Selection and Reads

requirements.text: For `document-tree`, the selected directory MUST contain `registry.json`. The [directory mapping format](mapping.md#record-and-index-documents) defines the record and index schemas and exact-byte representation. It also defines model and capabilities reads, label selection, Core document view, defaults and `xref`. Every internal `href` is [relative to this directory](mapping.md#root-and-storage-paths), including references in nested records. There is no implicit `xregistry` directory.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Layout Selection and Reads

requirements.text: Both layout modes carry the selected Registry's [resolution-owner capability](../federation/spec.md#signaling-who-performs-resolution). A consumer MUST NOT repeat catalog resolution for a `producer` view. Absence of the signal retains the default consumer-side process.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Layout Selection and Reads

requirements.text: For `oci-layout`, consumers MUST use the [OCI binding's image-layout selection](oci.md#22-image-layout-selection) and [descriptor-graph rules](oci.md#4-containment-and-range-shards).

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Layout Selection and Reads

requirements.text: External domain-document links remain explicit. Retrieving one requires separate caller authorization, URI-base handling and integrity checking. Relative links MUST NOT silently become paths outside the selected root.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Containment and Concurrent Changes

requirements.text: The caller MUST authorize a filesystem boundary before the resolver opens the selected directory. The resolver MUST verify that the directory is within that boundary, then constrain all internal reads to that selected root. A mere string prefix test is insufficient: `root-other` is not inside `root`.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Containment and Concurrent Changes

requirements.text: The resolver MUST check every directory component, including components of the selected root, for symlinks and Windows reparse points. Internal objects MUST be regular files. Consumers MUST NOT follow symlinks, junctions, mount-point reparse records or other path redirections. Consumers MUST NOT read device files, pipes, sockets and alternate data streams as snapshot content. Case folding, short-name aliases and reserved OS names MUST NOT select a different internal object. Git/File storage portability does not permit case-insensitive Core XID lookup.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Containment and Concurrent Changes

requirements.text: Before interpreting bytes, consumers MUST establish that the actual opened objects are contained within the selected root. When a hostile process can change paths concurrently, containment requires directory/handle-relative no-follow access, equivalent platform protection, or a private immutable copy made before resolution. Checking `realpath` before opening a mutable pathname is insufficient. Hard links also provide no immutability guarantee: a writer outside the directory can still change shared content.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Containment and Concurrent Changes

requirements.text: For document-tree reads, consumers MUST capture the root record once and retain its exact-byte SHA-256. Descendant references pin every consumed external record, index and document. The bytes of the containing file pin each inline record and index. For OCI reads, consumers MUST pin the selected root digest and verify every descriptor under the OCI binding.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Containment and Concurrent Changes

requirements.text: Consumers MUST detect changes during open/read operations, short reads and changes to already captured selection state. An observed change MUST produce `inconsistent_snapshot`. A stable descriptor mismatch is `integrity_error`.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Containment and Concurrent Changes

requirements.text: If the environment cannot guarantee a coherent read, the consumer MUST either capture a private stable snapshot or explicitly report the lack of an immutable filesystem pin. Consistent file timestamps alone are insufficient: the consumer MUST NOT use them to advertise an atomic capture of a live upstream Registry.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Containment and Concurrent Changes

requirements.text: A producer SHOULD construct a complete snapshot separately and then make it available atomically using platform-appropriate synchronization. Updating files in place while readers traverse them does not establish completeness. Retaining immutable old files can allow readers with an older pinned root to complete without mixing revisions.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Containment and Concurrent Changes

requirements.text: Origin MUST identify the file URI, layout and selected root hash/digest, plus the presence or absence of an immutable filesystem snapshot guarantee. It MUST NOT replace entity XIDs, Resource Version IDs or Core navigation.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Errors and Conformance

requirements.text: A producer MUST provide a complete snapshot in one explicitly declared layout. A consumer MUST implement that layout's metadata/document semantics and all applicable containment and consistency rules. A consumer MUST identify which layouts it implements. Support for one does not imply the other. An offline-complete claim additionally requires the selected layout's offline content closure.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Scope and Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Advertisement

requirements.text: `binding` MUST be `git`. `endpoint` MUST be an absolute HTTPS repository URL with a host, and MUST NOT contain credentials, a query or fragment. Native Git, SSH, `file:`, `git+https:` and remote-helper transports are not part of this binding. A web page URL is not implicitly a repository.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Advertisement

requirements.text: | `revision` | REQUIRED string: full Git ref or complete SHA-1/SHA-256 object ID. |

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Advertisement

requirements.text: | `path` | OPTIONAL portable relative directory. Default `xregistry`. `""` selects the repository tree root. |

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Advertisement

requirements.text: A full ref MUST begin with `refs/` and pass Git's [`check-ref-format`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-check-ref-format) rules. For example, `refs/heads/main` and `refs/tags/release-1` are valid. The resolver MUST NOT accept:

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Advertisement

requirements.text: A nonempty `path` MUST use `/`-separated portable directory components. Components MUST be 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `-` or `.`, begin with a letter, digit or `_`, and MUST NOT end in `.`. A component MUST NOT have a case-insensitive Windows device name (`CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1` through `COM9`, or `LPT1` through `LPT9`, including before an extension). Leading/trailing separators, empty components, `.` and `..`, backslashes, colon/drive names, URI escapes and OS aliases are forbidden. This constraint applies to the storage root locator, not to Core entity IDs.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Advertisement

requirements.text: An unknown selected parameter MUST produce `unsupported_operation`. Authentication and endpoint authorization are supplied by caller policy, never by embedded metadata credentials.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Revision and Object Selection

requirements.text: The resolver MUST establish one repository context using the selected HTTPS endpoint and the caller's access policy. It can fetch into an isolated object store, but MUST NOT create or execute a working tree. Any acquisition MUST be explicit, bounded and complete for the requested operation.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Revision and Object Selection

requirements.text: The resolver MUST resolve `revision` once. Lightweight tags and branches select their referenced object. The resolver MUST peel annotated tags to a commit. An object that cannot resolve to a commit is invalid selection input.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Revision and Object Selection

requirements.text: The resolver MUST record the resulting complete commit OID and retain that pin for the entire operation, including model, label and document reads. If the original ref moves, that movement MUST NOT change the pin or trigger a second resolution. Consumers MUST NOT substitute a currently reachable or newer commit when the selected commit is inaccessible.
