requirements.text: Native bindings MUST distinguish these document-view serializations from the logical operation that retrieves an alias's target document under Core. A resolver MUST report an unsupported view or alias-Version document view, and MUST NOT silently convert it to a different view.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Representations

requirements.text: A binding offering API-view results MUST define actually retrievable Core-conforming `self` and navigation URLs. An implementation-defined URI with no retrieval contract is insufficient. An OPTIONAL HTTP facade MUST conform separately to [Core HTTP](../../core/http.md). Neither `oci://` locators nor UA NodeIds become Core XIDs.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Representations

requirements.text: Formats MUST preserve extension attributes and domain bytes. A zero-byte document is present content and MUST NOT be replaced by `{}`, `null` or a missing document. Binary documents MUST NOT pass through text conversion.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: Every snapshot MUST have a complete internal containment graph. The completeness class determines how it handles external content:

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: - A linked snapshot MAY retain explicit external document references.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: - An offline-complete snapshot MUST also contain the declared xRegistry document content in its selected scope and the model material needed to interpret that content.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: The producer MUST identify the scope and completeness class. Missing internally referenced data is an invalid package in either class.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: Offline completeness does not mean copying all cataloged Registries or discovering arbitrary links inside every domain document. External reference bases and known content integrity descriptors MUST survive packaging. Materializing external content requires preserving its actual bytes.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: An immutable revision MUST remain pinned throughout an operation. A moving tag, branch or mutable directory name is not a revision pin. A resolver MUST report a live HTTP or UA endpoint without a snapshot guarantee as live, not as an atomic snapshot. Revision identifiers MUST NOT be substituted for Resource Version IDs.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: Digests identify exact bytes; they do not establish semantic equality. Equivalent publications can therefore have different digests. New snapshots MAY reuse unchanged content and subtrees, but MUST be readable without replaying older snapshots.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: The [publication extension](../publication/spec.md) adds named channels over these snapshots. A resolver selects a moving channel once per operation and retains the selected immutable context across collection pages, entity reads and document retrieval. Missing data in that context MUST NOT trigger a refresh or lookup against another channel head. Opening the channel again is a separately identified operation.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Errors

requirements.text: When an underlying Core error or transport diagnostic is available, the resolver error MUST retain it without exposing credentials. A resolver MUST NOT return an incomplete retrieval as a successful empty collection. Core's dangling-alias exception still applies.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Security Considerations

requirements.text: Catalog data and package contents are untrusted input. Discovery is not an authorization grant. A resolver MUST apply caller policy before contacting endpoints, following redirects, reading local paths or retrieving external documents. A resolver MUST scope credentials to the authenticated destination, and MUST NOT forward them merely because a catalog entry or redirect names it.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Security Considerations

requirements.text: Resolvers MUST bound traversal depth, request count and aggregate bytes, detect discovery/redirect cycles, and report when a bound is exhausted. SHA-256 integrity does not authenticate a publisher. Signature and provenance policies are separate from containment completeness. Git readers MUST NOT execute repository content. Filesystem readers MUST enforce containment, including symlinks and reparse points.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Conformance

requirements.text: A federation resolver MUST implement the resolution-owner signaling, selection, context, Core semantics, representations and failures defined above and identify each binding it implements. Conformance to one binding does not imply support for another.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Conformance

requirements.text: A snapshot producer MUST identify its format, scope and linked or offline-complete class and produce a complete internal graph. An OPTIONAL API facade requires separate protocol-binding conformance.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Conformance

requirements.text: Tests MUST distinguish full graph validation from selective lookup. A validator walking everything does not demonstrate efficient selective resolution. Run the shared and binding suites from the repository root:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.1. Thing Descriptions and Thing Models

requirements.text: A Thing Model (TM) is a JSON-LD 1.1 document conforming to [WoT-TM 1.1][WoT-TM-1.1]. It describes an abstract class of Things and typically omits `href` values from its forms. Thing Models are reusable: a concrete Thing Description MAY extend or compose one or more Thing Models through WoT `tm:extends` and `tm:ref` mechanisms or JSON-LD `@type` declarations.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.1. Thing Descriptions and Thing Models

requirements.text: Although both document classes use JSON-LD and share part of its vocabulary, a WoT Registry MUST treat them as distinct Resource types. Their intended use, validation rules and lifecycles differ.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.2. Relationship to Other xRegistry Specs

requirements.text: - A Thing Description's `forms` array describes protocol bindings that MAY also be represented as `endpoint` Resources. See [Section 6.3](#63-thing-description-to-endpoint-registry).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.2. Relationship to Other xRegistry Specs

requirements.text: - A Thing Description's property/action/event data schemas (declared inline via WoT data-schema vocabulary) MAY reference external schemas managed by the xRegistry Schema Registry. See [Section 6.4](#64-thing-description-to-schema-registry).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.2. Relationship to Other xRegistry Specs

requirements.text: - A Thing Description MAY reference one or more Thing Models from which it is derived. See [Section 6.1](#61-thing-description-to-thing-model).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.2. Relationship to Other xRegistry Specs

requirements.text: This specification does not require the Registry to resolve or validate these cross-references. An implementation MAY check that a referent exists, but it still stores and serves the document when a referent is absent. A Consumer composing a TD from Thing Models or binding an affordance to an endpoint depends on those references independently of the Registry's checks.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Each Version of a `thingdescription` or `thingmodel` Resource holds a complete WoT document, stored without rewriting its bytes. A Resource's `wotid` and registry Resource id are stable across compatible revisions. `wotid` is declared with [`matchversions`][xRegistry matchversions]. A registry MUST reject a Version that supplies a different `wotid`. A Thing Model's major version MUST be part of its `wotid`. A breaking change MUST use a new `wotid` and a new Resource ([Section 5.1.1](#511-breaking-changes-and-successor-identifiers)).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Thing Model Resources and Thing Description Resources MUST use Core [`versionmode`][Core versionmode] `semver` and [`singleversionroot`][Core singleversionroot] `true`. Core orders each Resource's [`ancestorid`][Core ancestorid] lineage by SemVer precedence and forbids multiple roots with these aspects. The assignment rules for the corresponding authored fields are:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: | TM | `version.model` | `versionid` MUST equal the authored value verbatim. | The registry MUST assign `0.0.0-N`. |

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: | TD | `version.instance` | `versionid` MUST equal the authored value verbatim. | The registry MUST assign `0.0.0-N`. |

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: For either Resource type, the registry MUST inspect the authored field without modifying the stored document. The original authored field MUST NOT be rewritten, including when absent or non-SemVer.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: A valid authored value is SemVer 2.0.0 without build metadata and fits Core's 128-character [id constraint][Core id constraints]. SemVer build metadata (`+build`) MUST be rejected as `invalid-version`, since `+` is not allowed by Core's id constraints. An authored SemVer value that exceeds Core's 128-character id limit MUST also be rejected under those constraints.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: `N` is the lowest positive integer whose complete id is not already used in the Resource. The registry MUST assign an omitted `versionid`. A supplied `versionid` MUST equal the authored or generated assignment, or the registry MUST reject it as `version-mismatch`. A supplied id that violates Core's id grammar MUST be rejected as `invalid-version` before this comparison. Core requires an immutable, unique [`versionid`][Core versionid]. This extension defines the assignment in place of its default [Version ID algorithm][Core Version IDs].

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: The Registry MUST perform assignment and creation atomically with respect to concurrent writes, so two writes cannot claim the same generated id.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Each Thing Model Version and each Thing Description Version MUST have a server-set, read-only `versionorigin`. Its value MUST be `authored` when the Version's id comes from a SemVer authored field, and `generated` otherwise.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Client-supplied `versionorigin` MUST be ignored under Core's [read-only attribute rules][Core read-only rules]. The model initializes the attribute to `authored`. When the registry assigns a generated id, it MUST replace that initial value with `generated`. The model default does not replace the assignment rules above.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Generated ids are prereleases. They MUST NOT be used as minimum-version floors, even when the target Version is absent.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: For Thing Models, the Resource-level [`compatibility`][Core compatibility] attribute in `meta` MUST default to `backward`. A backward-compatible TM revision MUST NOT remove or narrow an affordance, a data schema or an `@type`, and MUST NOT introduce a new mandatory member. Narrowing includes reducing the accepted values or operations of an existing member. These constraints apply to every earlier Version in the Resource's Core [`ancestorid`][Core ancestorid] lineage.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: A Registry MAY validate this domain-specific compatibility rule through Core's [`validatecompatibility`][Core validatecompatibility] capability. Core's [`strictvalidation`][Core strictvalidation] rules still apply. Absence of a domain validator does not permit a Producer to publish an incompatible revision under the same `wotid`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: When [`defaultversionsticky`][Core defaultversionsticky] is false, Core's SemVer [`versionmode`][Core versionmode] orders the default. A late `1.0.1` after `1.1.0` MUST NOT replace `1.1.0` as the default. A sticky default MUST be honoured.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: For migration, an operator SHOULD inventory every Version and root of a legacy Resource before enabling this model. Compatible TM roots SHOULD be imported into one SemVer-ordered lineage with ids assigned by the rules above. Incompatible roots MUST be placed in distinct Resources with distinct major-version `wotid`s.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: The operator SHOULD inventory legacy TD Resources with manually assigned `versionid`s and re-import them with ids assigned from `version.instance` or generated by these rules.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Where changing an old immutable id or authored document would be necessary, the operator SHOULD preserve the legacy Resource outside the conforming collection and import a copy under a new registry Resource id.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: The operator MUST preserve authored bytes, record old-to-new registry paths for callers holding pins, and establish a valid default before enabling `singleversionroot`. An operator MUST NOT claim that an unresolved multiple-root Resource conforms to this model.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.4. Document Store

requirements.text: An xRegistry-unaware WoT consumer MAY use a Version's `self` URL with the `$details` suffix removed, or its `shortself` URL, as a regular WoT TD or TM URL. The unchanged `self` URL returns xRegistry metadata rather than the document. The metadata and document URLs are not interchangeable.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.1. Notational Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2119).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.1. Notational Conventions

requirements.text: For clarity, OPTIONAL attributes (specification-defined and extensions) are OPTIONAL for clients to use, but the servers' responsibility will vary. Server-unknown extension attributes MUST be silently stored in the backing datastore. Specification-defined, and server-known extension, attributes MUST generate an error if the corresponding feature is not supported or enabled.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.1. Notational Conventions

requirements.text: However, as with all attributes, if accepting the attribute results in a bad state (such as exceeding a size limit or resulting in a security issue), then the server MAY choose to reject the request.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.1. Notational Conventions

requirements.text: In the pseudo JSON format snippets `?` means the preceding attribute is OPTIONAL, `*` means the preceding attribute MAY appear zero or more times, and `+` means the preceding attribute MUST appear at least once. The presence of the `#` character means the remaining portion of the line is a comment. Whitespace characters in the JSON snippets are used for readability and are not normative.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.2. Terminology / 2.2.1. Thing Description

requirements.text: The TD's `version.instance` carries its revision, including breaking major revisions. A major revision remains under the same `id`, `wotid`, and Resource. If a Resource declares the [`compatibility`][xRegistry compatibility] attribute, all its Versions MUST adhere to that policy. A TD that identifies a different Thing MUST use that Thing's `id` and a corresponding Resource. See [Section 1.3](#13-versioning).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.2. Terminology / 2.2.3. WoT Identifier

requirements.text: A WoT identifier is held in the `wotid` attribute. It is distinct from the xRegistry `thingdescriptionid`/`thingmodelid`, which identifies the Resource within a Registry. The two MAY hold the same string when the authored identifier satisfies xRegistry's id grammar. Most do not: a URL such as `https://fabrikam.example/things/lamp-42` is not a legal xRegistry id. The model therefore keeps them as separate attributes rather than reusing the Resource id. [Section 5.1](#51-wot-identifiers-and-registry-ids) defines how the two relate.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry

requirements.text: Implementations of this specification MAY include additional extension attributes, including the `*` attribute of type `any`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.1. Thing Description Groups

requirements.text: Every Thing Description (the `thingdescription` Resource) MUST reside inside a Thing Description Group.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: Thing Description Resources MUST use Core [`versionmode`][Core versionmode] value `semver` and [`singleversionroot`][Core singleversionroot] value `true`, as specified in [Section 1.3](#13-versioning). Core derives `ancestorid` by SemVer precedence and enforces one root ([`ancestorid`][Core ancestorid]).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: The Version-level `versionorigin` attribute is REQUIRED, read-only, and uses the strict enumeration `authored` or `generated`. The `versionid` is assigned from `version.instance` when that member is SemVer without build metadata. Otherwise it is the lowest free `0.0.0-N` id. The original document bytes, including `version.instance`, are not rewritten.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: The `format` attribute of a `thingdescription` Resource Version MUST be `"JSON-LD/1.1"`. [model.json](model.json) declares the `format` enumeration as `strict`, so a registry rejects any other value rather than merely discouraging it.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: The `contenttype` of a `thingdescription` document MUST be `application/td+json` per [WoT-TD 1.1 §12.1][WoT-TD-1.1], or another media type the deployment has explicitly registered for WoT documents.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: `contenttype` is client-supplied and determines the media type used to serve the stored bytes through the document view ([Section 1.4](#14-document-store)). A Registry MUST NOT serve a stored document under a client-supplied media type that would interpret it as active content, such as `text/html`, `image/svg+xml` or `application/xhtml+xml`. A Registry MUST either reject such a write or serve the document under the media type this section requires.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: WoT tooling dereferences a Version's document-view URL directly. For documents it did not author, a Registry SHOULD additionally return `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` or serve them from an origin separate from any Registry user interface. See [Section 7](#7-security).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: The `wotid` attribute is REQUIRED and holds the document's authored WoT identifier, distinct from the `thingdescriptionid`. See [Section 5.1](#51-wot-identifiers-and-registry-ids). The OPTIONAL `derivedfrom` attribute lists the `wotid`s of the Thing Models this Thing Description extends or composes. It is a producer-supplied index rather than an authority over the document's own references, as [Section 5.2](#52-preserving-customer-documents) describes.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: All Versions of a single Thing Description Resource MUST adhere to the semantic rules of the Thing Description's [`compatibility`][Core compatibility] attribute, if specified.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: Implementations of this specification SHOULD use the xRegistry default algorithm for generating new `versionid` values.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: The default Version is the one served when no Version is named. It MUST be determined by the xRegistry Core rules, including the Resource's [`defaultversionsticky`][Core defaultversionsticky] setting. A deployment MAY use that setting to pin the default to a Version other than the newest. This specification does not redefine default-Version selection. See [Version IDs][xRegistry version-ids] for more information.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.3. Thing Model Groups

requirements.text: Every Thing Model (i.e. the `thingmodel` Resource) MUST reside inside a Thing Model Group.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.4. Thing Model Resources

requirements.text: The `format` attribute of a `thingmodel` Resource Version MUST be `"JSON-LD/1.1"`, enforced by the same `strict` enumeration used for `thingdescription`. The `contenttype` MUST be `application/tm+json` per [WoT-TM 1.1 §12.2][WoT-TM-1.1], or another media type the deployment has explicitly registered for WoT documents, and the same constraint on serving stored bytes as active content applies as in [Section 4.2](#42-thing-description-resources).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.4. Thing Model Resources

requirements.text: The `compatibility`, `versionid`, `versionorigin` and [`ancestorid`][Core ancestorid] rules for Thing Models are defined in [Section 1.3](#13-versioning), subject to Core's [`compatibility`][Core compatibility] and [`versionid`][Core versionid] semantics. The Version-level `versionorigin` is a REQUIRED string with the strict enumeration `authored` or `generated`, and is read-only. The model declares `compatibility` under `metaattributes`, with `required: true` and `default: backward`, as Core requires for an attribute with a default.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.4. Thing Model Resources

requirements.text: The `wotid` attribute is REQUIRED on a `thingmodel` and holds the document's authored WoT identifier, which is distinct from the `thingmodelid`. Where a Thing Model extends another via a `tm:extends` link relation, or references one via `tm:ref`, or composes one via `tm:submodel`, the referenced Thing Models' `wotid`s SHOULD be listed in `derivedfrom`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.5. Formats / 4.5.1. WoT Thing Description

requirements.text: - The document's `@context` MUST include `https://www.w3.org/2022/wot/td/v1.1`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.5. Formats / 4.5.1. WoT Thing Description

requirements.text: - A URI-reference pointing to a TD MAY use a JSON-Pointer ([RFC 6901](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6901)) fragment to deep-link into a particular property, action, or event affordance, e.g. `…/thingdescriptions/lamp-42#/properties/status`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.5. Formats / 4.5.2. WoT Thing Model

requirements.text: - The document's `@context` MUST include `https://www.w3.org/2022/wot/td/v1.1` and the document's top-level `@type` MUST include `tm:ThingModel`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: Tools and autonomous agents need explicit metadata to choose among documents describing similar Things rather than inferring their provenance from titles or naming conventions. Both `thingdescription` and `thingmodel` Resources carry the following OPTIONAL attributes:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: A Consumer choosing between candidate Thing Models SHOULD prefer, in order:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: If the choice remains open, the Consumer SHOULD prefer the document whose `canonicalurl` it already trusts. [model.json](model.json) declares the `maturity` enumeration as `strict`, so a Registry rejects values outside this set. A Consumer that nonetheless encounters one, for example from a federated Registry, MUST NOT rank it above `Experimental`. This specification defines no precedence for it.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: These attributes are advisory and unverified assertions by the Resource's writer about the document's origin and maturity. This specification defines no mechanism for a Registry to validate a `publisher` or `standardsbody` claim. A Registry MUST NOT be assumed to have validated one.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: A Consumer MUST NOT treat these attributes as authenticated provenance. The preference order only breaks ties among documents the Consumer already trusts, whether by Group, writer identity or an out-of-band signature. It MUST NOT be used to establish trust in a document from an untrusted writer.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: One `wotid` MAY legitimately match several Resources written by different parties ([Section 5.3](#53-lookup)), so a Consumer can face this choice. See also [Section 7](#7-security).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: These attributes are also not part of a document's semantic identity. A registry MUST NOT treat two documents as the same document because their provenance attributes agree, nor as different documents because they differ: identity is `wotid` alone ([Section 5.1](#51-wot-identifiers-and-registry-ids)).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: These identifiers serve a similar purpose but follow different grammars. `https://fabrikam.example/things/lamp-42` is not a valid entity id or `xid` component. An `xid` is not what a Thing author writes. Where an authored identifier satisfies the id grammar, a client MAY use it as the Resource id. A Registry cannot rely on that choice.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: A deployment MAY derive its Resource ids from `wotid` values by a convention of its own. The [OpenUSD Artifact Registry][OpenUSD Draft] working draft defines one such construction. No convention is mandated by this specification, and a Consumer MUST NOT assume that an id it did not assign was produced by one.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: A `wotid` MUST NOT encode a compatible revision of the document it names. A Thing Model's major version MUST be included in that stable identity, for example `urn:fabrikam:lamp:v1` or `https://fabrikam.example/tm/lamp/v1`. Minor and patch revisions are carried by `versionid` and `version.model`, not appended to the identifier. No particular spelling of the major-version token is mandated.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: When a document is revised compatibly, its `wotid` and Resource id MUST remain unchanged, and a new Version is created under the same Resource. A Thing Model breaking revision uses a distinct major-version `wotid` as specified in [Section 5.1.1](#511-breaking-changes-and-successor-identifiers). A Thing Description major revision remains under its existing `id` and `wotid`. A new TD identifier names a different concrete Thing.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: A `wotid` is REQUIRED, and the rule for populating it depends on the document:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: - Where the document carries an `id` member, `wotid` MUST equal it verbatim. A registry that parses the stored document MUST reject a write whose `wotid` differs from that `id`, rather than storing two identities for one document. A registry that does not parse the document cannot detect the disagreement. Both types of registry MUST NOT rewrite either value to resolve the disagreement, because [Section 5.2](#52-preserving-customer-documents) forbids editing the document.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: - Where the document carries no `id` member — which [WoT-TD 1.1][WoT-TD-1.1] permits for TDs served from a fixed URL, and which is common for TMs — the Producer MUST supply a `wotid` at write time, and that supplied value is thereafter the document's identity in this registry.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: - A registry MUST reject a write that supplies neither an `id` member nor a `wotid`, rather than inventing one, because an invented identifier is not stable across registries.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids / 5.1.1. Breaking Changes and Successor Identifiers

requirements.text: A breaking Thing Model change MUST use a new major-version `wotid` and a distinct Resource. The predecessor's `wotid` MUST NOT be modified. A major Thing Description revision remains a Version of the same concrete Thing under the same `id`, `wotid`, and Resource. A distinct TD `id` and `wotid` identify a different concrete Thing, not a breaking revision of the existing one.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids / 5.1.1. Breaking Changes and Successor Identifiers

requirements.text: The predecessor Resource MUST be marked with Core's [`deprecated`][xRegistry deprecated] attribute, whose `alternative` MUST be the successor Resource's URL. Its Versions MUST remain retrievable. Deprecation alone MUST NOT cause the resolver to redirect a reference to the successor. A Consumer MAY inspect the successor and explicitly choose to adopt its different identity.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.2. Preserving Customer Documents

requirements.text: - A registry MUST store the WoT document byte-for-byte as supplied, apart from transformations the client explicitly requested.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.2. Preserving Customer Documents

requirements.text: - A registry MUST NOT rewrite the document's `id` member, its `links[].href` values, its `tm:extends` or `tm:ref` targets, or any other identifier internal to the document, into registry-specific identifiers.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.2. Preserving Customer Documents

requirements.text: - A retrieval of a stored Version through the document view MUST return the exact bytes supplied, as the xRegistry Core document view already requires. Re-serializing the document — reordering members, re-indenting, or normalizing its JSON-LD — is not permitted.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.2. Preserving Customer Documents

requirements.text: `derivedfrom` is a producer-supplied *index* of the document's references, not an authority over them. A registry MAY verify that it matches the `tm:extends`, `tm:submodel`, `tm:ref` and `links[].rel="type"` targets in the stored document, and SHOULD reject a write where the two disagree. Where a registry does not verify, the document is authoritative.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.2. Preserving Customer Documents

requirements.text: When making a trust, allow-list or compliance decision about a document's lineage, a Consumer MUST derive that lineage from the document itself and MUST NOT rely on `derivedfrom` alone.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: An implementation SHOULD serve this query in time that does not grow with collection size, in practice by indexing `wotid` on both `thingdescriptions` and `thingmodels`. A linear scan for each reference would make TD composition slower as the collection grows.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: A `wotid` SHOULD be unique within a Group, so that a Group-scoped query for one identifies a single Resource. Across Groups a `wotid` MAY repeat — the same vendor TM legitimately appears in two tenants' Groups. A registry-wide query MAY therefore match more than one Resource. A caller that needs exactly one narrows the query by naming the Group.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: A Registry-wide query MUST return every matching Resource rather than an arbitrary one of them. [Section 4.6](#46-provenance-and-selection-metadata) governs how a Consumer chooses among them.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: A request to the Resource URL without a Version returns the Core default, even when [`defaultversionsticky`][Core defaultversionsticky] is true. A registry MUST serve that default when no Version is named.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: For reference resolution, a resolver MUST use [Section 5.4](#54-versioned-reference-resolution), not lexical id order, publication time or an assumption that the default satisfies the reference.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: Callers SHOULD NOT fold the identifier and version into one opaque string. When carrying both through a transport, such as message headers, a caller SHOULD use separate values, for example a `wotid` header and a `versionid` header, rather than a single compound token like `urn:fabrikam:lamp@3` that every recipient has to take apart. The identifier stays a WoT identifier, and the version stays a `versionid` the recipient can put straight into a URL.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: A reference MAY carry a minimum SemVer, called its floor, but MUST NOT carry a version range. `tm:minVersion` is a member of `tm:extends` or `tm:submodel` links and a sibling of `tm:ref`. `td:minVersion` is a member of `td:extends` or `td:subthing` links and a sibling of `td:ref`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: A floor MUST be a SemVer 2.0.0 string without build metadata and within Core's 128-character [id limit][Core id constraints]. It MUST NOT have the generated `0.0.0-N` form. Invalid syntax or a generated floor MUST produce `invalid-version`. `td:minVersion` on a TM reference and `tm:minVersion` on a TD-to-TD reference MUST produce `invalid-floor`.

review.note: The public selection helper validates parsed floor syntax, the Core length boundary and the target-kind discriminator. Section 1.3 defines generated N as positive, so 0.0.0-0 remains an authored prerelease rather than a generated floor. Reference extraction and provider acquisition are separate obligations. Re-reviewed against PR #571 at 514f6eac: this floor clause and its context are unchanged; the successor clarifies the separate incomplete closure profile in section 5.4.4.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: For a TD with exactly one `rel: "type"` link, its `version.model`, when present, is the implicit floor of that link. If the link also has an explicit `tm:minVersion`, the greater value by SemVer precedence is the effective floor. An explicit lower value MUST NOT weaken the implicit floor. If only one floor is present, that floor applies.

review.note: For an already identified TM type link, selection derives the greater parsed implicit/explicit floor and preserves either floor when supplied alone. Sticky-default failures distinguish floor enforcement from merely choosing the highest Version. URI/context parsing and link extraction remain separate. Re-reviewed against PR #571 at 514f6eac: this floor clause and its context are unchanged; the successor clarifies the separate incomplete closure profile in section 5.4.4.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: For a TD with several type links and `version.model`, every type link MUST carry its own `tm:minVersion`. Otherwise, resolution MUST fail as `ambiguous-floor`, including when resolving a different, fully specified link. When every link has a floor, each link MUST use the greater of its own floor and `version.model`.

review.note: The selection request carries the parsed total link count and whether every link has a floor. The helper reports ambiguity even for a specified link, before malformed individual floors, and raises complete links to version.model. Deriving these inputs from customer documents is not claimed. Re-reviewed against PR #571 at 514f6eac: this floor clause and its context are unchanged; the successor clarifies the separate incomplete closure profile in section 5.4.4.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: For several type links without `version.model`, each link uses its own floor if present. An omitted floor MUST NOT produce `ambiguous-floor`.

review.note: With no parsed TD model version, missing floors on other type links do not cause ambiguity. A supplied floor still constrains selection and fails when unmet. Document parsing and provider integration remain separate. Re-reviewed against PR #571 at 514f6eac: this floor clause and its context are unchanged; the successor clarifies the separate incomplete closure profile in section 5.4.4.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: A non-SemVer implicit floor MUST produce `invalid-version`.

review.note: An unpinned type-link request validates its parsed implicit floor and reports invalid-version for malformed syntax. Pins bypass floor derivation as required by the resolver algorithm. This mapping does not include extracting version.model from a document. Re-reviewed against PR #571 at 514f6eac: this floor clause and its context are unchanged; the successor clarifies the separate incomplete closure profile in section 5.4.4.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: A `tm:ref` or `td:ref` is document-local when its URI-reference, resolved against the containing document's base URI and with its fragment removed, identifies that same document. A document-local reference targets the containing revision being processed, not a Resource lookup. When it carries a floor, the resolver MUST compare the floor with that revision's `version.model` for `tm:ref` or `version.instance` for `td:ref`. A `td:ref` floor also applies the TD major cap. A missing authored version, or one below the floor or outside the cap, MUST produce `unsatisfied`. An invalid authored version MUST produce `invalid-version`. The resolver MUST NOT select another Version of the containing Resource to satisfy a local reference.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: A resolver MUST return `(wotid, versionid, contentdigest, origin)`, where `origin` identifies the registry from which the stored bytes were obtained and `contentdigest` is the digest of those bytes. A Consumer MAY retain this tuple outside the document and pass either a digest pin or a `versionid` pin on a subsequent resolution. A request MUST contain at most one kind of pin. Documents MUST NOT carry registry version pins or digest pins. A floor is a compatibility requirement, not a pin. Authored references and document bytes MUST remain portable between registries.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.2. Resolver Algorithm

requirements.text: The resolver MUST apply these steps in order:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.2. Resolver Algorithm

requirements.text: 1. Find the Resource whose `wotid` equals the reference target. If none exists, fail as `not-found`. A deprecated Resource is eligible and MUST NOT be replaced automatically by its `deprecated.alternative`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.4. Publication closure

requirements.text: A WoT publication that claims domain-complete closure MUST include the `http://opcfoundation.org/UA/WoT-Binding/publication-closure/1` extension as a REQUIRED manifest extension. Its document format is `wot-publication-closure/1`, as defined by the [closure schema](schemas/publication-closure.schema.json). The extension does not change the authored WoT documents or their reference semantics.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.4. Publication closure

requirements.text: Each `entries` item, binding `source` and binding `target` MUST be an exact Version XID in the captured Registry view. A target MUST identify one associated Version document, not a Resource XID, default-Version alias, WoT identifier or URL. The captured Registry model determines the target Resource's kind. A Consumer MUST validate that kind and target identity against the source occurrence using the mapping defined for that reference kind. The closure document does not add a target-kind field or authorize a different selection rule. If no such mapping is defined, the Consumer MUST reject the binding.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.4. Publication closure

requirements.text: A producer MUST derive the closure from the captured source document bytes, not from the binding list. Each external reference occurrence in the closure MUST have exactly one binding to its exact target Version. The binding's `source`, `pointer`, `operator` and `href` MUST identify that occurrence and preserve its authored reference. A Consumer MUST verify those values against the captured source bytes and MUST NOT resolve a missing binding against a live Registry, select a default Version, or replace the target with a newer Version.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.4. Publication closure

requirements.text: The extension alone therefore does not establish WoT-complete closure. A producer MUST NOT claim that completeness unless it can identify and validate every in-scope reference under a defined mapping. A Consumer MUST reject a closure whose scope or target mapping it cannot validate. The existing schema and sample check the descriptor's shape, not these missing semantic mappings.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Relationships and Cross-References / 6.2. Thing Description to Thing Description

requirements.text: A TD-to-TD reference selects a Version of the target `thingdescription` Resource using its `wotid` and SemVer `versionid`, derived from the target `version.instance` as specified in [Section 1.3](#13-versioning). For `td:extends`, `td:subthing` and `td:ref`, `td:minVersion` is an OPTIONAL floor. A floor limits the target Version to `[floor, (major + 1).0.0)`. Without a floor, resolution selects the highest eligible Version overall and can cross major versions. The referencing TD's `version.instance` and `version.model` do not supply an implicit floor.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Relationships and Cross-References / 6.5. Affordance Grouping

requirements.text: - A registry MUST accept and serve a valid TD whose affordances are all declared in one document, with no grouping construct of any kind.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Relationships and Cross-References / 6.5. Affordance Grouping

requirements.text: - A registry MUST NOT require an affordance to belong to a group in order to be stored, retrieved, or referenced.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Relationships and Cross-References / 6.5. Affordance Grouping

requirements.text: Proposals to sub-divide a large TD's affordances, such as a `td:submodel` grouping member, are being discussed in the W3C WoT community. Were such a mechanism to be standardized, a WoT Registry would store a TD that uses it exactly as it stores any other TD, since the grouping is a member of the document rather than of the registry model. Support is OPTIONAL. A registry that does not understand the mechanism MUST still store and serve the document unchanged, per [Section 5.2](#52-preserving-customer-documents).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Relationships and Cross-References / 6.5. Affordance Grouping

requirements.text: Documents authored outside the Registry routinely contain no grouping construct. They MUST remain fully supported.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 7. Security

requirements.text: Implementations are expected to use authentication and authorization appropriate to the application domain and deployment environment. Those mechanisms MAY include OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, API keys or other options appropriate to the use case.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 7. Security

requirements.text: Operators of a WoT Registry SHOULD be aware that Thing Descriptions can expose detailed information about deployed devices, including network locations, operational endpoints, and security schemes. The [WoT Security and Privacy Considerations][WoT-Security] document gives additional guidance.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 7. Security

requirements.text: A Consumer or Registry that resolves them SHOULD confine resolution to the Registry and its declared federation links. Where a deployment has to dereference an authored URL it SHOULD:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 7. Security

requirements.text: The same `wotid` MAY appear in more than one Group ([Section 5.3](#53-lookup)). A writer with access to any Group within a Registry-wide query's scope can therefore publish a document carrying another party's `wotid` and claims of high `maturity`/`standardsbody` status. A Consumer selecting on those attributes alone would compose the attacker's Thing Model and bind its affordances to that model's endpoints.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 7. Security

requirements.text: Selection MUST therefore be scoped to writers the Consumer already trusts.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Scope and Terminology

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" are interpreted as described in [RFC2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Scope and Terminology

requirements.text: Channel names and snapshot IDs are not document Version IDs. Groups remain organizational containers. A Group that holds channel or snapshot Resources MUST NOT be used or interpreted as a channel, a snapshot or a compatibility declaration.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Model and Placement / Storage Boundary

requirements.text: Loading the model does not enforce publication immutability, conditional head updates, retention, digest identity or authorization. A publication adapter, such as a server module or storage layer in front of a Core store, MUST enforce those behaviors. A Core-only store MUST NOT advertise publication support merely because it loaded the model. Public APIs MAY be read-only.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Model and Placement / Resource Types

requirements.text: The [model](model.json) defines `channels`, `snapshots` and `objects`, with singular names `channel`, `snapshot` and `object`. It places them in an example organizational Group type, `publications`, whose singular name is `publication`. The sample channel `stable` belongs to the Group `team`, at `https://publisher.example.test/publications/team/channels/stable`. A deployment MAY import these Resource types into its existing organizational Group types using Core [`ximportresources`](../../core/model.md#reuse-of-resource-definitions). It MUST preserve the shared Resource definitions. Group IDs identify neither channels nor publication scopes.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Model and Placement / Resource Types

requirements.text: An object Resource in the example uses the explicit Version ID `content`; its document media type depends on the captured content. A publisher MAY reuse existing exact Versions instead of copying their bytes, provided the adapter ensures their immutability and retention. Changed captured bytes need another object identity; `registry-capture` is not an overwrite target for every release.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Model and Placement / Resource Types

requirements.text: A manifest MAY reference a manifest in another authorized Registry. Forks do not require copies of its document revisions.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Byte Descriptors

requirements.text: A byte descriptor MUST contain `reference`, `digest` as `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, and non-negative integer byte `size`. Its `reference` MUST contain `registry` and `version`:

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Byte Descriptors

requirements.text: - `registry` contains the selected `binding`, credential-free absolute `endpoint` and OPTIONAL `parameters`. Their meanings and validation follow Federation's [binding definitions](../federation/spec.md#discovery-and-binding-selection). This is one selected access context, not a catalog advertisement list. Priority and implicit HTTP access are not part of this reference.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Byte Descriptors

requirements.text: - `version` is an exact Version XID in that Registry. A consumer MUST NOT substitute a Resource's default Version or interpret a NodeId as the XID.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Byte Descriptors

requirements.text: A consumer MUST reject a descriptor that lacks these fields, such as one that supplies only a URL.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Byte Descriptors

requirements.text: The referenced Version MUST serve the stored document bytes, not a fresh serialization of entity metadata. This applies to Registry JSON and JSON manifests as well as binary documents. Snapshot manifests, captured Registry JSON, captured domain bytes and extension documents MUST be stored as Version documents.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Byte Descriptors

requirements.text: - Git references MUST select a complete commit object ID, not a branch or tag.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Byte Descriptors

requirements.text: - OCI references, including File OCI layouts, MUST select a digest, not a tag.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Byte Descriptors

requirements.text: An unsupported binding, unavailable Version, denied destination or failed integrity check MUST fail the read explicitly. A consumer MUST NOT retry through another binding, a live export or a newer channel head as automatic repair. Authorization and trust are supplied under caller policy, not by the descriptor.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Manifest Format

requirements.text: | `parent` | OPTIONAL descriptor of the preparation predecessor. |

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Manifest Format

requirements.text: | `extensions` | OPTIONAL URI-keyed domain closure and provenance descriptors. |

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Manifest Format

requirements.text: | `requiredExtensions` | OPTIONAL extension URIs needed for interpretation. |

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Manifest Format

requirements.text: Consumers MUST verify the exact size and SHA-256 of every descriptor they use. Manifest identity covers exact UTF-8 bytes, not parsed JSON equality. Whitespace changes can produce another ID. Producers SHOULD use deterministic serialization. This format does not canonicalize arbitrary domain documents.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Manifest Format

requirements.text: A manifest MUST NOT include its own digest. Consumers MUST reject unknown formats or unknown mandatory extension semantics instead of ignoring them.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Manifest Format

requirements.text: Every `requiredExtensions` entry MUST identify an included extension. Unlisted extensions are OPTIONAL to generic readers. A caller requesting a domain profile still requires that profile's extension and validation.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Registry JSON and Document Associations

requirements.text: The Registry descriptor covers the model, available model source and captured metadata. Registry JSON MUST use Core [document view](../../core/spec.md#doc-flag). It MUST contain a complete internal graph and sufficient model material, including immutable model includes, as specified by Federation. Its enabled capabilities MUST describe the captured view rather than the source server's write capabilities.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Registry JSON and Document Associations

requirements.text: When a view is served from another location, the origin fields preserve the document's source identity and `base` preserves the base for its relative references. View Version XIDs MUST be unique, including under Core's case-insensitive uniqueness rules. The association MUST NOT change the document's authored identifiers.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Registry JSON and Document Associations

requirements.text: An offline-complete manifest MUST supply every declared document in its scope, except aliases whose Core document operation resolves to another included Resource. Linked snapshots MAY reference exact Versions in another Registry, but MUST NOT claim bytes omitted from their offline package are offline available. An authored external link remains domain content. If its bytes are captured by this publication, the publisher stores them as a Version document too. Metadata-only types do not acquire documents by appearing in a manifest. Domain bytes MUST be captured through raw reads or byte-preserving Core [binary representation](../../core/spec.md#binary-flag), not JSON parsing and reserialization.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Registry JSON and Document Associations

requirements.text: A change to the model, captured metadata, document selection or extensions changes the manifest's checked graph and therefore its ID. A parent records preparation history only; it establishes neither compatibility nor numeric order and defines no merge algorithm. Reading a snapshot MUST NOT require reading its parent.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Capture Classification

requirements.text: - `source-snapshot` is permitted only when the source provides an immutable capture guarantee. For this claim, the producer MUST retain its source identity and capture evidence in a provenance extension under `requiredExtensions`.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Manifest and Integrity / Capture Classification

requirements.text: The classification does not weaken the output's immutability or internal completeness. A consumer requiring atomic source capture MUST reject `live-observation`.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Publishing and Opening a Channel / Publishing a Snapshot

requirements.text: The manifest and necessary content are written before the head update; they become part of the channel's published state only when selected by `head`. An authorized publisher MUST perform these steps:

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Publishing and Opening a Channel / Head Update Rules

requirements.text: - `scope` MUST equal the new manifest's scope.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Publishing and Opening a Channel / Head Update Rules

requirements.text: - `head` MUST have no separate default-Version alias maintained as a second authority. Core defaults on the channel's metadata-only Version are not publication selection.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Publishing and Opening a Channel / Head Update Rules

requirements.text: - The adapter MUST validate the new head before making it visible.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Publishing and Opening a Channel / Head Update Rules

requirements.text: - A stale epoch MUST preserve the old head and return Core's [`mismatched_epoch`](../../core/spec.md#mismatched_epoch).

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Publishing and Opening a Channel / Head Update Rules

requirements.text: - Unconditional channel-head updates MUST be rejected by the adapter.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Publishing and Opening a Channel / Head Update Rules

requirements.text: - An implementation lacking atomic compare-and-update MUST NOT offer writes.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Publishing and Opening a Channel / Head Update Rules

requirements.text: Every successful head update MUST advance the Meta epoch, including a rollback to a previously selected manifest. Rolling `stable` back from S13 to S12 moves the epoch from 17 to 21, not back to 12. The same channel Resource identity MUST NOT be reused after deletion. An authority MUST retain that non-reuse history or use a distinct Resource identity. This avoids an old epoch accidentally authorizing a write to a recreated channel.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Publishing and Opening a Channel / Opening a Channel

requirements.text: An authorized reader opens a channel by reading its Meta once, verifying the manifest at `head`, and establishing the immutable context described in [Open Context and Discovery](#open-context-and-discovery). Every subsequent read and page request uses that selected snapshot. It MUST NOT reread the channel to fill missing members. Refresh is a new open operation.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Open Context and Discovery / Open Record

requirements.text: The schema defines the `open` record with `format`, `scope`, `snapshot`, `registry`, `completeness`, OPTIONAL `channel` selection, and OPTIONAL constituent `sources`. Here `format` is `xregistry-open/1`. The channel selection records its selected Registry access, Resource XID and observed Meta epoch. Unlike a byte descriptor, its `reference` has `resource` instead of `version`, because a channel selection belongs to Resource Meta. The sample [open record](samples/open.json) for a reader that opened `stable` at epoch 12 is:

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Open Context and Discovery / Open Record

requirements.text: `snapshot` and `registry` MUST equal the selected manifest descriptor and its Registry descriptor. `scope` and `completeness` MUST match the checked manifest. In the sample, `snapshot` equals the channel's `head`, and `registry` equals the manifest's `registry` field.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Open Context and Discovery / Open Record

requirements.text: An open record is transport and access context. It is neither a new Core entity nor a replacement for `self`. The record supplies the information needed to retrieve the manifest and captured Registry JSON Version document. It MUST be available to the caller rather than kept only in logs. Library and native bindings MUST return the equivalent schema-defined record or report unsupported publication-context access.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Open Context and Discovery / OPC UA Access

requirements.text: For OPC UA, the caller reads `scope`, the complete `head` and `MetaEpoch` on the selected channel Resource through the binding's Meta representation. The adapter MUST return a coherent selection: a mixed head or a head paired with another update's epoch is not an open result. The reader then resolves the retained references through the selected bindings. The open record is returned as caller-visible context; no HTTP Link, standard UA context node or new companion Method is implied.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Open Context and Discovery / OPC UA Access

requirements.text: An adapter offering UA publication writes MUST atomically replace the complete head under the expected Meta epoch and enforce this extension's validation and retention rules. A native Meta extension update can be used only when it provides those guarantees. Separate UA Property writes or a batch of Write requests do not establish atomicity. Otherwise publication writes MUST be reported as unsupported; native read support does not imply write support.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Open Context and Discovery / HTTP Projection

requirements.text: A publication HTTP projection MUST serve a snapshot-specific Registry root through Core HTTP. The root response MUST contain an HTTP `Link` with an absolute `rel` URI of `https://xregistry.io/workingdrafts/publication/context`, targeting the associated open-record JSON. The root's metadata response and its open record MUST describe the same snapshot. The link target is subject to the same credential and redirect policy as any other destination.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Open Context and Discovery / HTTP Projection

requirements.text: A moving channel endpoint MAY redirect to that snapshot-specific root. If it serves a response directly, navigation, pagination and the context link MUST remain bound to the selected snapshot. A service unable to supply this guarantee MUST report live behavior, not publication conformance. The extension does not change ordinary non-publication HTTP endpoints.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Open Context and Discovery / HTTP Projection

requirements.text: A pin-aware consumer MUST obtain and validate the open record and manifest before claiming a pinned result. In an HTTP projection, snapshot-specific API `self` and navigation URLs MUST be retrievable Core URLs. Native projections use their binding's addressing and selected context. Source identities remain in the manifest associations. Contexts are not inferred from equal XIDs or root epochs.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Export, Federation and Binding Equivalence / Export

requirements.text: Export remains a binding operation over the selected view. For HTTP, Core [`GET /export`](../../core/http.md#get-export) remains the [document-view](../../core/spec.md#doc-flag) and inlining operation. On a publication root it MUST serialize only the already selected snapshot. Native bindings use their own export operations; this extension does not require them to issue HTTP requests.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Export, Federation and Binding Equivalence / Export

requirements.text: A publisher MAY also expose the exact captured Registry JSON Version document. API serialization and exported JSON can have different bytes from the stored Registry descriptor while representing the same captured graph. Only the descriptor representation is checked with that descriptor's digest.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Export, Federation and Binding Equivalence / Offline Packages

requirements.text: A byte-preserving offline export MUST include the manifest and all objects needed by its completeness claim. Captured bytes MUST NOT be rewritten when a package moves to another location. Publication readers MUST NOT fetch external objects during offline replay.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Export, Federation and Binding Equivalence / Offline Packages

requirements.text: Paths use `/` between nonempty segments of ASCII letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, and end in a file name with one extension. Absolute paths, `.`/`..`, backslashes and percent encodings are prohibited. Readers MUST enforce resolved containment, including symbolic links, and apply byte and traversal limits before reading.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Export, Federation and Binding Equivalence / Offline Packages

requirements.text: The `objects` array MUST cover the selected manifest, captured Registry JSON, associated documents and extensions needed for its completeness claim. Parent manifests are not needed merely to read the selected snapshot.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Export, Federation and Binding Equivalence / Offline Packages

requirements.text: The byte bundle provides direct offline publication access; it does not define another Federation native Registry layout. A bundle can accompany a directory mapping or OCI layout. Before claiming its Snapshot ID, native readers still need their own format and verified equivalence with the manifest. This extension adds no OCI role or Git directory-mapping field. A byte-bundle reader MUST NOT advertise unsupported native binding conformance.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Export, Federation and Binding Equivalence / Reference Comparison

requirements.text: Reference comparison MUST use the `binding` value, endpoint, validated parameters and decoded Version XID:

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Export, Federation and Binding Equivalence / Reference Comparison

requirements.text: A package MUST reject duplicate equivalent references, even if they name different local files.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Export, Federation and Binding Equivalence / Binding Equivalence

requirements.text: A publication consumer MUST verify that any alternate Registry API or package represents the model, metadata and byte associations fixed by the manifest. An unchecked assertion that two endpoints share a Registry ID is insufficient. Binding-specific Git commits, OCI digests and Snapshot IDs remain distinct. A binding without a checked mapping to the manifest MUST NOT claim that ID.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Export, Federation and Binding Equivalence / Binding Equivalence

requirements.text: Binding access fields inside a manifest contribute to its exact-byte identity. Changing HTTP references to UA references creates another manifest and Snapshot ID, even if the captured graph and document bytes agree. To expose one unchanged manifest through another binding, a caller needs an explicit access mapping with checked equivalence to the original exact Version references. This extension does not define an alternate-endpoint discovery protocol. Readers MUST NOT infer such a mapping from equal Registry IDs or silently substitute bindings.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Export, Federation and Binding Equivalence / Federated Sources

requirements.text: Federation MAY discover publication roots through existing HTTP advertisements, or serve checked packages through its other bindings. No new advertisement parameter is added. Existing bindings retain their own format and version rules. A publication reader can use the manifest and Registry descriptors directly without pretending to implement a native package binding.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Export, Federation and Binding Equivalence / Federated Sources

requirements.text: When several sources form a view, each selected immutable source context, the interpreted view model and the exact composition policy MUST be captured to claim reproducible composition. The `sources` array records each source's snapshot and selected Registry access context. Policy and model records use checked extension descriptors. Their semantics MUST be supported by the producer or consumer that reconstructs the composition. A materialized producer-resolved snapshot can instead be consumed directly under its own complete Registry descriptor.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Export, Federation and Binding Equivalence / Federated Sources

requirements.text: Independently pinned sources do not establish one simultaneous capture. Federation precedence selects whole Resources, not compatible Versions or substitute channel heads. Source failures MUST retain Federation's no-silent-fallback behavior. Publication writes remain outside Federation.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Domain Closure and Compatibility

requirements.text: Generic completeness covers declared xRegistry content. It does not cover arbitrary links embedded in that content. A domain profile MAY define closure extensions that bind source Version and reference locations to exact target revisions. It MUST identify the recognized reference kinds, source bases, target identities, mandatory validation and handling of cycles and external dependencies.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Domain Closure and Compatibility

requirements.text: For a profile that defines a closure extension, the producer MUST identify the entry documents from which the closure is evaluated. It MUST determine references from those documents and their transitive dependencies; the list of bindings alone is not evidence that the closure is complete. Each external reference occurrence in that closure MUST have exactly one binding to an exact target Version. A binding MUST identify its source Version and reference location using the profile's defined rules.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Domain Closure and Compatibility

requirements.text: Each entry, source Version and target Version MUST be represented by a document association in the captured Registry view. Bindings MUST be unique under the profile's binding key, MUST match the source bytes and MUST cover the complete reachable closure from the entries. A consumer MUST reject missing, duplicate, inconsistent or unreachable bindings and MUST NOT replace a bound target with a live or newer Version. The profile MUST define how a consumer determines that a target satisfies the reference and the caller's acceptance requirements.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Domain Closure and Compatibility

requirements.text: Each binding's target MUST identify one exact Version XID in the captured Registry view. The captured Registry model determines that Version's Resource kind; a consumer MUST NOT infer the kind from the XID text or the binding's operator alone. The domain profile MUST define how the source occurrence's identity and expected kind match the target. If a consumer cannot establish that match from the captured content and the profile's rules, it MUST reject the binding rather than resolve the reference against a live Registry.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Domain Closure and Compatibility

requirements.text: Consumers requesting such a profile MUST reject absent or unsupported closure data. Exact selection and compatibility validation are separate operations. A snapshot fixes what to evaluate. It does not waive an authored floor, compatibility selector or caller acceptance policy.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Domain Closure and Compatibility

requirements.text: One document revision MAY appear in several snapshots and channels. A channel name such as `stable` or `preview` does not establish a compatibility class. When a selected channel head is incompatible with a constrained request, that request MUST fail. Readers MUST NOT search older snapshots for a compatible result. Raw exact retrieval remains distinct from validated consumption.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Workflows and Lifecycle

requirements.text: - **Retention and deletion.** Retain objects reachable from current heads and retained snapshots. Emergency revocation or deletion can make pins unavailable and MUST be reported explicitly.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Workflows and Lifecycle

requirements.text: Snapshot metadata and manifest bytes MUST NOT be overwritten under their existing identity. Domain revisions used by a retained snapshot MUST be captured immutably or served from retained checked bytes. A Core Version ID alone does not ensure immutable content.

source.section: xRegistry Publications: Channels and Snapshots / Workflows and Lifecycle

requirements.text: Access authorization and retention are deployment policy. Integrity does not grant access or authenticate a publisher. Readers MUST apply Federation's destination, credential, traversal and byte-limit policies. Model or schema validation alone cannot authorize publication.

source.section: WoT Publication and Versioning Design / WoT Channels, Snapshots and Dependency Bindings / What is versioned?

requirements.text: A channel resembles a Git branch only in that it has a mutable head and a publisher can fork it cheaply. The manifest's OPTIONAL parent records preparation history. It does not enable automatic merge, rebase, a working tree or the Git protocol. Reconciliation creates another complete, validated snapshot.

source.section: WoT Publication and Versioning Design / WoT Versioning: Design and Operating Workflows / Design mechanisms / D6. Reference requirements

requirements.text: For mixed-profile type links, profile discovery precedes the legacy implicit/ambiguity rules, which apply to the SemVer-target subset. Incremental links retain their own explicit line and OPTIONAL explicit numeric floor. An unknown or unavailable profile causes failure rather than weakening the requirement.

source.section: WoT Publication and Versioning Design / WoT Versioning: Design and Operating Workflows / Design mechanisms / D9. Implementation responsibilities

requirements.text: - `WoTDependencyDataType` keeps `RequiredVersion` string-valued and profile-interpreted, and adds OPTIONAL `RequiredCompatibilityLine`. Projection-source floors and lines use the same fields. The source entry's `uav:sourceDigest` remains in the projection-plan bytes; compare it with the `ContentDigest` in the target record with the same `EdgeIndex`. The digest, floor and line MUST all hold for that exact Version.

source.section: WoT Publication and Versioning Design / WoT Versioning: Design and Operating Workflows / Design mechanisms / D9. Implementation responsibilities

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL `WoTRefreshOptionsDataType.PublicationContext` has type `WoTPublicationContextDataType`, with `Uri` and an OPTIONAL `ManifestDigest`. Without a digest, `Uri` names a channel opened once per Refresh; the selected digest is reported in `WoTRefreshSummaryDataType.ManifestDigest`. With a digest, it identifies an exact snapshot. Every recognized dependency uses its captured binding without provider, alias or older-snapshot fallback. Missing or unsupported closure, binding or content, and a manifest-digest mismatch produce `closure-incomplete`. Without a publication context, Refresh performs live selection.

source.section: WoT Publication and Versioning Design / WoT Versioning: Design and Operating Workflows / Publisher workflows / P01. Author an editable TM or TD

requirements.text: The author chooses a stable `id` and root `uav:compatibilityLine` A, with the context in D5. The authored version is OPTIONAL for incremental use. The publisher submits the bytes to the configured incremental endpoint. The response identifies the stored revision and digest.

source.section: WoT Publication and Versioning Design / WoT Versioning: Design and Operating Workflows / Consumer workflows / C05. Compose TM targets

requirements.text: Place the line and OPTIONAL floor on a `tm:extends` or `tm:submodel` link, or beside an ordinary `tm:ref`. D5 and D6 normalize the requirement without changing the operator. D7 selects the containing document before traversing an external fragment.

source.section: WoT Publication and Versioning Design / WoT Versioning: Design and Operating Workflows / Consumer workflows / C09. Resolve SemVer type-link floors

requirements.text: D6 retains `ambiguous-floor` when one is missing. Without root `version.model`, each SemVer link has only its own OPTIONAL floor. An explicit pin retains the existing precedence over floor derivation.

source.section: WoT Publication and Versioning Design / WoT Versioning: Design and Operating Workflows / Consumer workflows / C10. Resolve mixed-profile type links

requirements.text: A TD has one SemVer type link and one incremental type link. Discover both profiles first. D6 applies root `version.model` only to the SemVer subset. The incremental link independently requires A and an OPTIONAL integer floor.
